347.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 1, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji): So Dar. What is that gate of yours like, and what is that home like, where (you) sit and take care of all? The sounds of your countless instruments of many kinds play there, and so many are the musicians who play for you. So many of your ragas, with their raginis, are sung there, and so many are your singers. Wind, water and fire sing of you; Dharam Raj (the judge of souls) sings of you at your door. Chitr and Gupt, who know how to write, sing of you; what they write, Dharam Raj weighs and judges. Shiva, Brahma and the goddesses sing of you, ever beautiful, adorned by you. The Indras, seated on their thrones, sing of you with the gods at your door. The Siddhas sing of you in samadhi (deep meditative absorption); the sadhus sing of you in contemplation. The celibates, the charitable and the contented sing of you; the mighty heroes sing of you. The learned pandits and the great rishis sing of you, age after age, along with the Vedas. The enchanting women who charm the mind sing of you, in heaven, in the mortal world and in the netherworld. All the jewels you have created sing of you, along with the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage. Warriors of great might and heroes sing of you; the four sources of life sing of you. The regions, the worlds and the universes, made and set in place by you, sing of you. They alone sing of you who please you, your devotees, steeped (in your love) and full of delight. So many others sing of you who do not come to my mind; what can Nanak consider? He, he alone, is ever true; the Master is true, and true is his glory. He is, and he will be; he does not depart, nor will he depart, he who made the creation. He who brought forth Maya of many colours, many kinds and many species watches over what he has made, having made it, as befits his greatness. Whatever pleases him, that he will do; no command can then be given (to him). He is the King, the Emperor over kings; O Nanak, (our part is) to live in his will. ॥1॥
Dharam Raj judges each soul by its deeds; Chitr and Gupt are, by tradition, the two recorders at his court who write down the deeds of every being.

Mach is the mortal world, between heaven and the netherworld. The jewels: by tradition, the fourteen jewels that came out of the ocean when it was churned. The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are the tiraths held most holy in India.
The four sources of life (khaani): birth from the egg, from the womb, from sweat and from the earth.
348.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). That Purakh, the Being who pervades all, is Niranjan, free of the stain of Maya (the world's illusion and lure); the Lord, the all-pervading Being, is free of that stain; the Lord is beyond reach, wholly beyond reach, without limit. O Lord, the eternal Creator, all meditate on you, all meditate on you. All beings are yours, Lord; you are the Giver to every being. Meditate on the Lord, revered Sants (saints): he makes all sorrows pass away. The Lord himself is the Master, and the Lord himself the servant; O Nanak, what is a poor creature (by itself)? You are within every heart, and in all without any gap; O Lord, you, the one Being, pervade all. Some are givers and some are beggars; all these are your wondrous plays. You are the giver yourself, and yourself the one who enjoys (the gifts); apart from you I know no other. You are the Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), endless, endless; which of your virtues shall I name and describe? Those who serve you, those who serve you, Lord: your servant Nanak is a sacrifice to them. O Lord, those who meditate on you, who meditate on you, live at peace in the world. Liberated, liberated are those who have meditated on the Lord; the noose of Jam has snapped for them. Those who have meditated on the Fearless, on the Fearless Lord: he takes away all their fear. Those who have served, who have served my Lord, merge into the very form of the Lord, Har Har. Blessed, blessed are those who have meditated on the Lord; your servant Nanak gives himself in sacrifice to them. The storehouses of devotion to you, of devotion to you, Lord, are full beyond end, beyond all end. Your devotees, your devotees praise you, O Lord, many, countless, without end. Many, so many, worship you, O Lord; numberless (beings) practise austerities and repeat (your Name). Many, so many of yours read the many Simritis and Shastras, and carry out the rites and the six duties. O servant Nanak, those devotees, those devotees alone are good who please my Lord God. You are the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the Creator, Lord; no other is as great as you. In every age you are the One; always, always you are the One; you are the unmoving Creator, ever the same. O Lord, whatever pleases you yourself, that alone comes about; whatever you yourself do, that takes place. You yourself brought forth the whole creation, and you yourself, having made it, have destroyed it all. Servant Nanak sings the virtues of the Creator, who knows each and every one. ॥5॥
Niranjan: nir (without) and anjan (collyrium, black stain); the One on whom the stain of Maya does not fall.
Ji, in nearly every line of this shabad, is a word of reverence for God.
ਜਨੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ (with the aunkar) is the subject: servant Nanak himself is the sacrifice; ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ (without it) is an address, O servant Nanak, or, with a postposition understood, of servant Nanak.

The Simritis are the Hindu books of conduct and law, the Shastras the books of the six schools of philosophy; the six duties (khat karam) are a Brahmin's: to study and to teach, to perform sacrifice and to have it performed, to give alms and to receive them.
348.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Everyone calls you great, (O God,) having heard (it from others), but how great you are is (told) only on seeing you. Your worth cannot be fixed, nor can you be put into words. Those who speak of you stay merged in you. O my great Master, deep and profound, fathomless in virtues, no one knows how much, how vast, your expanse is. All who practise surat (attention fixed on God) joined together and practised it; all who weigh worth joined together and weighed (yours); yet by the men of knowledge, the men of meditation, the teachers and the teachers of teachers, not even a sesame seed's worth of your greatness could be told. All truthfulness, all austerities, all good deeds, and the great powers of the Siddhas, the accomplished ones: without you, no one has attained this siddhi (accomplishment). It comes by (your) grace, and then no one can hold it back. What can the poor speaker (say)? Your storehouses are filled with praises. The one to whom you give (your praise), what can anyone do against him? O Nanak, the True One (himself) is the one who adorns (him). ॥4॥
The Siddhas are yogis held to have reached perfection; siddhi is attainment, the miraculous powers among it.
349.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). When I utter (his Name), I live; when it is forgotten, I die. The True Name is hard to utter. If hunger for the True Name arises, then, eating (of the Name) in that hunger, the sorrows are driven away. Why should he be forgotten, O my mother? The Master is true, and (is found) through the True Name. Of the True Name's greatness, even a sesame seed's worth, they have grown weary telling, yet none has found its worth. If all were to join together and set about describing him, he does not become greater, nor does he become less. He does not die, nor is there mourning (for him). He keeps on giving, and what he gives to be enjoyed never runs out. This is his quality: there is no other (like him); none has been, and none will be. As great as you yourself are, so great is your gift, (you,) who made the day and made the night. Those who forget the Master are low-born; O Nanak, those without the Name are the outcastes. ॥4॥
Kamjaat (low-born) and sanaat (counted outside the four castes) are not caste by birth here: the Guru says the low are those who forget the Master.
349.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If a beggar at the door cries out, the Master within the mansion hears (his cry); whether he gives him comfort or pushes him away, it is honour he gives him all the same. Recognise the light (of God in all), and do not ask anyone's caste; hereafter there is no caste. (God) himself makes (beings) act, and himself acts, and himself takes to heart (their) grievances. (O God,) when you, the Creator, are the doer of all, what dependence on anyone is there, and what is the world? (God) himself creates (beings), and himself gives (to them); he himself holds them back from evil-mindedness. By the Guru's grace, (in whose) mind (God) comes to dwell, from within (that one) pain and darkness depart. (God) himself makes the Truth dear (to a being); to others (he) does not give the Truth. Says Nanak: if (he) gives (it) to anyone, he calls (that one) to no account hereafter. ॥4॥
349.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The workings of the mind are the cymbals and the ankle-bells; the (love of the) world is the drum: these are the instruments that play. The mind, a Narad, dances: this is the sway of Kalyug; where can the celibate and the virtuous set their feet? O Nanak, be a sacrifice to the Name. The world is blind; the Master (alone) knows all. The disciple, on the contrary, eats from the guru; for love of bread he comes to live in (the guru's) house. Even if (one were given) a hundred years of living and eating, only that day is approved on which (one) recognises the Master. No compassion stirs at the sight of (one in need); no one does without give and take. The king does justice (only) if (something) comes into (his) hand; if one appeals in God's name, no one heeds. Says Nanak: in form and in name one is human, but in deeds a dog that obeys orders at (its master's) door (for scraps). If by the Guru's grace (one) knows (oneself) a guest (here), then (one) gains some honour in the Lord's court. ॥4॥
Narad, the sage of the Puranas, roams the worlds singing and dancing with his vina; here he stands for the restless mind.
Taam (Arabic ta'am): food, bread.
350.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O God,) all the speaking and hearing there is, is your own current of life; all the form there is, is your body. You yourself are the one who tastes, you yourself the life that dwells (in all); O mother, I can speak of no other, no second. My Master is One; he is One, brother, he alone is One. (He) himself kills and himself sets free; himself he takes and gives. (He) himself watches over (all), himself delights, himself casts his glance of grace. Whatever is to be done, (he) himself is doing; nothing else can be done. As (he) acts, so is (he) named; (O God,) all this is your greatness. Kalyug is the woman who sells wine, Maya the sweet wine, and the drunken mind keeps on drinking. (God) himself makes forms of many kinds; this is what poor Nanak says. ॥4॥
350.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Let wisdom be the instrument, and love the drum (the pakhavaj); (then) bliss arises, and the mind is ever full of zest. This is devotion, this the practice of austerity; Dance in this joy, setting your feet down with care. One who knows (how to sing God's) praise keeps the full beat; any other dancing is only the pleasures and the whims of the mind. Let truth and contentment be the two cymbals that play; let being ever in bloom be the bells upon the feet; let having no love for another be the raag and its music; Dance in this joy, setting your feet down with care. Let the fear (of God), held in heart and mind, be the whirling turn, whether sitting or rising, always and ever; let knowing the body to be ashes be the rolling on the ground; Dance in this joy, setting your feet down with care. Let there be love for the teaching in the gathering of the Sikhs, hearing the True Name through the Guru, and, O Nanak, uttering it again and again; Dance in this joy, setting your feet down with care. ॥4॥
350.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O Lord, you) brought forth the air and set the whole earth in place, and bound water and fire together. Blind (in his folly), the ten-headed (Ravan) had his own head cut off; did killing Ravan make (you) any greater? What praise of you can be spoken? You fill all, pervading every one. Creating the beings, you hold the way (of their lives) in your hand; did putting a nose-rope on Kali (the serpent) make (you) any greater? Whose husband are you, and whom is one to call your wife? You pervade all, with no gap between. Brahma, the giver of boons, went with his family into the (lotus) stalk to search out (the source of) creation; going on, he found no end to it. Did slaying Kans make (you) any greater? (You) brought forth the jewels; the ocean of milk was churned, and the others (gods and demons) cried out in anger: We did this. Says Nanak, how can the hidden (Lord) stay hidden? (It was he who) shared out (the jewels) one by one. ॥4॥

Kali: the serpent Kaliya, whom, in the Puranas, Krishna subdued in the Yamuna. In the Puranas Brahma was born of a lotus that grew from Vishnu's navel, and went down its stalk to find where it began, but found no end.
The gods and demons quarrelled over the jewels that came out of the churned ocean; in the Puranas Vishnu took the form of Mohini, an enchantress, and shared them out one by one.
351.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Deeds and conduct grew into a spreading vine, and its fruit was the Name of the Lord (Ram). It has no form or outline; the Shabad that the Pure Lord made sounds (within), unstruck. If anyone comes to know (the Lord) and tells (of him), he alone drinks the Amrit. Those who drank it became rapt with joy; their bonds and nooses broke. Within (them), (their) light merged in the Light; then they gave up (chasing) the gains of Maya. (O Lord, they) saw your form in every light, and your Maya in all the worlds. In this (world), a form of strife, (the Lord) sits apart, unattached, and, present within (all) as his own reflection, keeps watch (over all). (Such a) yogi plays the vina of the Shabad, (rapt) in the sight of the Infinite One's form; through the unstruck Shabad he is dyed in the Husband Lord: this is the reflection Nanak speaks. ॥4॥
351.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O Lord,) my virtues (are only these): loads of talk upon my head. Of all talk, the (worthy) talk is (talk of) the Creator. Eating, drinking, laughing are (all) in vain as long as you do not come to mind in the heart. Then what care is left (for anyone), and what (more) is there to do, if, born into this (human) life, one takes what is worth the taking? The mind's thinking is (that of) a maddened, drunken elephant; (so) whatever we say is all error upon error. With what face can we make a prayer (to you) when sin and virtue both stand by (us) as witnesses? As you make anyone, so does he become; apart from you there is no second. Such understanding as you give, such does one receive; as it pleases you yourself, so you make (the world) go. The jewel-like raags, their consorts (the raginis) and (all) their family: within it (all) springs the sublime Amrit. O Nanak, this is the Creator's own wealth and riches, if anyone grasps this thought. ॥4॥
The family of the raags: in the old tradition of Indian music each raag has its raginis (consorts) and its sons.
351.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). In his grace (the Husband Lord) came to his own home; then (my) companions gathered and set about the wedding. Seeing this play, (my) mind was filled with bliss: the Husband has come to wed (me). Sing, sing, O women, (songs of) discerning reflection; into our home has come the Husband, the Life of the world. Our wedding took place at the Guru's door; when the Husband met (me), then I knew that (his) Shabad pervades the three worlds; (my) self-conceit went, and (my) mind was won over. (The Lord) himself brings his own work to completion; by no one else can it be done. This work, in which are truth, contentment, compassion and dharma, some rare one grasps through the Guru. Says Nanak, he alone is the Husband of all; she on whom he looks with grace becomes the happy wife. ॥4॥
351.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (For one who has subdued the mind) home and forest are alike; (he abides) in Sahaj and in love. (His) evil thinking is gone, and in its place is (the Lord's) praise. (His) ladder of truth is the True Name on (his) lips; serving the True Guru, he finds his own true home. One who crushes the mind: know him (to have mastered) the six darshanas (the six schools of philosophy); (he sees) in all the light of the Lord God, perfect and whole. (One with) great thirst (for Maya) puts on many guises; the pain that Maya's poison brings drives peace from (his) body; lust and anger steal the wealth within. Leaving double-mindedness, (one) crosses over through the Name. (One who has won the mind) sings (the Lord's) praise and (knows) the bliss of Sahaj; the love of Gobind is (his) friend and kin. (He knows that the Lord) himself acts, and himself is the Forgiver; body, mind and life (he keeps) with the Lord, laid before him. Falsehood and vices (bring) great suffering to the body; guises and castes all look (to him) like dust. Whatever is born comes and goes; O Nanak, only the Name and (his) Will are everlasting. ॥4॥
352.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is one lake, and in it lotuses beyond compare; (the lake) keeps them ever in bloom, fragrant and fair. (There) swans peck at bright pearls, (and remain) a part of the Lord of the world, the Master of every power. Whatever is seen springs up and perishes; (but) the lotus in the lake is never seen without water. Only a rare one understands and finds (this) secret; the Veda speaks always of the three branches (of Maya). (One whose) attention merges in the understanding of the Shabad attains the supreme state, serving the True Guru. He is free, steeped (in the Lord), remembering (him) in love; (abiding) in the King of kings, he is ever in bloom. (O Lord,) one whom you save in your mercy, though a sinking stone, you carry across in your boat. (He saw) the Light in the three worlds, and knew (the Lord) in the three worlds; (his attention) turned back (from Maya), and he brought (the Lord's) home into (the) home (of his heart). One who, with loving attention fixed, worships day and night: Nanak falls at the feet of such ones. ॥4॥

The lake is the Saadh Sangat, the lotuses the Sants who live in it, the swans the Gurmukhs; as the lotus in the lake stays in bloom by water, so the mind that abides in the Sangat by the Naam. The three branches: the three qualities of Maya.
352.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). With the Guru's true teaching, wrangling goes far away; too much cleverness only gathers dirt. The dirt that has clung is wiped away through the True Name; by the Guru's grace one keeps loving attention fixed (on the Lord). (The Lord) is present, right before (us); (make your) prayer (to him). Pain and pleasure, know it as true, rest with God the Creator. Whoever deals in falsehood keeps coming and going (in birth and death); there is no end to (his) talking and telling. What has he seen? He gains no insight, no understanding; without the Name no contentment comes to (his) mind. All who are born are gripped by (the) disease (of the soul); they are tormented by the pain of Haumai and Maya. Those alone escape whom God has kept safe; serving the True Guru, they have tasted the savour of Amrit. (One who) holds back the wandering mind and tastes the Amrit, (who), serving the True Guru, utters the Amrit Shabad, through the true Shabad attains liberation and the high state; O Nanak, he casts out the self from within. ॥4॥
352.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One whom he has made (his own) has become (one with) the True; to him the True Guru gave the Amrit Name. The Name is in (his) heart, and (his) mind is never broken off (from the Lord); night and day he is in the Beloved's company. O dear Lord, keep (me) in your refuge. By the Guru's grace (I) have found the Lord's savour; the Name, that precious thing, the nine treasures, has come to (me). (One whose) deeds and dharma are the true Name of the True One: to him I am ever a sacrifice. Those steeped in the Lord are accepted (at his court); their company is the supreme treasure. The bride who has gained the Lord for her Husband is blessed; dyed in the Lord, she reflects on the Shabad; she herself crosses over, and carries (her) companions and family across; serving the True Guru, she reflects on the essence. The True Name is our caste and honour; true love is (our) deeds, dharma and self-restraint. O Nanak, no account is asked of one whom (the Lord) forgives; that One alone wipes out (all sense of) a second. ॥4॥
353.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Some come (into the world) and, having come, go away (empty-handed); some, steeped in the Lord, remain absorbed (in him); some find no place to rest, neither on earth nor in the sky; they are the luckless, who do not meditate on the Lord's Name. From the Perfect Guru are found the high state and the (right) way of living. The world is a sea of dread, full of poison; through the Guru's Shabad the Lord carries (us) across. Those whom God himself joins (to himself), death cannot crush. Through the Guru those beloved ones stay pure, as lotuses stand above the water, untouched by it. Tell me, whom can we call bad or good? God (Brahm) is seen (in all); through the Guru the True One is found. Reflecting on the Guru's teaching, I tell of the Untellable; joining the Guru's company, I reach the farther shore. (Pondering) the many distinctions of the Shastras, the Vedas and the Simritis, (and) bathing at the sixty-eight (tiraths): (all this is) the Lord's savour in the heart. Through the Guru one stays pure; no filth clings (to him). O Nanak, the Name (dwells) in the heart by great good fortune written from the start. ॥4॥
353.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Bowing low again and again, I fall at my Guru's feet; (by his grace) I have beheld within (me) the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram). Reflecting (on his virtues), I have dwelt on the Lord in my heart; seeing (him) in my heart, I have pondered (him). Utter (the Name of) Ram (the Lord); he brings deliverance. By the Guru's grace one gains the Lord, the jewel; ignorance is wiped away, and light dawns. (One who) only talks with the tongue: (his) bonds do not break; caught in Haumai, (his) wandering does not end. When the True Guru is met, Haumai breaks; only then is one accepted in the (Lord's) reckoning. (One who holds to) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and devotion to the Beloved, and enshrines in the heart the Dear One, the Ocean of peace: him the Lord, Lover of devotion, the Life of the world, the Giver, carries across, (granting him) the wisdom of the Guru's teaching. One who fights his mind and dies (to self) finds God, and stills the mind's desire within the mind itself. O Nanak, (one on whom) the Life of the world shows mercy keeps (his) loving attention fixed (on him) in Sahaj. ॥4॥
353.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Those who have come to understand: to whom do they speak, to whom do they recite, whom do they instruct? Whom do they teach? Having read and reflected, they have understood, and through the True Guru's Shabad they live in contentment. Through the Guru's teaching, such a Lord, pervading every body, so deep and profound: worship him, O my mind. (Within them rise) endless waves of devotion to the Lord and of his love; keeping company with the Lord's virtues, they are pure night and day. The worldly Saakat's birth is wasted; the servant devoted to the Lord stays detached (from the world). Pure is the body of one who has sung the Lord's virtues; recognising his own self, he keeps his mind fixed (on the Lord). (The Lord) is the Primal One, infinite, beyond the farthest beyond, a diamond; dyed in that ruby (the Lord), my mind has grown steady. Those who only talk, talking on and on, are dead (within). That God is not far; O God, you are (near). I have seen the whole world to be Maya's shadow; Nanak has meditated on the Naam through the Guru's teaching. ॥4॥
354.1: Raag Asa, a Tituka, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One is a beggar who lives on alms; another is a king, lost (in his kingship). One receives honour, another dishonour; another pulls down and builds up again, his mind fixed (on that). (O Lord,) no one is greater than you; whom could I point out as good? For me, your Name is my only support; you are the Giver, the One who can do all, the Creator. I do not find the way; I go off on crooked paths; (so) in the Lord's court there is no place for (me) to sit. I am blind in mind, bound by Maya; (my) body wastes away and decays every day. (Yet) great is my hope of eating and living on; (while) every breath and every morsel is counted in your reckoning. Day and night (the Lord) gives the blind a lamp (of understanding), and cares for the one drowning in the terrifying world-ocean. Those who speak the Name, hear it and accept it: to them I am a sacrifice. Nanak makes one prayer: soul and body, all is in your keeping. When you give it, I repeat your Name, and (I) find a place to sit in the Lord's court. When it pleases you, the evil mind goes away, and the jewel of divine knowledge comes and settles in the mind. When (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, the True Guru is met; Nanak humbly prays: (then the soul) swims across the world-ocean. ॥4॥
Tituka: a hymn whose every stanza has three lines; here each line is a pair of short lines.
354.2: Raag Asa, Panchpade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). A cow without milk, a bird without wings, plants without water are of no use; what is a sultan whom no one salutes? (O Lord,) dark is the chamber (of the heart) in which your Name is not. (O Lord,) why do you slip from the mind? (Forgetting you) brings great pain. Let (any other) pain befall, but may you not be forgotten. (In old age) the eyes go blind, the tongue loses its taste, and no sound reaches the ears; one walks on one's feet (only) when led by the hand from in front: such are the fruits that grow without (the Lord's) service. Those who plant the Word as the trees of a garden in the clean soil (of the heart), and water them with love: on all of them grows the one fruit, the Naam; but without (the Lord's) grace how can (anyone) obtain it? As many beings as there are, all are yours; without serving (you) no one gains the fruit. Pain and pleasure are as you will; apart from the Name, the soul cannot endure. To die (to self) within (the Guru's) teaching is life; what other life is there? If I live (any other way), that is no way (to live). Says Nanak: (the Lord) gives life to all beings; (O Lord,) keep (me) wherever it pleases you, you alone. ॥5॥
355.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (My) body is the Brahmin, and the mind his dhoti; divine knowledge is the sacred thread, and meditation the ring of kusha grass. The Lord's Name and his praise are the bath I beg for, that by the Guru's grace I may stay merged in God. O Pandit, reflect on God in this way: in the Name is purity, the Name is what I study, and in the Name are right conduct and observance. The outer sacred thread lasts only as long as the light (of life) is with (the body); keep the Name in your heart: (that is) the dhoti and the frontal mark; (the Name alone) stands by you here and hereafter. Apart from the Name, do not go seeking other rites. Love is the worship; burn away Maya completely; see the One alone, and seek no other. One who recognises the Essence in the sky of the Tenth Gate and keeps the Lord on his lips reads the (true) scripture and reflects on it. Love (of the Lord) is (his) food, (and by it) doubt and fear flee; with the radiance of the Watchman (the Lord) within, no thief comes near. To know the one God is the tilak on (his) forehead; one who understands God has discernment within. (God) cannot be won over by rituals; reading scripture, no one finds (his) worth. the eighteen (Puranas) and the four (Vedas) have not found (his) secret; O Nanak, the True Guru has shown (me) God. ॥5॥
Janeu: the sacred thread worn by Brahmins; kuspaati: a ring of kusha grass worn on the finger during worship.
355.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). That person alone is a (true) servant, slave and devotee who becomes Gurmukh and so the Master's slave. He who fashioned the creation destroys it again; apart from him there is no other at all. Reflecting on the True Name through the Guru's Shabad, the Gurmukhs are found true in the court of the True One. True is (their) plea, true their prayer; the Husband Lord in his mansion hears it and gives his approval. He calls (such a one) to his true throne and bestows honour; whatever he does comes to pass. (O Lord, the Gurmukh's) strength is yours alone; you alone are (his) support; the Guru's Shabad is (his) true seal of passage. Whoever accepts the Hukam departs in honour; bearing the true seal, (he) meets no barrier (on the way). The pandits read the Veda and expound it, but they do not know the secret: the real thing (the Name) is within. Without the Guru there is no awareness, no understanding that the True God pervades (all). What can I say? What can I say and describe? You yourself know, O Lord of all wonders. O Nanak, the one door (of the Lord) is (the Gurmukh's) only support; there the Gurmukh lives on the Truth. ॥5॥
355.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The body is an unbaked clay pot, full of misery; it is born, it perishes, and it suffers pain. This world is an ocean hard to cross; how can it be crossed? Without the Lord and the Guru no one reaches the far shore. Without you (I have) no other, my Beloved; without you there is no other, O Lord. In all colours and all forms you alone are; (the Lord) forgives the one on whom he casts his glance of grace. The wicked mother-in-law (Maya) does not let me dwell in the house (of my heart); the wicked one does not let me meet my Husband. I serve the feet of my companions and friends (in the holy company); by the Guru's grace the Lord has cast his glance of grace (on me). Reflecting on myself and subduing my mind, I have found there is no friend like you. As you keep me, so must I live; you give pain and pleasure, and what you do, that alone (comes to pass). Hope and desire are both destroyed; (I) have become free of hope in the three qualities. The fourth state is reached through the Guru; (I) have taken the shelter of the assembly of the Sants. All divine knowledge and meditation, all chanting and austerity, are (gained by) the one in whose heart is the Lord, unseen and unfathomable. O Nanak, the one whose mind is dyed in the Lord's Name gains, through the Guru's teaching, (his) service in Sahaj. ॥5॥
356.1: Raag Asa, Panchpade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Family is attachment; all worldly affairs are attachment; give up attachment: (it) is all corruption. Give up attachment and doubt, O brother, (so that) the True Name may dwell in heart and body. When the True Name, the nine treasures, is found, (then) no son weeps and no mother grieves. In this attachment the world is drowned; only a rare one crosses over, through the Guru. Caught in this attachment, you will fall into births again; clinging to attachment, you will go to the city of Jam. (People) take initiation from a guru and practise chanting and austerities, (yet) their attachment does not break, nor are they accepted (in the Lord's court). When (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, this attachment departs, and, O Nanak, (the soul) stays merged in the Lord. ॥6॥
356.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The True One, unseen and infinite, himself does (all); I am a sinner; you are the Forgiver. Everything happens as you will; acting by the stubbornness of the mind, one is ruined in the end. The manmukh's intellect is caught up in falsehood; without the Lord's Simran, it suffers for its sin. Give up the evil mind and earn some profit; whatever is born comes from the (Lord), unseen and unfathomable. Such is our Friend and Helper: the Guru, the Lord, has met (me) and made devotion firm (within). In all (other) dealings there is loss; the Lord's Name is what pleases Nanak's mind. ॥5॥
356.3: Raag Asa, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Learning is truly reflected upon only when one does good to others; when the five (passions) are subdued, then one truly dwells at a place of pilgrimage. The ankle-bells ring (to purpose) only if the mind is attuned (to the Lord); then what can Jam do to me hereafter? One free of all hope is a (true) sanyasi; when one keeps a yogi's continence, then one is (truly) a householder. One who has compassion and reflects on his own body is a (true) Digambar; he dies (to self) himself, and kills no other. (O Lord,) you are One; the other guises are many; Nanak does not know your wonders. ॥4॥
Ankle-bells are worn by those who dance in worship. Digambar (sky-clad): a Jain ascetic who goes naked; the Jains hold to ahimsa, harming no living being.
356.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). It is not with one (fault) alone that I am filled, that I could wash it away with virtues; my Husband stays awake, while I sleep the whole night through. How, like this, can I become dear to my Husband? The Husband stays awake, while I sleep the whole night through. Full of hope and thirst, I come to his bed, (but I do not know) whether, before him, I shall please the Husband or not. O mother, how am I to know what will become (of me)? Without the sight of the Lord I cannot bear to live. I have not tasted (his) love, nor has my thirst been quenched; that youth is gone, and (now) the bride regrets it. Even now, may I wake, hoping and thirsting (to meet him); turned away (from the world), may I live free of (worldly) hopes. If (the bride) sheds her Haumai and so adorns herself, then the Husband delights in her on the bed (of the heart). Only then, O Nanak, is she pleasing to the Husband's mind, (when,) giving up her own greatness, she merges in her Master. ॥26॥
Each of the four stanzas of this shabad is followed by a Rahao line of its own.
357.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). In her parents' home the bride was very naive; I did not know the worth of that Husband. One alone is my Husband; there is no second (like him). When he casts his glance of grace, union (with him) comes about. In her in-laws' home the bride recognised the True One; in Sahaj and in love she came to know her Beloved. When, by the Guru's grace, such understanding comes, then the bride is pleasing to the Husband's mind. Says Nanak: she who adorns herself with the fear (of God) and with love, the Husband ever delights in her on the bed (of the heart). ॥4॥
357.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). No one is anyone's son, and no one anyone's mother; (yet the world,) in false attachment and doubt, has gone astray. O my Master, I am of your making; when you give (it), I repeat your Name. Someone full of faults may cry out (at his door); when it pleases him, he alone forgives. By the Guru's grace (my) evil-mindedness is gone; wherever I look, there is that One alone. Says Nanak: if such understanding comes, then one merges in the True One alone. ॥4॥
357.3: Raag Asa, Dupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (Our) dwelling has come to be in that terrible lake whose water he himself has made fire. In the mire of attachment the foot cannot move; before our eyes (many) have drowned there. O mind, O foolish mind, you do not remember the One. As you forget the Lord, your virtues have wasted away. I am neither celibate (jati) nor virtuous (sati), nor am I learned; my life has turned out the life of a foolish, ignorant one. Nanak humbly prays: (let me be) in the refuge of those who have not forgotten you. ॥2॥
The saravarra is a lake, here the world: its water is the fire of craving and its mire attachment. Pankaj here is not the lotus but the mire (pank).
Bhaile and dubiale are past forms of an eastern dialect: has come to be, have drowned.
357.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Six are the schools, six (their) teachers, and six (their) teachings; but the Guru of these teachers is the One (God), whose guises are many. The house (the school) in which the Creator is praised: hold fast to that house; in it lies your greatness. Visas, chasas, gharis, pahars, lunar days and weekdays (together) make up the month; the sun is one and the seasons many; (in the same way,) O Nanak, the Creator has so many guises. ॥2॥

The six houses are the six schools (darshanas) of Indian philosophy: Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Sankhya, Yoga, Mimamsa and Vedanta; the six teachers are their founders: Gautama, Kanada, Kapila, Patanjali, Jaimini and Vyasa.

The units of time: a visa is the time of fifteen blinks of the eye, fifteen visas make a chasa; a ghari is about twenty-four minutes and a pahar about three hours; the lunar days (thitis) are the dates of the moon's calendar.
358.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (Though you have) lakhs of troops, lakhs of drums and spears, and lakhs rise to salute (you), (though) your command runs over lakhs, and lakhs rise to do you honour; yet if (this) honour does not count in (the Lord's) reckoning, all these works are fruitless. Without the Lord's Name the world is (mere) entanglement; however much the fool is taught, he is still blind, wholly blind. Lakhs may be earned, lakhs amassed and spent; lakhs may come and lakhs may go; yet if (this) honour does not count in (the Lord's) reckoning, where then will beings find a place? There may be lakhs of expositions of the Shastras, and lakhs of pandits reading the Puranas; yet if (this) honour does not count in (the Lord's) reckoning, all of it is rejected. Honour springs from the True Name, and the Creator's Name is received by (his) grace. If (the Name) dwells in the heart day and night, then, O Nanak, by (his) glance of grace one reaches the far shore. ॥4॥
358.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The One Name is my lamp, and into it I have poured suffering as the oil; its light has dried that (oil) up, and my meeting with Jam is ended. O people, let no one take this for idle jest: gather lakhs of heaps (of wood) together, and a speck of fire is (all it takes to burn them). My pind and my leaf-plate are (the Name of) Keshav, and my kiria the True Name of the Creator; here and there, hereafter and before, this is my support. Your praise is (my) Ganga and Banaras, (in which my) soul bathes; the true bathing comes only when love (for the Lord) holds fast day and night. One (pind) for the gods, another for the forefathers: the Brahmin rolls the pind and eats (it himself); O Nanak, the pind of (the Lord's) grace never runs out. ॥4॥
Lokee and chhamichhari: by the Darpan, the gods and the forefathers (pitars), to whom pinds are offered in the rites for the dead (149.7). A ratti is a very small weight.
358.3: Raag Asa, Ghar 4, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. For the sight (of you) the gods have borne pain and hunger and made pilgrimages; yogis and celibates, keeping to their disciplines, have put on the saffron garb. For your sake, O Master, they are dyed in (your) love. Your names are many, your forms without end; how many your virtues are cannot be told. (Some) have left gates and homes, palaces, elephants and horses, and their native lands, and gone away; pirs, prophets, saliks and sadiks (the steadfast in faith) have left the world to be accepted (at your door). They gave up tastes, comfort and pleasures, and every savoury food; they left off clothes and took to skins; sorrowing and aching (for you) at your door, dyed in your Name, they became dervishes. (Some took) the leather pouch, the begging bowl, the staff and the deerskin; (some) the topknot, the sacred thread and the dhoti. You are the Master, and I am your player in guises; Nanak humbly prays: what (pride) of caste (is mine)? ॥4॥
359.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 5, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Within, in the mind, the five (lust and the rest) dwell hidden; they do not stay still, but roam about like homeless wanderers. My mind does not stay steady with the Merciful One; (it is) greedy, deceitful, sinful and false, and Maya has a strong hold on it. (The bride says:) I will wear a garland of flowers round my neck as a necklace; when my Beloved meets me, then I will adorn myself. My friends are five, and (their) husband is one; (they) cling to the tree (of the body), but the dear soul is bound to depart. The five friends join together and wail; Nanak humbly prays: the husband (the soul) is seized to give his account. ॥4॥
In this shabad the body speaks as a bride: the five friends are the five senses, and the one husband is the soul, which must leave the body.
359.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 6, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If the mind becomes a pearl for her jewel, and the breath the thread that strings it; if the bride wears forgiveness as the adornment of her body, then, made dear (to him), she delights in her Beloved. O Beloved, (your) many virtues have charmed the bride; virtues like yours are found in no other. If she takes the Lord, Har Har, for a necklace and wears it at her throat, and takes Damodar for her dandasa (the bark that colours the teeth); if she makes the Creator the bracelets she wears on her hands, and in this way holds her mind (on him); if she wears Madhusudan as the ring on her hand, and takes the Supreme God for her silk; if the bride has patience braided into her hair, and puts on Sri Rang as the kohl (of her eyes); if she lights a lamp in the temple of the mind, and makes her body the bed; then, when the King of wisdom comes to the bed, O Nanak, he takes his joy in her. ॥4॥
359.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The one who is created does as he is made to do; what complaint, brother, can be made of him? Whatever (God) means to do, he is doing; what cleverness has the created? (O God,) the one who pleases you finds your Hukam good; O Nanak, it is he who receives greatness and merges in the True Name. By the deeds done, the writ (of life) has been written; no order comes again (to undo it). What was written is what unfolds; none can wipe it out. If anyone talks too much in the (Lord's) court, he gets the name of a loose-tongued talker; his game of satranj is not won, and his piece is left raw. No one is wise for being a learned pandit, and no one bad for being a fool; the one whom (God) keeps in submission (to his will) and moves to praise him: he alone is called a banda (his servant). ॥4॥

Satranj here, by the Darpan, is the game of chaupar (113.1), in which a piece that does not reach home stays raw. Bandi (submission to God's will) and banda (his servant, a man) are a play on one word.
359.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The Guru's Shabad in my mind is my earrings, and forgiveness the patched coat I wear; whatever (the Lord) does, I accept as good; (so) I gain the treasure of the yoga of Sahaj. O brother, the one whose soul is joined (to God) is a yogi through all the ages; his union is with the Supreme Essence. He has found the Amrit Name of the Immaculate One, and within his body he enjoys the relish of (divine) wisdom. Having given up imaginings and disputes, I sit on my seat in the city of Shiv (the Lord, the source of good); the Shabad is my horn, its sound ever beautiful; day and night (my mind) sounds its note. Reflection is my begging bowl, wise understanding my staff; (seeing the Lord) present everywhere is my ashes. The Lord's praise is my discipline (of yoga); to live turned to the Guru is (my) path of the detached (Atit). (Seeing) the light (of the Lord) in all, in its many kinds and countless colours, is my sammia (arm-rest). Says Nanak: listen, Bharthari the yogi: (true yoga is) attention fixed on the one Supreme Lord. ॥4॥
Bharthari: a famous yogi of Gorakhnath's order, by tradition a king of Ujjain who gave up his throne for yoga; yogis also took the names of their famous masters.
The sammia (bairagan) is the wooden rest on which a yogi leans his arms in meditation; the pat (patra) is the begging bowl; Atit (the detached) is a name for an order of renunciants.
360.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Make divine knowledge the molasses, meditation the dhava flowers, and good conduct the kikar bark to put in; make the body the furnace and love the cooling cloth: from this wash the nectar is distilled. O brother, the mind, intoxicated, drinks the essence of the Name and stays absorbed in the joy of Sahaj; day and night it stays rapt in loving attention (to the Lord), and it has taken hold of the unstruck Shabad. The Perfect One, in Sahaj, gives this true cup to drink to that one alone on whom he casts his glance of grace. One who deals in Amrit: why would he set his love on worthless wine? The Guru's teaching is the Amrit Bani; as soon as one drinks it, one is accepted. One who loves the sight of (the Lord's) door: what would he do with liberation or paradise? Dyed in (the Lord's) praise, he is ever detached, and does not lose his life in a gamble. Says Nanak: listen, Bharthari the yogi: (such a one) is intoxicated with the stream of Amrit. ॥4॥

Liquor is distilled from molasses set to ferment with dhava (mahua) flowers and kikar bark (kas); the pocha is the wet cloth that cools the pipe, so that the vapour drips as spirit. Some yogis drank liquor for their trances.
360.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (The Creator) took Khurasan under his protection and struck terror into Hindustan; the Creator takes no blame upon himself: he made the Mughal (Babur) into Jam and sent him to invade. Such slaughter fell that (the people) cried out in anguish; did you feel no pain? O Creator, you are the one who takes care of all. If the strong strike the strong, the mind feels no grievance; (but) if a mighty lion falls upon the herd and kills, its master is called to account. The dogs have spoiled and ruined jewels (of people); no one takes any thought of the dead. You yourself join and you yourself part; see, (this is) your greatness. If someone gets himself a great name and enjoys whatever pleasures his mind fancies, in the Master's eyes he is still an insect, however many grains he pecks. Only if he dies (to himself) again and again and so lives, and utters the Name, O Nanak, does he gain anything. ॥3॥
Khurasan: to the people of Hindustan, the lands west of the Indus; the Mughal is Babur, who invaded Hindustan from there.
360.3: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. By great good fortune one receives the darshan (sight) of the Lord, through the Guru's Shabad and through true bairag (longing for the Lord). The six darshans (schools of philosophy) hold sway (in the world), but the Guru's darshan is beyond reach and boundless. Through the Guru's darshan come liberation and the high state, and the True One himself comes to dwell in the mind. Through the Guru's darshan the world is saved, if one gives (it) love and affection. But rare is the one who gives such love and affection; through the Guru's darshan there is lasting peace. Through the Guru's darshan (is found) the door of liberation; one who serves the True Guru becomes a support for his family. The one without a Guru attains no high state at all; robbed by their faults, such people suffer blows. Through the Guru's Shabad there is peace and calm in the body; through the Guru, no pain touches such a one. Jamkaal comes nowhere near him; O Nanak, the Gurmukh merges in the True One. ॥4॥
Darshan is sight, and also a school of thought, a way of seeing the truth. Here the Guru's darshan is both the sight of the Guru and the path he shows.
361.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One who has died through the Shabad sheds self-conceit from within; he serves the True Guru without a trace of greed. The fearless Giver is ever in his mind. Only by good fortune does anyone receive the True Bani. Gather virtues, and the faults within will depart; through the Shabad of the Perfect Guru you will merge (in the Lord). One who is a buyer of virtues knows (the worth of) virtues; through the Amrit Shabad he utters the Naam. Through the True Bani he becomes pure; through virtues the Naam is obtained. Virtues are priceless; they cannot be obtained (for any price); through the True Shabad they come to dwell in a pure mind. Fortunate are those who have meditated on the Naam and enshrined the Giver of virtues in their minds forever. I am a sacrifice to those who gather virtues; at the True One's door I sing the praises of the True One. (The Lord) himself gives (this gift), and (the receiver abides) in Sahaj and in love. O Nanak, the worth (of this gift) cannot be told. ॥4॥
361.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Great is the glory in the True Guru: he unites in union (with the Lord) those long separated. (The Lord) himself brings (them to the Guru) and, having brought them, unites (them with himself); he himself assesses his own worth. By what means can the Lord's worth be assessed? The Lord is beyond the farthest beyond, beyond reach and beyond the senses; only a rare one meets him through the Guru's Shabad. Rare is the one who, through the Guru, knows (his) worth; few receive (this understanding), by his grace. Through the lofty Bani one becomes lofty; rare is the one who, through the Guru, utters (the Naam) by the Shabad. Without the Name there is sorrow and pain in the body; when the True Guru is met, then the pain is lifted. Without meeting the Guru, one earns only sorrow; the manmukh receives heavy punishment. The Lord's Name is sweet, rich in relish; (but only he) keeps drinking it whom he (the Lord) gives it to drink. By the Guru's grace one obtains the Lord's relish; O Nanak, dyed in the Naam, one attains the high state. ॥4॥
361.3: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). My God is true, deep and profound; even as one serves him, the body finds peace and calm. Through the Shabad his servants have crossed over (the world-ocean), in Sahaj and in love; I fall at their feet forever. Those whose minds are dyed, having embraced the Lord's love: their pain of birth and death is gone, and through love they have met the Lord in his court. One who tastes the Shabad finds the true flavour and enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind. The Lord God always fills every place; he himself is near, he himself is far. Everyone speaks and talks (of him) for the sake of speaking, (but) he himself forgives and unites (one with himself). He is not found by saying and describing; by the Guru's grace he comes to dwell in the mind. The Gurmukh sheds self-conceit from within, and, dyed in the Lord's love, puts an end to attachment. Through reflection on the Guru's Shabad he becomes utterly pure; O Nanak, (joined) to the Naam, he becomes able to embellish (the lives of others). ॥4॥
362.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those attached to the love of another have suffered pain; without the Shabad they have squandered their life for nothing. One who serves the True Guru gains understanding, (and then) no such one clings to the love of another. Those who hold to the root (the Lord) are accepted. Night and day repeat the Name of Ram in your heart, and through the Guru's Shabad know the One Lord. One who clings to the branch goes without fruit; for blind deeds the blind one is punished. The blind manmukh finds no place of rest; a worm of filth, he rots in the filth. Through service of the Guru one finds lasting peace; joining the company of the Sants, he sings the Lord's praises. absorbed in the Naam alone, he reflects on the Naam; he himself crosses over and becomes the saviour of his family line. One who, attuned to the Naam, makes the Guru's Bani resound (within), O Nanak, finds through the Shabad (the Lord's) mansion, (his true) home. One who, by the Guru's teaching, has bathed in the pool of Truth, in the Lord's water, has washed away the filth of evil-mindedness and all sin. ॥4॥
The root is the Lord, the source of all; the branch is what grows from him: Maya, or the worship of other gods in place of him.
362.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The manmukhs die, and in dying they spoil their death; in the love of another they destroy their own soul. Saying mine, mine over and over, (the manmukh) comes to ruin; he does not recognise his own self, and stays asleep in doubt. He has truly died who dies through the Shabad: the Guru has taught (him) to hold praise and slander alike; in this age, repeating the Lord's (Name), he departs with the profit. One without the Naam wastes away in the womb (of births); lured by another, he (wastes) his life in vain. Without the Naam the whole (world) burns in pain; the Perfect True Guru has given this understanding. The fickle mind suffers many blows; having slipped away from here (this human life), it finds no place of rest. The womb and the round of births are a dwelling of filth; in that house the manmukh makes his home. To my own True Guru I am ever a sacrifice; he has merged the Gurmukh's light in the Light (of God). Through the pure Bani one comes to dwell in one's own home (within); O Nanak, (such a one) subdues Haumai and remains ever detached (from Maya). ॥4॥
362.3: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The slave (of the Lord) has lost (the pride of) his caste; offering body and mind, he has come to the True Guru's refuge. The Naam in his heart is (his) great glory; the beloved God is ever his companion. He is the (true) slave who dies while living; he holds sorrow and joy both alike, and by the Guru's grace is saved through the Shabad. The work (for him) to do has been ordained from the Lord's court: without the Shabad no one is accepted. (His) deed is the Lord's praise, and he enshrines the Naam (in his heart); (the Lord) himself gives (this gift) and makes no delay. Following its own mind, the world strays in doubt; without capital it carries on a false trade. Without capital no merchandise comes into one's hands; led astray by self-will, one wastes one's life. One who serves the True Guru becomes (the Lord's true) slave; his caste is exalted, and he himself is exalted. By the Guru's ladder he rises higher than all. O Nanak, through the Naam comes greatness. ॥4॥
Lala: a slave bought by his master; here the servant who has handed himself over wholly to the Lord.
363.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The self-willed (soul-bride) practises falsehood upon falsehood; she never attains her Master's mansion. attached to another, she strays in doubt; bound by the sense of mine, (the soul) keeps coming and going. O mind, look at the adornment of the forsaken soul-bride: (so is one who) fixes the mind on sons, wife, wealth and Maya: (all) falsehood, attachment, hypocrisy and vice. She who pleases God is a happy wife for ever; through the Guru's Shabad she adorns herself. Her bed is a place of ease; night and day she enjoys union with the Lord; meeting her Beloved, she finds lasting peace. She is a true happy wife who loves the True One; she keeps her Husband always enshrined in her heart. She sees him close at hand, ever present: my God pervades all. Caste and beauty do not go along to the world hereafter; as are the deeds one does, so does one become. Through the Shabad one rises ever higher; O Nanak, such a one merges in the True One. ॥4॥
363.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The servant dyed in devotion (abides) in Sahaj and in love; living in the true awe of the Guru, he merges in the True One. Without the perfect Guru there is no devotion; having lost their honour, the manmukhs weep. O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, and meditate on him always; (so) there is bliss always, day and night, and one gains whatever fruit one wishes for. From the perfect Guru one finds the Perfect (Lord), and makes the Shabad and the True Name dwell in the heart. Bathing in the pool of Amrit, the inner self is made pure; merged in the True One, (such ones) are pure for ever. (Such a one) sees the Lord God ever present; by the Guru's grace (he sees him) filling every place. Wherever I go, I see him there; apart from the Guru there is no other giver (of this gift). The Guru is an ocean, filled with treasures, with excellent jewels and gems beyond measure. By the Guru's grace the Giver gives (these jewels); O Nanak, the Forgiving Lord grants his grace. ॥4॥
363.3: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Guru is an ocean; the True Guru is that True One himself. Only by perfect fortune is the Guru served. That one understands (this) whom (the Lord) himself makes understand, and by the Guru's grace (the Lord) has him do (his) service. With the jewel of wisdom comes full understanding; by the Guru's grace ignorance is destroyed; one stays awake night and day, and sees that True One. One who burns away attachment and pride with the Guru's Shabad and gains understanding from the perfect Guru recognises through the Guru's Shabad the (Lord's) mansion within; his coming and going ends, and, merged in the Naam, he becomes steady. The world is (only) birth and death; the manmukh is heedless, and attachment to Maya is (for him) thick darkness. He speaks ill of others and lives by much falsehood; a worm of filth, he sinks into filth. Joining the Sat Sangat, one gains full understanding; the Guru's Shabad makes devotion to the Lord firm (within). One who accepts (God's) will has peace for ever; O Nanak, he merges in the True One. ॥4॥
364.1: Raag Asa, Panchpade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One who dies (to self) through the Shabad has bliss for ever; he meets the True Guru, and (through him) Gobind, the Great. He does not die again, nor does he come and go; through the perfect Guru he merges in the True One. Those for whom the writ of the Naam was written from the very beginning meditate on the Naam night and day, always; from the perfect Guru (they receive) the mark of devotion. Those whom the Lord God unites (with himself): their profound state cannot be told. The perfect True Guru has given (them) this glory: the highest rank, and absorption in the Lord's Name. Whatever (God) does, he does himself alone; in a single moment he sets up and pulls down. (One who) only says it over and over, telling it to others, even if he toils a hundred times, (his toil) is not accepted. Those who have merit stored in their treasury, (God) brings to meet the Guru; the Guru lets them hear the True (Name), the Bani and the Shabad. Where the Shabad dwells, from there pain departs; through the jewel of wisdom one merges, in Sahaj, in the True One. There is no other wealth as great as the Name; (it comes to) the one on whom that True One bestows it. Through the perfect Shabad, he enshrines it in the mind; O Nanak, one dyed in the Naam finds peace. ॥5॥
364.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One dances and plays many instruments, (but) this mind is blind and deaf: to whom does he speak and recite? Within him greed is a fire, and wandering doubt a gale; the lamp (of wisdom) does not burn, and he gains no understanding. With devotion through the Guru, light dawns in the heart; recognising one's own self, one meets that God. The dance done through the Guru: love for the Lord takes hold; casting out the self from within, one keeps the beat. My true God himself is the knower (of all); through the Guru's Shabad, recognise Brahm within. With devotion through the Guru, affection and love (spring up) within, the Guru's Shabad (dwells there), and reflection (on the Lord) in Sahaj. Devotion through the Guru is the way; (by it) that True One (is found); devotion and dance in hypocrisy bring only pain. This is devotion: that the servant dies while living, and by the Guru's grace crosses the world-ocean. Devotion by the Guru's word is accepted, and the dear Lord himself comes and settles in the mind. When the Lord is gracious, he brings (one) to meet the True Guru; (then) one's devotion is unwavering, and one fixes the mind on the Lord. Those dyed in devotion have lasting glory; O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam have peace. ॥5॥
365.1: Raag Asa Kafi, Ghar 8, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. By the Lord's will the True Guru is met, and the True One is understood; the one in whose mind the Lord dwells by the Guru's grace, he alone understands (him). My Husband Lord alone is the Giver; there is no other at all. When by the Guru's kindness he dwells in the mind, then there is peace for ever. In this age the Lord's Name is fearless (and makes one fearless); it is found through reflection on the Guru's teaching. Without the Name, the blind and foolish self-willed (soul-bride) is in Jam's power. By the Lord's will his servant serves him, and understands that True One. By the Lord's will he is praised; in accepting his will there is peace. By the Lord's will the precious gift of human birth has been received, and the understanding made noble. O Nanak, praise the Naam; through the Guru the supreme state is reached. ॥4॥
Kafi: this hymn is to be sung in Asa blended with Raag Kafi. The closing figures count the hymns in Raag Asa so far: 39 by the First Guru and 13 by the Third, 52 in all.
365.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. You are the Creator, the abode of truth, my Master. Whatever pleases you, that alone will be; whatever you give, that alone I receive. All (creation) is yours; all have meditated on you. The one to whom you show grace has found the jewel of the Naam. The Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) found it; the manmukh (the self-willed) lost it. You yourself have parted (beings from you), and you yourself have united (them). You are the river; all is within you alone. Apart from you there is no other. All beings and creatures are your play. By the will that parts, even one who had met is separated; by the will that unites, there is meeting (again). Only the one whom you make to understand comes to know (you), and he ever speaks and tells of the Lord's virtues. Whoever has served the Lord has found peace; in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) he has merged in the Name of the Lord. You yourself are the Creator; all that happens is your doing. Apart from you there is no other, no second. You create and create, watch over (your creation), and know all about it. O servant Nanak, (the Lord) is revealed within the Gurmukh. ॥4॥
Sachiar: sach and alaya (abode), the abode of truth, God who ever abides.
ਸਭ ਤੇਰੀ ਤੂੰ ਸਭਨੀ ਧਿਆਇਆ: here ਤੂੰ means you as the object (ਤੈਨੂੰ), and ਸਭਨੀ means by all.
Vijog and sanjog: the powers of God's will that part beings and bring them together.
366.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Someone has formed a faction with a friend, a son and a brother; someone has formed a faction with in-laws, kinsmen and a son-in-law; someone has formed a faction with officials and headmen, for his own ends; my faction is the Lord, who pervades all. I have formed my faction with the Lord; the Lord is my support. Apart from the Lord I have no other side or faction; I sing the Lord's virtues, countless and many. Those with whom (people) form factions pass away; forming factions in falsehood, (people) repent. They do not last for ever, and they practise deceit in the mind. I have formed my faction with the Lord, whose equal in might there is none. All these factions are the spread of Maya and attachment; the foolish fight over Maya. They keep being born and dying, and lose the game (of life) in a gamble. My faction is the Lord, who sets right this world and the next, all of it. In Kalyug, the five thieves stir up factions and quarrels; and lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride are made to grow. The one on whom (God) shows grace, he unites with the Sat Sangat. My faction is the Lord, who has done away with all these factions. False love of another, settling in, creates factions; (one) scrutinises others' faults and swells one's own pride. As one sows, so one eats. Servant Nanak's faction is the Lord; (this) dharma comes back victorious over the whole world. ॥5॥
366.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). As (Gurbani) is heard over and over in the heart, the Amrit (of the Name) has grown dear to the mind; Gurbani has revealed the Unseen Lord. O my sisters, through the Guru, listen to the Naam; the One alone pervades within every heart; with your mouths speak the Guru's words of Amrit. In my mind and body there is love (for the Lord) and a great longing; by great good fortune I have found the True Guru, the Purakh. Those who wander in the love of another, after Maya, the poison, are luckless: they have not found the True Guru. The Lord himself has given (me) the Amrit to drink, the sweet essence of the Lord; through the perfect Guru, Nanak has found the Lord. ॥4॥
366.3: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). In my mind and body is love (for God), and (his) Name is my support. I repeat the Name; the Name alone is the essence of peace. Repeat the Name, my friends and companions. Without the Name I have no other (support); only by great good fortune is (the Name of) the Lord received through the Guru. Without the Name one cannot live. By great good fortune one finds the Lord through the Guru. Those empty of the Name bear the soot of Maya on their faces. Without the Name, cursed, cursed is such living. The Lord, greatest of the great, is found by great good fortune; O Nanak, (he himself) has the Name given through the Guru. ॥4॥
367.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). I sing (God's) virtues, I speak the word of (his) virtues; through the Guru I utter and tell the Lord's virtues. Repeating the Name again and again, bliss has come into my mind. The True Guru has made the Name, the True, the True, firm (within me); with delight I have sung the praises of (the Lord of) supreme bliss. The Lord's servants, his people, sing the Lord's praises; by great good fortune they find the Lord, who is detached (from all). Those without virtue carry the filth of Maya about; without virtue the proud are born and die. In the pool of the body (God's) virtues have been brought to light; O Nanak, through the Guru, by churning (it), the essence is drawn out. ॥4॥
367.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). I hear the Name; the Name alone is pleasing to my mind. By great good fortune one finds the Lord through the Guru. Repeat the Name through the Guru, and light dawns (within). Without the Name I have no support; with every breath and every morsel I dwell on the Name. (Since) I heard tell of the Name alone, it has been dear to my mind; whoever tells me of the Name is my friend and companion. The fools empty of the Name have gone (from the world) naked; seeing the poison (of Maya), they burned and burned to death like the moth. (God) himself establishes, and having established, himself pulls down; O Nanak, the Lord himself gives the Name. ॥4॥
367.3: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Gurmukh has made the vine of the Lord, Har Har, grow; it has borne fruits, full of flavour to those who relish the Lord. Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the Lord of endless waves. Repeating the Name again and again, praise (God) through the Guru's teaching; (so) death, Jam's servants and the serpent are slain. The Lord, Har Har, has placed (his) devotion in the Guru; the Guru, pleased, gives (it) to the Sikh, O my brother. One who does deeds in Haumai knows nothing of the way (of devotion); he is like the elephant that bathes and (then) throws dust over its head. If (people's) fortune is great, great and lofty, O Nanak, (they) repeat the Name and, (joined) to the True One, become pure. ॥4॥
367.4: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). A hunger for the Name of the Lord, Har Har, has been awakened in my mind; hearing the Name, the mind is satisfied, O my brother. Repeat the Name, my friends, Sikhs of the Guru. Repeat the Name; in the Name itself you will find peace; through the Guru's teaching keep the Name in your mind and consciousness. Hearing the Name, the Name alone, the mind turns green (with life); earning the profit of the Name through the Guru's teaching, it blossoms. Without the Name one is a leper, blinded by attachment; all the deeds one does are fruitless, entanglements that bring pain. It is the one of great good fortune who repeats the praise of the Lord, Har Har Har; O Nanak, by the Guru's teaching, his attention (liv) is held fast in the Name. ॥4॥
368.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 6, three shabads by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The yogi takes (his instrument) in hand and plays the string, but the veena sounds hollow. O yogi, through the Guru's teaching utter the Lord's praises, and this mind will be drenched in the Lord's love. O yogi, give your understanding the teaching of the Lord. In every age the one Lord, Har Har, is at work; before him I bow. They sing raags and speak in many ways, but this mind keeps playing its own games. (They are like those who) yoke (the oxen to) the well to water the land, but the oxen have got up and gone off to graze on the vines. In the town of the body sow the deeds of (remembering) the Lord; the Lord sprouts, and the field turns green. Make the mind steady and yoke that mind as the ox, and with it water (the field) with the Lord through the Guru's teaching. (O God,) the yogis, the jangams, the whole creation are yours; whatever understanding you give, by that they walk. O God of servant Nanak, Knower of hearts, O Lord, urge my mind on and join it (to yourself). ॥4॥
368.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Why should one go looking for ankle bells to keep time, why play the rabab? In coming and going (for them) an instant passes; for that long I would hold the Name in my heart. Such devotion has taken shape in my mind that I cannot live an instant, a moment, without the Lord, as a fish dies without water. Why should one tune the five (strings) and the seven (notes) to sing, why raise the strain of a raag? In tuning and choosing, an instant, a moment, a little while passes; for that long my mind sings the praises of the Lord (Ram). Why should one dance, stretching out the feet, why stretch out the hands? In stretching out hands and feet a moment's delay passes; for that long my mind remembers the Lord (Ram). Why should one try to win the people's trust? When the world is won over, no honour comes of it. O servant Nanak, meditate on the Lord in your heart always; then everyone hails (you). ॥4॥
368.3: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Let us join the Sat Sangat, meet the Lord's Saadh (the Guru), and, joined in the Sangat, sing the Lord's praises. (So) the jewel of divine knowledge shines, there is light in the heart, and the darkness of ignorance goes. O servants of the Lord, dance, meditating on the Lord, Har Har. If I meet such Sants, O my brother, I would wash the feet of those servants. O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, holding your attention on the Lord night and day. Whatever you wish for, that fruit you will obtain, and hunger will not come upon you again. The Lord himself is the boundless Creator; the Lord himself speaks and makes (all) speak. (O God,) those Sants alone are good who are pleasing to you, whose honour you accept. Nanak is never sated with uttering the Lord's praises; the more he utters them, the more peace he finds. The Lord has given the storehouses of his devotion; the buyer of virtues trades and carries them away. ॥4॥
369.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa Kafi, Ghar 8, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Death has come, ordained from the very start; it is through Haumai that one weeps (over it). Meditating on the Name through the Guru, one becomes steady. Those who, through the Perfect Guru, have understood that they must depart win acclaim; they have earned the Name, that excellent profit, and through the Shabad they are merged (in God). The days written beforehand, O mother, those days have come; the departure, today or tomorrow, has been decreed from the start. Wasted is the life of those who have forgotten the Name; they have played a game of dice in the world and lost this mind. Those who have found the Guru have peace in life and in death; O Nanak, true, they merge in the True One, in the True One. ॥4॥
369.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). (Whoever,) having received the precious gift of human birth, has meditated on the Name has, by the Guru's grace, understood (its worth) and merged in the True One. Those for whom it was so written from the start have practised the Name; at the True One's door they are found true, and (he) has called them into his palace. The treasure of the Name is within (everyone), (but) it is found through the Guru; meditating on the Name night and day, let us sing the Lord's praises. Within lies the wealth (of the Name) with its countless virtues, (but) the self-willed do not find it; (the manmukh) swells with pride in Haumai, and through that pride goes astray by himself. O Nanak, (the manmukh) goes astray by himself, by his own doing alone; through the Guru's teaching there is light in the mind, and the True One is found. ॥4॥
369.3: Raag Asavari, Ghar 16, two shabads by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji), Sudhang. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Night and day I sing the Kirtan of the Lord's Name. The True Guru has shown me the Lord's Name; I cannot live an instant, a moment, without the Lord. Hearing (of the Lord), Simran and the Lord's Kirtan are (all) I have; I cannot live without the Lord, not for a single instant. As the swan cannot live without the lake, so how can the Lord's servant live without serving the Lord? Some have set their love on another, holding duality in the heart; some have set their love on attachment and pride; the Lord's servant has set his love on the Lord, the state of nirvana; O Nanak, he keeps remembering the Lord God, Har Har. ॥2॥
Asavari is a raag akin to Asa, and its shabads stand within Raag Asa. Sudhang: in its pure form, sung in the raag's own notes.
369.4: Raag Asavari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mother, tell me (where to find) my Beloved, the Lord (Ram), O mother. I cannot live an instant, a moment, without the Lord, as the camel delights in the vine. My mind has grown full of longing and turned away (from the world), for the sight of the Lord, my Friend. As the bumblebee cannot be without the lotus, so I cannot live without the Lord. Keep me in your refuge, O beloved Lord of the world; fulfil my longing, O Lord, Master of the earth (Gusain). Bliss wells up in servant Nanak's mind when you show him your sight, O Lord, even for the blink of an eye. ॥2॥
The closing figures total the shabads of Raag Asa so far: 39 by the First Guru, 13 by the Third, 15 by the Fourth, 67 in all.
370.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Whoever set his love on (Maya) was in the end devoured by her; whoever seated her in comfort, to him she showed great fear. Brothers, friends and family quarrel (among themselves) at the sight of her; by the Guru's grace she has come under our control. Seeing her so, (all) have been bewitched: seekers, Siddhas, gods and men; all but the Saadh (the Guru) have been cheated by the cheat. Some wander as renunciates, but she seizes them through lust; some, as householders, hoard her, but she does not become their own; some are called sati (givers of charity), and she torments them greatly; the Lord has saved us by attaching us to the True Guru's feet. She has led the ascetics astray even as they practise austerities; all the pandits she has enticed through greed; she has enticed (the beings of) the three qualities, she has enticed the heavens; the True Guru has saved us, giving (us) his hand. To the one who knows (God) she is a handmaid in waiting; with folded hands she serves him and prays: Whatever you say, that work I will do; O servant Nanak, (she says,) I will not come near the Gurmukh. ॥4॥
The shabad does not name her; in the commentaries she is Maya, who herself speaks in the last two lines. Sati: here, a giver of charity (so the Darpan and the Santhya).
370.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My Husband has set me apart from my mother-in-law; my sisters-in-law, younger and elder, have died of grief and anguish; the hold of the household's elder brother-in-law has ended; my Husband, skilful and wise, has protected me. Listen, O people: I have found the sweet essence of love. The wicked are slain, the enemies destroyed; the True Guru has given me the Lord's Name. First, I gave up the love of Haumai; second, I gave up the ways of the world; leaving the three qualities, foe and friend have become alike (to me); meeting the Saadh (the Guru), I have recognised the quality of the fourth state (turiya). In the cave of Sahaj I have set my seat; the unstruck sound (Anhad) of the One whose form is light has begun to ring; reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, there is supreme bliss; the bride steeped in the love of her Beloved is blessed, a happy wedded wife. Servant Nanak speaks of the contemplation of God; whoever hears it and lives it crosses over. He is neither born nor dies, neither comes nor goes; he remains merged in the Lord. ॥4॥
The commentaries read the household so: the Husband is God, the mother-in-law ignorance (avidya), the sisters-in-law hope and craving, and the elder brother-in-law Dharam Raj.
370.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Single-minded devotion (to the Lord) is a bride of noble nature, peerless in beauty, perfect in conduct. The home in which she dwells is graced with glory; (but) only some rare being has won her, through the Guru. Meeting the Guru, I have won a bride of noble deeds, who graces the sacred rite, the wedding, and every occasion.
