As long as she lived with her father (the Guru), so long did her husband (the soul) wander about in great sadness. (When he) served and won the favour of the True Being, the Guru brought her into the home, and then every comfort was found. She bears the thirty-two good marks; Truth is her offspring, her sons. She is obedient, accomplished and fair. She fulfils the wishes of her husband and master's heart, and she has contented all the wives of her husband's brothers, younger and elder. In all the family she is the best, and she gives good counsel to her husband's brothers, younger and elder. Blessed is the home where she comes and shines forth; O servant Nanak, (life there) passes in peace upon peace. ॥4॥

In this shabad devotion is a bride: the Guru is her father and the soul her husband. The commentators read her sisters-in-law as hope and craving, and her husband's brothers as the senses (or as greed and pride).

The thirty-two good marks (battih sulakhani): by tradition, the qualities of an ideal wife, among them modesty, compassion, humility and patience. Jaj is a sacred rite (yajna) and kaaj a wedding; at such rites a wife stands beside her husband.
371.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Every resolve I make, she (Maya) keeps from ripening; she stands on guard close by goodness and self-restraint. She takes on many disguises and displays many forms; she will not let me dwell in my home, and leads me astray this way and that. She has (set herself up as) mistress of the house, and gives me no place to live in it; if I make an effort, she tangles me (all the more). She came sent from the Source as a servant, (yet) she has conquered the nine regions and every place and space; on river banks and at places of pilgrimage she spares neither yogis nor sannyasis; (scholars) have worn themselves out reading the Simritis and studying the Vedas. Where I sit, there she sits too, at my side; in her might she forces her way into all the worlds. Taking refuge with the feeble, I cannot stay safe (from her); tell me, friend, to whom shall I go? On hearing counsel, I came to the True Guru; the Guru made the mantra of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm within me. Singing the praises of the Infinite, I have come to dwell in my own home within; God has met me, and Nanak is free of care. The house is mine (now), and this mistress is mine; (now) she is my servant; the Guru has made me one of (the Lord's) court. ॥4॥
The woman of this shabad is not named; the commentators read her as Maya, sent into the world to serve, who has made herself mistress of the house of the heart.
371.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The first counsel was that I should send a letter; the second, that I should send two men (to speak for me); the third, that I should try some means or other; but I gave up everything, O God, and meditated on you alone. (Now) there is supreme bliss, freedom from care and Sahaj; the foes and the enemies have perished, and I have found peace. The True Guru gave me this teaching: soul and body are all the Lord's domain. Whatever I do is by your strength; you are my shelter, you alone my support. Leaving you, O God, to which side could one go? There is no other, no second, equal to you. To whom does your servant owe deference? It is the Saakat who strays, wandering in the wilderness. Your greatness cannot be told; wherever it may be, you take (your servant) in your embrace and save him. Nanak, your servant, is in your refuge; God has kept (my) honour, and songs of rejoicing ring out. ॥4॥
372.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Banker,) struggling across alien lands, I have come for trade; I had heard of a peerless, profitable ware. I have brought a capital of virtues tied in the hem of my cloth; seeing the jewel (of the Name), this mind of mine clings to it. O Banker, the traders have come to your door; bring out the goods, and let the deal be struck. The Banker (God) sent me to the Banker (the Guru); priceless is the jewel, priceless the capital. I found a loving friend to act as go-between, (through him) the bargain was made, and my mind is steady. It fears no thieves, no wind, no water; in Sahaj I bought it, and in Sahaj I shall take it away. Earning it by truth, I have met no pain, and I have brought it home safe and sound. The profit is gained, and joy has come; blessed is the perfect, forgiving Banker! Only someone rare has gained this bargain, through the Guru; Nanak has brought home a fruitful cargo. ॥4॥
The Banker (Shah) is the Lord, or the Guru through whom he trades; the traders are seekers, and the jewel and the goods are the Name.
372.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (My Husband) did not weigh any merit or fault of mine, nor look at my beauty, my colour or my adornment; I knew nothing of the ways of good manners and good conduct; (yet) the Beloved took me by the arm and brought me to his bed. Listen, my friend: my Husband has done a husband's part by me; his hand upon my brow, he has made me his own and kept me safe; what do these unknowing people know (of it)? Now, at last, my wedded happiness shines; my Husband has met me, and has looked into all my pain. In my courtyard is the radiance of the moon; night and day there is bliss with my Beloved. My clothes are dyed a deep red; all my jewels and the flowers at my throat adorn me. My Beloved looked upon me with his glance, and I gained all treasures; the hold of the wicked enemies is at an end. I enjoy happiness ever, and delight ever; the Naam, the nine treasures, is in my home, and I am fulfilled. Says Nanak, when the Husband has adorned (the soul-bride), she is a happy wife, abiding for ever with her Husband. ॥4॥
372.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (People) give alms (to the Brahmins) and pay them worship; yet even as they take what is given, they deny it. O Brahmin, at the door to which you must go, at that door it is you who will repent. Such Brahmins are drowned, O brother, who plot harm against the innocent. Greed is within them; they wander about as if rabid; they slander others, and lift a load (of sin) on to their heads. Robbed by Maya, (the Brahmin) does not remember (the Lord); lost in doubt, he strays on many paths. Outwardly they put on many religious garbs, but within, the poison of Maya has laid siege and encamped. He teaches others but has no understanding himself; such a Brahmin succeeds nowhere. O foolish Brahmin, keep God in mind; seeing and hearing, he is with you. Says Nanak, if (it is your) good fortune, give up your pride and fall at the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
372.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Pain and sickness have gone from the body; the mind is pure, singing the praises of the Lord, Har Har; joining the company of the Saadh (the Guru), there is bliss; now my mind wanders nowhere. The burning (within) is quenched through the Guru's Shabad, O mother; all fever and dread are gone; I have met the Guru who cools and calms, and (abide) in Sahaj and in love. My running about has ended, for I have understood the One alone; now, unshaken, I have settled in my place. (O Lord,) your Sants save the world; beholding the sight of them, I am content. The sins of (many) births have fallen behind me; now, steadfast, I have taken hold of the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). (My) mind sings songs of joy in the strain of Sahaj; death no longer devours it. O Cause of creation, my all-powerful (Lord), Giver of peace, my Lord King, Har Har: Nanak lives by repeating your Name; like warp and weft you are with me, my help. ॥4॥
373.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The slanderer howls and wails; the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, has slipped from his mind; the slanderer receives what he himself has done. If anyone keeps him company, (the slanderer) takes him along on his way. The slanderer carries a load as huge as a python, of things that are not, and burns (himself) in the fire. What comes to pass at the door of the Supreme God, Nanak tells aloud: the Lord's devotees are in bliss for ever; singing the Lord's Kirtan, (the devotee) blossoms. ॥2॥
373.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When I had made every adornment, even then my mind was not content. I put many perfumes on my body, (yet) I do not find that joy, not even a sesame seed's worth. In my mind I cherish this hope: that seeing my Beloved I may live, O my mother. Mother, what am I to do? This mind finds no patience. Longing for my darling Beloved steals it away. Clothes, jewellery and pleasures of many special kinds: these too I count as of no worth. Honour, fame, respect and greatness, the whole world at my command, a home so fair, like a ruby: (yet) only if I please God shall I be happy for ever. Dishes and foods of many kinds, pleasures and shows spread out in plenty, kingdom, lands, and wide command: (with these) the mind is not filled, and its thirst does not go. Without meeting (him), I cannot get through this day; if God is met, (the soul-bride) gains every comfort. Searching and searching, I have heard this word: without the Saadh Sangat no one has crossed over. One with good fortune on the forehead has found the True Guru; that one's hope is fulfilled, and the mind is satisfied. When God was met, the burning (within) came to an end; O Nanak, (that one) found (him) within mind and body. ॥4॥
373.3: Raag Asa, Panchpade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). First, your kind is noble (you are born human); second, your family line is held in honour; third, your dwelling place is beautiful; yet your form is marred, for there is pride in your mind. (O soul-bride,) you are lovely, fair of form, wise and clever, yet you are caught in great pride and in attachment. Your kitchen is spotlessly pure; having bathed, you worship and put a red tilak (on your brow); you boast with words, and with your mouth you utter wisdom; but the dog of greed has wasted all your good ways. You wear (fine) clothes and enjoy pleasures; you keep up (religious) observances for a good name among people; you spread about perfume, sandalwood and sweet scents; but your companion is wicked anger, the chandal (outcaste). All other species are your water-carriers (your servants); on this earth the rule is yours; gold, silver and wealth are in your keeping; but lust has spoilt your virtuous character. She on whom the Lord King casts his glance of mercy is set free from captivity (to the vices). One who, joining the Saadh Sangat, has found the Lord's sweet essence: says Nanak, that body is fruitful. As a happy wedded wife (of the Lord), all beauty and all comforts become you; (then) you are truly most beautiful and wise. ॥12॥
This shabad speaks to the soul-bride, the human being, whose birth stands above all other species. Rahao Dooja: the second Rahao (Pause) of this shabad, which answers the first.
374.1: Raag Asa, two Iktuke, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Whoever is seen to be alive (in ego) must surely die; whoever has died (to self) shall remain unshaken. Those who have died while living: those dead ones truly live; they have put the medicine of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, into their mouths, and through the Guru's Shabad they drink the essence of Amrit. The unbaked pot (of the body) must surely break; one whose trikuti (the knitted brow of inner fretting) is loosed comes to dwell in his own home within. Whoever climbs high (in pride) falls into the nether world; whoever lies low on the ground (in humility) is not touched by death. Those who went wandering about have gained nothing; those are steadfast who have lived the Guru's Shabad. Soul and body, all is the Lord's property; O Nanak, meeting the Guru, (those who know this) are filled with joy. ॥5॥
Iktuke: hymns whose every stanza is a single tuk (one verse in two halves); the figure 2 says that two such hymns follow.
374.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Your puppet (of a body) has been fashioned with great skill; know it for the truth: it will turn to dust. Keep your Root (the Lord) in mind, O heedless fool; why do you take pride in so little? You are a guest (in this world), given three seers (of grain) a day; everything else is with you only in trust. Filth, bones and blood, wrapped up in skin: over this you have taken up pride. If you understand the One Thing (the Name), you will become pure; without that understanding you remain impure for ever. Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to the Guru, by whom the Lord is found, the all-pervading, all-knowing Being. Raag Asa, Iktuke Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). One ghari of the day is to me as many days; my mind finds no rest: how shall I meet my Beloved? Not one moment, not one day ever seems to pass for me; in my mind is a great longing for his sight; if only some Sant would unite me with my Husband. The day's four watches are as long as the four ages; when night falls, there seems to be no end to it. She whom the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) together have parted from her Husband wanders and wanders, weeping and wringing her hands. To servant Nanak the Lord has shown his sight; knowing his own self, he has attained the highest peace. ॥4॥
A seer is an old measure of weight; three (light) seers of grain were held to be a day's food.
375.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the Lord's service is the supreme treasure; the Lord's service is (to utter) the Amrit Name with the mouth. The Lord is my companion, my friend ever at my side; in pain or in pleasure he is present whenever I remember him; how can poor Jam frighten me? The Lord is my shelter; the Lord's is the strength I have; the Lord is my friend, the support of my mind. The Lord is my stock in trade, the Lord my credit; I earn the wealth (of the Name) through the Guru; the Lord is my Banker. Through the Guru's grace this understanding comes; servant Nanak merges in the Lord's embrace. ॥4॥
375.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). If God is merciful, then I fix this mind (on the True Guru), and serving the True Guru I obtain every fruit. O mind, why should you grieve? My True Guru is perfect; he grants the mind's desires, he is the treasure of every comfort, a pool of Amrit ever brimming full. Whoever has enshrined the lotus feet (of the Lord) within the heart, in him the Light has shone forth, and he has met the beloved Lord (Ram). The five companions (the senses) joined to sing a song of joy, and sounded the unstruck music (nad) of the Bani. Guru Nanak was pleased, and the Lord King was met; the night (of life) has passed in peace, in Sahaj and in love. ॥4॥
375.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In his mercy the Lord has become manifest (within me); I have met the True Guru and found the perfect wealth. Such wealth of the Lord should be gathered, O brother: fire does not burn it, water does not drown it, and it never leaves one's side to go elsewhere. It never falls short, nor does it run out; the mind, eating of it and spending it, stays satisfied. He is the true banker in whose house the Lord's wealth is stored; from this wealth the whole world gains. He alone has found the Lord's wealth whose due it was, written beforehand; O servant Nanak, at the very end the Name is (the soul's) adornment. ॥4॥
375.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). As a farmer sows his crop and cuts it, unripe or ripe, O mortal, (so death comes at any age). Know that whoever is born shall die; the devotee of Govind (alone) has become steadfast. After the day, night will surely fall; and when the night is gone, morning comes again. The unfortunate lie asleep in attachment to Maya; by the Guru's grace some rare one wakes. Says Nanak, let (the Lord's) praises be sung every day; (so) the face becomes radiant, and the mind pure. ॥4॥
376.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) yours are the nine treasures, all the treasures; (you are) the Fulfiller of desires, who protects at the last. You are my Beloved; then what hunger can there be? When you dwell in my mind, no pain touches me. Whatever you do, that alone is accepted; O true Master, true is your command. When it pleases you, then I sing the Lord's praises; in your house there is justice for ever and ever. O true Master, unseen, beyond all knowing, as you attach him, so Nanak is attached to (your) service. ॥4॥
376.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The Lord) is near to every being, ever at their side; his power is at work in every form and colour. (My) mind does not fret, nor pine, nor is it given to weeping, (for) our Master is imperishable, unmanifest, beyond the reach of the senses, secure for ever. (O Lord,) to whom need your humble servant defer, when the King himself upholds his honour? The slave whom God has freed from caste need fear no one's envy. (The Lord) depends on no one, and is free of all care; says servant Nanak: hail the Great Master as wondrous (Wah). ॥4॥
376.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Forsaking the Lord's sweet essence, (man) is drunk on shallow pleasure; the treasure is in his own house, yet he gets up and goes outside (to seek it). He cannot bear to hear the true, Amrit discourse; caught up in false tales, he quarrels. He draws his wages from the Master, but serves another; with such sins is the mortal covered over. He hides from the One who is ever his companion; what is of no use, that he begs for again and again. Says Nanak: O God, merciful to the meek, as it pleases you, so cherish (us). ॥4॥
376.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord's Name is the wealth of soul and breath; here and hereafter it is what serves them (soul and breath). Without the Lord's Name, all else is too little; my mind is sated and fulfilled by the Lord's sight. The Gurbani is a ruby, a storehouse of devotion; singing it, hearing it and living it, (the mind) is filled with joy. (My) mind is attached to the lotus feet (of the Lord); the True Guru, pleased, has given this gift. The Guru has given Nanak such teaching that he has recognised the imperishable God in every heart. ॥4॥
376.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord who fills every place has brought forth delights and wondrous plays; his own work he has himself made fair. Complete is all the making of the perfect Master, whose glory is spread abroad, filling every place. He whose Name is a treasure, whose renown is spotless, is himself the Creator; there is none other. All beings and creatures are in his hand; God pervades all, and is with everyone. The Perfect Guru has made a perfect arrangement; O Nanak, the devotees have been given honour. ॥4॥
377.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through the Guru's Shabad, shape this mind of yours; the sight of the Guru is the Lord's wealth: gather it. O noble understanding, come and dwell in my heart, that I may meditate on Govind and sing his virtues, and that the Name may grow most dear to me. In the True Name are fullness and content; the dust (of the feet) of the Sants is bathing at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage. In all I know the one Creator; joining the Saadh Sangat, the intellect has gained discernment. Giving up pride, (I have become) the servant of all; the Guru has blessed Nanak with (this) gift. ॥4॥
377.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (My) intellect is lit up, (my) understanding made whole; by it, evil-mindedness and distance (from the Lord) are destroyed. Such is the Guru's teaching I have received that, drowning in a dreadful dark well, I have come out (of it), O my brother. (This world) is a vast, unfathomable ocean of fire; the Guru, a mine of jewels, is the ship that carries (one) across. This Maya is hard to cross, dark and perilous; the Perfect Guru has shown (me) the way, plain to see. I have no chanting, no austerity, no clever argument at all; O Guru, Nanak (has come) into your refuge. ॥4॥
377.3: Raag Asa, two Tipade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Drinking the Lord's sweet essence, one stays dyed (in it) for ever; other tastes wear off in a moment. Those drunk with the Lord's essence have bliss in the mind for ever; in other tastes, anxiety takes hold. Whoever drinks the Lord's essence is wholly intoxicated, enraptured; all other tastes are shallow, O brother. The worth of the Lord's essence cannot be told; the Lord's essence is kept in the shop of the Saadh (the Guru). For lakhs and crores (of coins) no one obtains it; (O Lord,) you give it to the one whose lot it is to receive it. Tasting it, Nanak is lost in wonder; O Nanak, this savour has come from the Guru. here and hereafter, (he) does not leave it to go anywhere else; Nanak is steeped in the Lord's sweet essence. ॥3॥
377.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O soul-bride,) if you wipe out lust, anger, greed and attachment, the evil-mindedness you have taken up yourself falls away; if, becoming humble, you serve, you will be dear to your Beloved's heart. Listen, O lovely one: the words of the Saadh (the Guru) bring rescue; your pain, hunger and dread will be gone, and you will find peace, O woman who longs for a mind at peace. Wash (his) feet and serve the Guru: the soul grows pure, and the poison and the thirst (of Maya) are driven out. If you become the handmaid, the lowly handmaid, of (the Lord's) servants, you will win honour at the Lord's door. This alone is right conduct, this alone the daily way: obey (the Lord's) command, and your devotion is fulfilled. Whoever lives by this mantra (teaching), O Nanak, is carried across the terrifying world-ocean. ॥3॥
378.1: Raag Asa, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). You have received this lovely human body; this is your turn to meet Gobind (the Lord of the universe). All other tasks are of no use to you at all; join the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) and remember the Naam alone. Set yourself to the task of crossing the ocean of the world; your life is passing in vain in the love of Maya. (O Lord,) I have practised neither repetition (of the Name), austerity, self-restraint nor any deed of dharma; I have not served the Saadh (the holy one), nor have I known you, O Lord, my King. Says Nanak, we are of lowly deeds; save the honour of one who has come into your refuge. ॥2॥
The first six lines counsel the soul; in the last four Nanak prays humbly to God on behalf of all beings.
378.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) apart from you I have no other at all; you are within my mind. You are (my) friend, my companion, my God; why then, O my soul, are you afraid? Yours is my shelter, in you my hope; sitting or rising, sleeping or waking, with every breath and every morsel, may I never forget you. Keep me, keep me in your refuge, O God; (this world) is a fearsome ocean of fire. O True Guru, Giver of peace to Nanak, we are your children, O Gopal. ॥2॥
378.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). God has set the Lord's servants free; my mind is at one with the Beloved; the fever has died, as if it had eaten poison. Neither chill nor heat touches (one) at all who sings the praises of the Name of Ram; the witch has no hold at all on the mind that is in the refuge of the lotus feet. By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), (the Lord) has become merciful and has himself become (my) help. Nanak sings ever of the Treasure of virtues, dread and pain wiped away. ॥2॥

Chill and heat (pala, tau) are the two stages of a fever: first the shivering, then the burning. Daki (Sanskrit dakini) is a witch. Bhai Vir Singh's Santhya takes this shabad and the next as thanks for being spared a spreading fever; the Darpan reads the fever and the witch as Maya.
378.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have taken the medicine of the Lord's Name; I have found comfort, and the very seat of pain is destroyed. The fever has left, by the word of the Perfect Guru; there is joy, and all sorrows are wiped away. All beings and creatures have found peace who, O Nanak, have meditated on the Supreme Lord in their minds. ॥2॥
378.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). That hour (of death), which no one wishes for, arrives; without (the Lord's) Hukam, how can one understand, though it be explained? (The body) is consumed by the cold (water), the hot (fire) or the earth; (but) that (soul) is neither child nor old, O brother. Servant Nanak is in the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru); by the Guru's grace (he) has crossed beyond fear. ॥2॥
Cold, hot and earth: water, fire and earth, which take the dead body when it is given to the river, burnt or buried.
378.6: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). For ever and ever the soul is lit up in one who, in the Saadh Sangat, dwells at the Lord's feet. Repeat the Name of Ram every day, O my mind; you will find coolness, calm and lasting peace, and all your sins will go, O mind. Says Nanak, one whose destiny is perfect meets the True Guru, and meets the perfect Supreme Lord. The thirty-four (shabads) of the Second Ghar.
With this shabad the thirty-four shabads of the Fifth Guru in Ghar 2 of Raag Asa are complete; the count of the shabads that follow runs on from them.
378.7: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). She whose friend is the Lord, the Master, God: her pain is gone, and never again is she in misery. In his mercy he has joined her to his feet; she is at ease, in comfort, Sahaj and bliss. Singing (his) virtues in the Saadh Sangat, she has grown beyond all weighing; remembering the Lord, O Nanak, she has become priceless. ॥2॥
379.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Lust, anger, Maya, pride and envy: all these (we) have gambled away and lost; truth, contentment, compassion, dharma and truthful living: these (we) have brought into our own home. All the burdens of birth and death are ended; joining the company (of the holy), the mind has become pure; the Perfect Guru has taken (us) along and carried (us) across in an instant. The mind remains the dust (of the feet) of all, and all appear as dear friends. My Master pervades all; giving his gifts, he takes care of all beings. He himself is the One, the One alone, only the One; the whole expanse is the One's alone. Repeating (the Name) again and again, all have become holy; meditating on the one Name, they have saved a great many. The Lord of the world is deep, profound and boundless; he has no end at all, no near shore and no far shore. By your grace, (O Lord,) Nanak sings (your) praises, and, meditating again and again, bows before God. ॥4॥
379.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) you are infinite, unmanifest, beyond the reach of the senses; all this (visible) form is yours. What cleverness can we creatures show, when everything is within you? O my True Guru, by your wondrous play keep your children safe; give (me) good understanding, that I may ever sing (your) virtues, O my Master, inaccessible and infinite. As the mortal in the mother's womb lives on the support of the Name: he is in bliss, keeps (the Lord) in mind with every breath, and the fire (of the womb) cannot touch him. Another's wealth, another's wife, the slander of others: take away (my) love for these; may I serve (your) lotus feet within my heart, upheld by the Perfect Guru. Home, mansions and palaces, whatever is seen: none of them goes along; as long as you live in this age of Kalyug, O servant Nanak, cherish the Naam (in your heart). ॥4॥
379.3: Raag Asa, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Rule, lands, the bloom of youth, home, renown, a handsome form, youthful vigour, great wealth, elephants and horses, rubies bought for lakhs and brought home: hereafter, in the Lord's court, (none of it) is of use; the proud man departs and leaves (it all) behind. Why should the mind be set on anything but the One? Rising, sitting, sleeping and waking, let us meditate on the Lord for ever and ever. One may win marvellous, splendid contests in the arena and win the fights on the battlefield, and brag with his mouth like this: I kill, I bind, I let go; (yet when) the Hukam of the Supreme Lord came, he left (it all) one day and was gone. One may perform religious rites and duties in many ways, yet not know the Creator; he preaches but does not practise it himself, and does not recognise the Shabad, the essence; naked he came and naked he will go, like an elephant that (bathes and then) scatters dust over itself. Listen, Sants, good people, all my friends: this expanse is false (it perishes). Crying mine, mine, the fools have drowned; they have wasted away and died. O Nanak, (whoever) has met the Guru and meditated on the Naam has been carried across through the True Name. ॥4॥
380.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The whole world lies asleep in delusion, blinded by its worldly affairs; only some servant of the Lord stays awake. It is engrossed in the great enchantress (Maya), her love dearer to it than life; some rare one renounces her. The peerless lotus feet of the Lord, the mantra of the Sants: to these some Saadh holds fast. O Nanak, in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) they awake, dyed in divine knowledge; this is (the Lord's) grace on the most fortunate. ॥4॥
380.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) whatever pleases you is accepted (by your servants); that alone is peace and Sahaj in (their) minds. (You are) the Cause of creation, all-powerful, infinite; O brother, there is no other (like God). Your servants sing your praises, relishing them again and again. What you yourself do and have (others) do is your servant's counsel, resolve and wisdom. Your Naam is Amrit, O Beloved; in the Saadh Sangat (your servants) have found its taste. Those servants alone are filled to contentment and made whole who have sung of the Lord, the treasure of peace. O Master, one who leans on you has no anxiety. Those on whom your mercy has fallen are worthy bankers, rich in good fortune. From the moment (one) has had the sight (of God), doubt, attachment and deceit have all gone out (of him); O Nanak, he has made the True Naam the stuff of his daily life, and is merged in love of the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
380.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The slanderer) washes off the grime others gathered birth after birth, but reaps what he himself has done. Here he has no peace, in the Lord's court no shelter; he goes to the city of Jam and burns there. The slanderer has squandered his precious life. In nothing can he reach (his aim), and hereafter he finds no place. The hapless slanderer's own past deeds have come upon him; what can the poor man do? He is brought to ruin where no one shields him; to whom can he cry for help? Nowhere is there release for the slanderer; so it has pleased the Master. As each one slanders the Sants, so the Sants find comfort in it. The Sants lean on you, O Master; you are the Sants' helper. Says Nanak, the Lord has kept the Sants safe and swept the slanderers away. ॥4॥
381.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One who) washes the outside while the mind within stays filthy has lost both his places (this world and the next). Here he is gripped by lust, anger and attachment; hereafter he sobs and weeps. The understanding that worships Govind is of another kind. Beating its hole does not kill the snake; the deaf one does not hear the Naam. (One) gives up and throws away the labour of earning a living, yet does not know the worth of devotion; he takes to arguing over the Vedas and Shastras, but does not recognise the essence, union (with God). As a false coin is laid bare when it comes under the eye of the money-testers, (so) the Knower of hearts knows everything; what can be hidden from him? Cheated in falsehood and fraud, the (mortal) whose days are few perishes in an instant. Nanak has spoken the truth, the truth, the truth: keep (God) in your own heart and see. ॥4॥
381.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). As he strives, (the servant's) mind grows pure; he dances by casting out his self-conceit. He seizes the five (passions) and keeps them under control, and (keeps) Ekankar, the One Creator, in his mind. (O God,) your servant dances (thus): he sings (your) praises, and plays the unstruck Shabad as his rebab, pakhavaj, cymbals and ankle-bells. First he awakens his own mind, and then he delights others. He repeats the Name of Ram in his heart, and with his mouth recites it to all. With his hands he washes the feet of the Saadhs, and puts the dust of the Sants on his body. He offers up his mind and body, laying them before the Guru, and obtains the true treasure. Whoever hears and beholds (this dance) with faith is rid of the pain of birth and death. Such a dance wards off hell; O Nanak, (by it) the Gurmukh awakens. ॥4॥
The rebab is a stringed instrument, the pakhavaj a two-headed drum, the taal a pair of cymbals; those who danced in worship danced to them.
381.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The mind's bent, once) a lowly Chandal woman, has become a Brahmin woman; from a Shudra woman she has risen to the highest, O brother. The flame (of craving), left empty though (it took in) the underworlds and the skies, is quenched and spent, O brother. The cat of the house (the mind's greed) has learnt another lesson; seeing the mouse (of worldly things), she takes fright, O brother. The Guru has put the lion (of pride) in the power of the goat (of humility), and set the dog (of the senses) to (eating) grass, O brother. With no props the thatch is held up; the homeless (wandering mind) has gained a home, O brother. With no setter the jewelled ornament has been set, and a wondrous gem fixed in it, O brother. The complainant could never reach justice; once silent, he has received the verdict, O brother. She who sat in state upon the carpet (in pride) now seems as one dead; the glaring of eyes (at others) has fled, O brother. Ignorant is he who says, I know; one who (truly) knows does not stay hidden, O brother. Says Nanak, one whom the Guru has given the Amrit (of the Naam) to drink blossoms, relishing it again and again, O brother. ॥4॥

This shabad speaks in paradoxes; the commentators read each image as the changed state of a mind the Guru has given the Amrit of the Naam to drink (the last line). Chandal: a caste held to be lower even than the Shudra.
382.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Cutting (their) bonds, (God) has forgotten (their) faults; he has kept to his age-old way. Like a mother and father he has been merciful, and has cherished (them) as his children. The great Gopal has kept the Guru's Sikhs safe; looking on (them) with his gracious eye, he has drawn (them) out of the vast ocean of the world. He by whose Simran one is freed from Jam, and finds peace in this world and the next: with every breath and every morsel repeat (his Name) with your tongue; let his praises be sung day after day. Through loving devotion (they) have attained the supreme state; in the Saadh Sangat (their) sorrows have fled. Nothing wears away or is lost, and no fear takes hold: the pure wealth of the Lord is tied in (their) knot. At the last moment God has been (their) help; here and hereafter he is the protector. (God is) my life, my friend, my well-wisher and my wealth; Nanak is for ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥4॥
382.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When you are (my) Master, what fear can there be? Whom but you should I praise? If you alone are (mine), I have everything; for me there is no other but you. O Father (God), I have seen the world to be poison. Protect (me), my Lord of the world; your Naam is my support. You know all the pain of the mind; to whom else should it be told? Without the Name the whole world has gone mad; when the Naam is found, peace is found. What is there to say, and to whom should it be told? Whatever is to be said is (to be said) to God. All that comes to pass is your doing; for ever and ever my hope is in you. If you grant (me) greatness, that greatness is yours; here and hereafter I meditate on you alone. O God of Nanak, ever the Giver of peace, my strength is your Name alone. ॥4॥
382.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Your Naam is Amrit, O Master; this supreme essence (your) servant has drunk. The fears and burdens of birth after birth are ended; sin is destroyed, and the doubt of duality (is gone). Beholding the sight of you, I have come alive; hearing your words, O True Guru, my mind and body have grown cool and calm. By your grace (I) came to the Saadh Sangat; this work you yourself have done. I have clasped your feet firmly, O God; with ease the poison (of Maya) has withered away. Your Naam, O God, is the treasure of peace; this imperishable mantra I have received; the True Guru in his grace gave it to me; my fever, my anguish and my enmity are gone. Blessed is the human body (I) have been given, through which God has united (me) with himself. Blessed is that Kalyug (too), if Kirtan is sung in the Saadh Sangat and, O Nanak, the Naam is the heart's support. ॥4॥
383.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Everything has come about from the very first (by his will); what other knowledge can anyone have? For all (its) slips and failings, the Supreme Lord God has forgiven his own child. My True Guru is merciful for ever; he has kept me, poor and lowly, safe. The sickness is cut away and I have found supreme peace; (the Guru) has put the Lord's Amrit Naam in my mouth. (The Guru) has cast away my countless sins; my bonds are cut, and I am free. Seizing (my) arm, the Guru has lifted (me) out of the blind well, deep and dreadful. I have become fearless, all fear is erased; the Protector has protected (me). Such is your gift, my God, that all (my) affairs are set right. In my mind I have met the Master, the treasure of virtues; Nanak has sought (his) refuge and is at ease. ॥4॥
383.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When I forget you, everyone turns against me; when you come to mind, (all) serve me. No other, no second, do I see, O True One, unseen and unfathomable. When (he) comes to mind, he is ever merciful; what can poor people do? Tell me, whom should one call bad, and whom good? All beings are yours. Yours is my support, yours my mainstay; giving (your) hand, you protect (me). No one speaks an ill word to the person on whom your grace rests. That alone is peace, that alone is greatness, which pleases God's mind. You are wise, you are ever kind; if I am given the Naam, I revel in joy. Before you is my prayer: soul and body, all is yours. Says Nanak, all greatness is yours; no one even knows my name. ॥4॥
383.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Show mercy, O God, Knower of hearts; in the Saadh Sangat the Lord is found. Opening the doors, he shows the sight of himself, and one does not come into birth again. May I meet my beloved Master and be rid of all my sorrows, O brother; in the company of one who has worshipped the Supreme Lord in the heart, may I swim across, O brother. (The world) has become a great wilderness, an ocean of fire, where one dwells amid joy and grief; meeting the True Guru, the mind has become pure, repeating with the tongue the Lord's Amrit (Name). (Man) has set up body and wealth, all of it, as his own, and is bound in soft bonds (of attachment); by the Guru's grace those servants are set free who have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har. God the Protector has saved those who are pleasing to their God. Soul and body, all is yours, O Giver; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥4॥
383.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). You have broken free of the foul sleep of attachment, O friend; what grace has come upon you? The great enchantress (Maya) has no hold on you; where has your sloth gone, O friend? Lust, anger and pride are hard to master; by what discipline have you escaped them, O friend? (They) have plundered good men, gods, demons, the beings of the three qualities, the whole world, O friend. Fire in the forest has burnt up much of the grass; only some rare green plant is left, O friend. I cannot describe one so mighty; no words can tell that one's worth, O friend. (She answers:) In a room of lamp-black I was not blackened; my colour has stayed spotless, O friend. The Guru's great mantra has come to dwell in (my) heart; I have heard the wondrous Naam, O friend. God in his mercy cast (his) gracious glance and joined (me) to his feet. Through loving devotion, O Nanak, (I) have found peace, and am absorbed in the company of the Saadh. ॥4॥
384.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The red gown looks lovely on your body, (O friend); you have pleased the Beloved, and so you have won (his) heart. How did this glow of yours come about, O friend? With what dye have you turned so rosy red? You alone are beautiful; yours alone is the married bliss; in your house is the Beloved, in your house is good fortune. You are pure in conduct, you are foremost; you have pleased the Beloved, you alone have lofty wisdom. (She answers:) I pleased the Beloved, and so (I am dyed) in the deep red (of his love); says Nanak, (he) has looked on (me) with a kindly eye. Listen, my friend: this is all my labour: God, who adorns and makes beautiful, has himself adorned (me). ॥1॥
384.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When I was far (from him), the pain was great; now, by (the Guru's) counsel, I have been brought into his presence. My complaining is over, my friends and companions; my doubt is gone; the Guru has united me with my Husband Lord. Bringing (me) near, (he) has placed (me) on the Beloved's bed; I am freed from bowing in deference (to others). Through the Shabad there is light in the mansion (of my heart); my Master is full of bliss and play. Good fortune is on my forehead: my Husband has come home; servant Nanak has gained a wedded bliss that endures. ॥4॥
384.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My mind is joined to the Name of the True One; with people, my dealings go only as far as need requires. Outwardly I am on easy terms with all, and glad with them, yet I stay untouched, as the lotus does in the water. With my mouth I talk with everyone, but my God I hold close to my heart. (To others my mind) seems very hard and cold, (yet) this mind (of mine) is the dust of everyone's feet. Servant Nanak has found the Perfect Guru, (who) has shown (me) the One (Lord), within and without. ॥4॥
385.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Strong in his youth, (a man) revels in pleasures; (but) without the Name he mingles with the dust. He wears rings in his ears and fine clothes on his body, (sleeps on) a soft bed, and is proud in his mind. Elephants beneath him, a golden canopy over his head; (yet) without devotion to the Lord, he is taken and buried in the earth. (There may be) many women of beautiful form, (but) without the Lord's sweet essence all tastes are insipid. Maya is a deceiver, and the vices are poison; O God, merciful Being, Nanak has come to your refuge. ॥4॥
385.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). There is a garden, in which very many trees have been planted; in it the Amrit of the Naam has come to fruit. O wise one, reflect in such a way that the state beyond all desire may be reached. All around are pools of poison, (but) in the middle is the Amrit, O brother. The one who waters it is the one Gardener alone; he looks after every leaf and every branch. He has brought every kind of plant and set it (in this garden); all of it has flowered; not one is without fruit. The one who has received from the Guru the Amrit fruit, the Naam: O servant Nanak, he has crossed over (the ocean of) Maya. ॥4॥
In this shabad the garden is the world, its trees and plants are living beings, and the Gardener is the Creator; the pools of poison are Maya's vices, and the Amrit is the Naam.
385.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) your Name has made (for me) the delights of a kingdom; as I sing your Kirtan, yoga too is attained. In your shelter every comfort has come about; the True Guru has drawn back the curtains of doubt. Understanding (your) Hukam, I enjoy every joy and delight; through the True Guru's service (I) have become wholly free of desire. One who has known you is approved, whether householder or renunciant; the one dyed in the Naam is the one free of desire. The one who has received the treasure of the Naam: says Nanak, that one's treasury is full. ॥4॥
385.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). If I go to a place of pilgrimage, (I find people) crying I, I; if I ask the pandits, they are steeped in Maya. O friend, tell me of that place where the Lord's Kirtan, Har Har, goes on day after day. The Shastras and the Vedas (teach) the reckoning of sin and merit, (by which) one is born again and again in hell and in heaven. In the householder's life there is anxiety, in renunciation there is pride; doing rituals, the soul is caught in entanglements. (The one whose) mind has come under control by God's grace: O Nanak, through the Guru that one has crossed over (the ocean of) Maya. In the Saadh Sangat let us sing the Kirtan of the Lord; this place is found through the Guru. ॥7॥
385.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). There is peace at home, and peace outside too; remembering the Lord, all sorrows are destroyed. (O Lord,) when you come into the mind, there is every comfort; (but) only the one who pleases you repeats the Naam. Repeating your Name, body and mind are cooled and calmed; repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, the camp of sorrow is torn down. Only one who understands (God's) Hukam is approved, one who bears the True Shabad as his seal of passage. The Perfect Guru has made the Name of the Lord firm (within me); says Nanak, my mind has found peace. ॥4॥
386.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) where you send me, there I go; what you give me, in that I find my comfort. O Govind, Lord of the world (Gosain), I am your servant for ever; by your grace I am filled and content. What you have given, that I wear and eat; by your grace, O God, I spend (my days) in comfort. Within my mind and body I meditate on you alone; I set no one beside you as your equal. Says Nanak: (grant that) I may meditate (on you) thus for ever, (and) attain the highest state, falling at the feet of the Sants. ॥4॥
386.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Rising, sitting and sleeping, let us meditate (on the Lord); walking on the road, let us sing of the Lord, Har Har. With the ears, let us listen to the Amrit account (of the Lord's praises), hearing which there is bliss in the mind, (and) all the sorrows and sicknesses of the mind are lifted away. In every task and every work, on the road and at the river crossing, let us repeat (his Name); by the Guru's grace, let us drink the Lord's Amrit (of the Name). Day and night let us sing the Kirtan of the Lord; (the one who sings it,) that person is not set on the road of Jam. (O Lord,) the one who does not forget you at any hour: O Nanak, falling at that one's feet, the highest state is attained. ॥4॥
386.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (Remember the Lord,) through whose remembrance peace comes to dwell (in the mind); there is well-being, and sorrows are destroyed. Live in bliss; sing the praises of God; for ever and ever win the favour of your True Guru. Live by the True Guru's true Shabad; (so,) steady and seated in your own home (within), you will find your God. Do not hold ill will for another in your mind; (then) no sorrow (will come) to you, O brother, O friend. The Guru has given the Lord, Har Har, as the charm and the mantra; O Nanak, (the one who received it) has come to know this peace, night and day. ॥4॥
Tantra and mantra (tantu, mantu): charms and spells by which people sought to harm others or gain their ends; the charm and the mantra the Guru gives is the Name of the Lord.
386.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The lowly one, whom no one even knows, is honoured in the four directions by repeating the Naam. I beg for the sight of you: grant it, O Beloved; whom has your service not carried across? The one whom no one would come near: the whole creation rubs and washes that one's feet. The mortal who was of use to no one: by the grace of the Sant (the Guru), that one's name is (now) repeated (by all). In the Saadh Sangat the mind that slept wakes up; then, O Nanak, God seems sweet. ॥4॥
386.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). With my eyes I behold the One, the One alone, (and) ever and ever keep the Name of the Lord treasured (in my heart). I sing the praises of Ram, of Ram the beautiful; by the power of the Sant (the Guru), in the Saadh's company, I meditate, O brother, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. The One on whose thread all creation is strung: he alone pervades every heart. In an instant he brings about the creation and the dissolution (of the world), (yet) himself stays untouched, beyond (Maya's three) qualities. He does and causes all to be done; he is the knower of hearts; Nanak's Master delights in bliss. ॥4॥
387.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The wanderings of millions of births have ended; (the game of) this human body, so hard to come by, is won, not lost. Sins are wiped out, sorrow and pain are far away; by the dust of the Sants' feet (they) have become pure. God's Sants have the power to save; (but) they meet only the one for whom such union was written from the very start. The Guru has given the mantra (of the Name), and there is bliss in the mind; craving is quenched, and the mind has become steady. The Name, that precious thing, is the nine treasures and the siddhis; O Nanak, (this) understanding is received from the Guru. ॥4॥
387.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Thirst (for Maya) and the darkness of ignorance are gone; serving the Saadh (the Guru), a host of sins has been cut away. There is peace, Sahaj, and abundant bliss; through the Guru's service, minds have become pure, hearing the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Har Har. The folly and the stubbornness of the mind are destroyed; God's will has come to seem sweet. The feet of the Perfect Guru were grasped, (and) the sins of millions of births were washed away. This life, a jewel, has borne its fruit; says Nanak, God has shown mercy. ॥4॥
387.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Keep your True Guru treasured (in the heart), ever and always; dust the Guru's feet with (your) hair. Wake up, O mind, you who can wake! Without the Lord nothing else will be of use (to you); attachment is false, (the world's) spread is perishable. Fall in love with the Guru's Bani; (when) the Guru is merciful, sorrow goes. Apart from the Guru there is no other resting place; the Guru is the Giver, and it is the Guru who gives the Name. The Guru is himself the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; at all hours, O Nanak, meditate on the Guru. ॥4॥

347.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 1, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji): So Dar.
What is that gate of yours like, and what is that home like, where (you) sit and take care of all?
The sounds of your countless instruments of many kinds play there, and so many are the musicians who play for you.
So many of your ragas, with their raginis, are sung there, and so many are your singers.
Wind, water and fire sing of you; Dharam Raj (the judge of souls) sings of you at your door.
Chitr and Gupt, who know how to write, sing of you; what they write, Dharam Raj weighs and judges.
Shiva, Brahma and the goddesses sing of you, ever beautiful, adorned by you.
The Indras, seated on their thrones, sing of you with the gods at your door.
The Siddhas sing of you in samadhi (deep meditative absorption); the sadhus sing of you in contemplation.
The celibates, the charitable and the contented sing of you; the mighty heroes sing of you.
The learned pandits and the great rishis sing of you, age after age, along with the Vedas.
The enchanting women who charm the mind sing of you, in heaven, in the mortal world and in the netherworld.
All the jewels you have created sing of you, along with the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.
Warriors of great might and heroes sing of you; the four sources of life sing of you.
The regions, the worlds and the universes, made and set in place by you, sing of you.
They alone sing of you who please you, your devotees, steeped (in your love) and full of delight.
So many others sing of you who do not come to my mind; what can Nanak consider?
He, he alone, is ever true; the Master is true, and true is his glory.
He is, and he will be; he does not depart, nor will he depart, he who made the creation.
He who brought forth Maya of many colours, many kinds and many species
watches over what he has made, having made it, as befits his greatness.
Whatever pleases him, that he will do; no command can then be given (to him).
He is the King, the Emperor over kings; O Nanak, (our part is) to live in his will. ॥1॥
348.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).

That Purakh, the Being who pervades all, is Niranjan, free of the stain of Maya (the world's illusion and lure); the Lord, the all-pervading Being, is free of that stain; the Lord is beyond reach, wholly beyond reach, without limit.
O Lord, the eternal Creator, all meditate on you, all meditate on you.
All beings are yours, Lord; you are the Giver to every being.
Meditate on the Lord, revered Sants (saints): he makes all sorrows pass away.
The Lord himself is the Master, and the Lord himself the servant; O Nanak, what is a poor creature (by itself)?
You are within every heart, and in all without any gap; O Lord, you, the one Being, pervade all.
Some are givers and some are beggars; all these are your wondrous plays.
You are the giver yourself, and yourself the one who enjoys (the gifts); apart from you I know no other.
You are the Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), endless, endless; which of your virtues shall I name and describe?
Those who serve you, those who serve you, Lord: your servant Nanak is a sacrifice to them.
O Lord, those who meditate on you, who meditate on you, live at peace in the world.
Liberated, liberated are those who have meditated on the Lord; the noose of Jam has snapped for them.
Those who have meditated on the Fearless, on the Fearless Lord: he takes away all their fear.
Those who have served, who have served my Lord, merge into the very form of the Lord, Har Har.
Blessed, blessed are those who have meditated on the Lord; your servant Nanak gives himself in sacrifice to them.
The storehouses of devotion to you, of devotion to you, Lord, are full beyond end, beyond all end.
Your devotees, your devotees praise you, O Lord, many, countless, without end.
Many, so many, worship you, O Lord; numberless (beings) practise austerities and repeat (your Name).
Many, so many of yours read the many Simritis and Shastras, and carry out the rites and the six duties.
O servant Nanak, those devotees, those devotees alone are good who please my Lord God.
You are the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the Creator, Lord; no other is as great as you.
In every age you are the One; always, always you are the One; you are the unmoving Creator, ever the same.
O Lord, whatever pleases you yourself, that alone comes about; whatever you yourself do, that takes place.
You yourself brought forth the whole creation, and you yourself, having made it, have destroyed it all.
Servant Nanak sings the virtues of the Creator, who knows each and every one. ॥5॥
348.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Everyone calls you great, (O God,) having heard (it from others),
but how great you are is (told) only on seeing you.
Your worth cannot be fixed, nor can you be put into words.
Those who speak of you stay merged in you.
O my great Master, deep and profound, fathomless in virtues,
no one knows how much, how vast, your expanse is.
All who practise surat (attention fixed on God) joined together and practised it;
all who weigh worth joined together and weighed (yours);
yet by the men of knowledge, the men of meditation, the teachers and the teachers of teachers,
not even a sesame seed's worth of your greatness could be told.
All truthfulness, all austerities, all good deeds,
and the great powers of the Siddhas, the accomplished ones:
without you, no one has attained this siddhi (accomplishment).
It comes by (your) grace, and then no one can hold it back.
What can the poor speaker (say)?
Your storehouses are filled with praises.
The one to whom you give (your praise), what can anyone do against him?
O Nanak, the True One (himself) is the one who adorns (him). ॥4॥
349.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
When I utter (his Name), I live; when it is forgotten, I die.
The True Name is hard to utter.
If hunger for the True Name arises,
then, eating (of the Name) in that hunger, the sorrows are driven away.
Why should he be forgotten, O my mother?
The Master is true, and (is found) through the True Name.
Of the True Name's greatness, even a sesame seed's worth,
they have grown weary telling, yet none has found its worth.
If all were to join together and set about describing him,
he does not become greater, nor does he become less.
He does not die, nor is there mourning (for him).
He keeps on giving, and what he gives to be enjoyed never runs out.
This is his quality: there is no other (like him);
none has been, and none will be.
As great as you yourself are, so great is your gift,
(you,) who made the day and made the night.
Those who forget the Master are low-born;
O Nanak, those without the Name are the outcastes. ॥4॥
349.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If a beggar at the door cries out, the Master within the mansion hears (his cry);
whether he gives him comfort or pushes him away, it is honour he gives him all the same.
Recognise the light (of God in all), and do not ask anyone's caste; hereafter there is no caste.
(God) himself makes (beings) act, and himself acts,
and himself takes to heart (their) grievances.
(O God,) when you, the Creator, are the doer of all,
what dependence on anyone is there, and what is the world?
(God) himself creates (beings), and himself gives (to them);
he himself holds them back from evil-mindedness.
By the Guru's grace, (in whose) mind (God) comes to dwell,
from within (that one) pain and darkness depart.
(God) himself makes the Truth dear (to a being);
to others (he) does not give the Truth.
Says Nanak: if (he) gives (it) to anyone, he calls (that one) to no account hereafter. ॥4॥
349.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The workings of the mind are the cymbals and the ankle-bells;
the (love of the) world is the drum: these are the instruments that play.
The mind, a Narad, dances: this is the sway of Kalyug;
where can the celibate and the virtuous set their feet?
O Nanak, be a sacrifice to the Name.
The world is blind; the Master (alone) knows all.
The disciple, on the contrary, eats from the guru;
for love of bread he comes to live in (the guru's) house.
Even if (one were given) a hundred years of living and eating,
only that day is approved on which (one) recognises the Master.
No compassion stirs at the sight of (one in need);
no one does without give and take.
The king does justice (only) if (something) comes into (his) hand;
if one appeals in God's name, no one heeds.
Says Nanak: in form and in name one is human,
but in deeds a dog that obeys orders at (its master's) door (for scraps).
If by the Guru's grace (one) knows (oneself) a guest (here),
then (one) gains some honour in the Lord's court. ॥4॥
350.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O God,) all the speaking and hearing there is, is your own current of life; all the form there is, is your body.
You yourself are the one who tastes, you yourself the life that dwells (in all); O mother, I can speak of no other, no second.
he is One, brother, he alone is One.
(He) himself kills and himself sets free; himself he takes and gives.
(He) himself watches over (all), himself delights, himself casts his glance of grace.
Whatever is to be done, (he) himself is doing; nothing else can be done.
As (he) acts, so is (he) named; (O God,) all this is your greatness.
Kalyug is the woman who sells wine, Maya the sweet wine, and the drunken mind keeps on drinking.
(God) himself makes forms of many kinds; this is what poor Nanak says. ॥4॥
350.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Let wisdom be the instrument, and love the drum (the pakhavaj);
(then) bliss arises, and the mind is ever full of zest.
This is devotion, this the practice of austerity;
Dance in this joy, setting your feet down with care.
One who knows (how to sing God's) praise keeps the full beat;
any other dancing is only the pleasures and the whims of the mind.
Let truth and contentment be the two cymbals that play;
let being ever in bloom be the bells upon the feet;
let having no love for another be the raag and its music;
Dance in this joy, setting your feet down with care.
Let the fear (of God), held in heart and mind, be the whirling turn,
whether sitting or rising, always and ever;
let knowing the body to be ashes be the rolling on the ground;
Dance in this joy, setting your feet down with care.
Let there be love for the teaching in the gathering of the Sikhs,
hearing the True Name through the Guru,
and, O Nanak, uttering it again and again;
Dance in this joy, setting your feet down with care. ॥4॥
350.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord, you) brought forth the air and set the whole earth in place, and bound water and fire together.
Blind (in his folly), the ten-headed (Ravan) had his own head cut off; did killing Ravan make (you) any greater?
What praise of you can be spoken?
You fill all, pervading every one.
Creating the beings, you hold the way (of their lives) in your hand; did putting a nose-rope on Kali (the serpent) make (you) any greater?
Whose husband are you, and whom is one to call your wife? You pervade all, with no gap between.
Brahma, the giver of boons, went with his family into the (lotus) stalk to search out (the source of) creation;
going on, he found no end to it. Did slaying Kans make (you) any greater?
(You) brought forth the jewels; the ocean of milk was churned, and the others (gods and demons) cried out in anger: We did this.
Says Nanak, how can the hidden (Lord) stay hidden? (It was he who) shared out (the jewels) one by one. ॥4॥
351.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Deeds and conduct grew into a spreading vine, and its fruit was the Name of the Lord (Ram).
It has no form or outline; the Shabad that the Pure Lord made sounds (within), unstruck.
If anyone comes to know (the Lord) and tells (of him),
Those who drank it became rapt with joy; their bonds and nooses broke.
Within (them), (their) light merged in the Light; then they gave up (chasing) the gains of Maya.
(O Lord, they) saw your form in every light, and your Maya in all the worlds.
In this (world), a form of strife, (the Lord) sits apart, unattached, and, present within (all) as his own reflection, keeps watch (over all).
(Such a) yogi plays the vina of the Shabad, (rapt) in the sight of the Infinite One's form;
through the unstruck Shabad he is dyed in the Husband Lord: this is the reflection Nanak speaks. ॥4॥
351.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) my virtues (are only these): loads of talk upon my head.
Of all talk, the (worthy) talk is (talk of) the Creator.
Eating, drinking, laughing are (all) in vain
as long as you do not come to mind in the heart.
Then what care is left (for anyone), and what (more) is there to do,
if, born into this (human) life, one takes what is worth the taking?
The mind's thinking is (that of) a maddened, drunken elephant;
(so) whatever we say is all error upon error.
With what face can we make a prayer (to you)
when sin and virtue both stand by (us) as witnesses?
As you make anyone, so does he become;
apart from you there is no second.
Such understanding as you give, such does one receive;
as it pleases you yourself, so you make (the world) go.
The jewel-like raags, their consorts (the raginis) and (all) their family:
within it (all) springs the sublime Amrit.
O Nanak, this is the Creator's own wealth and riches,
if anyone grasps this thought. ॥4॥
351.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In his grace (the Husband Lord) came to his own home; then (my) companions gathered and set about the wedding.
Seeing this play, (my) mind was filled with bliss: the Husband has come to wed (me).
Sing, sing, O women, (songs of) discerning reflection;
into our home has come the Husband, the Life of the world.
Our wedding took place at the Guru's door; when the Husband met (me), then I knew
that (his) Shabad pervades the three worlds; (my) self-conceit went, and (my) mind was won over.
(The Lord) himself brings his own work to completion; by no one else can it be done.
This work, in which are truth, contentment, compassion and dharma, some rare one grasps through the Guru.
Says Nanak, he alone is the Husband of all;
she on whom he looks with grace becomes the happy wife. ॥4॥
351.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(For one who has subdued the mind) home and forest are alike; (he abides) in Sahaj and in love.
(His) evil thinking is gone, and in its place is (the Lord's) praise.
(His) ladder of truth is the True Name on (his) lips;
serving the True Guru, he finds his own true home.
One who crushes the mind: know him (to have mastered) the six darshanas (the six schools of philosophy);
(he sees) in all the light of the Lord God, perfect and whole.
(One with) great thirst (for Maya) puts on many guises;
the pain that Maya's poison brings drives peace from (his) body;
lust and anger steal the wealth within.
Leaving double-mindedness, (one) crosses over through the Name.
(One who has won the mind) sings (the Lord's) praise and (knows) the bliss of Sahaj;
the love of Gobind is (his) friend and kin.
(He knows that the Lord) himself acts, and himself is the Forgiver;
body, mind and life (he keeps) with the Lord, laid before him.
Falsehood and vices (bring) great suffering to the body;
guises and castes all look (to him) like dust.
Whatever is born comes and goes;
O Nanak, only the Name and (his) Will are everlasting. ॥4॥
352.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
There is one lake, and in it lotuses beyond compare;
(the lake) keeps them ever in bloom, fragrant and fair.
(There) swans peck at bright pearls,
(and remain) a part of the Lord of the world, the Master of every power.
Whatever is seen springs up and perishes;
(but) the lotus in the lake is never seen without water.
Only a rare one understands and finds (this) secret;
the Veda speaks always of the three branches (of Maya).
(One whose) attention merges in the understanding of the Shabad
attains the supreme state, serving the True Guru.
He is free, steeped (in the Lord), remembering (him) in love;
(abiding) in the King of kings, he is ever in bloom.
(O Lord,) one whom you save in your mercy,
though a sinking stone, you carry across in your boat.
(He saw) the Light in the three worlds, and knew (the Lord) in the three worlds;
(his attention) turned back (from Maya), and he brought (the Lord's) home into (the) home (of his heart).
One who, with loving attention fixed, worships day and night:
Nanak falls at the feet of such ones. ॥4॥
352.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
With the Guru's true teaching, wrangling goes far away;
too much cleverness only gathers dirt.
The dirt that has clung is wiped away through the True Name;
by the Guru's grace one keeps loving attention fixed (on the Lord).
(The Lord) is present, right before (us); (make your) prayer (to him).
Pain and pleasure, know it as true, rest with God the Creator.
Whoever deals in falsehood keeps coming and going (in birth and death);
there is no end to (his) talking and telling.
What has he seen? He gains no insight, no understanding;
without the Name no contentment comes to (his) mind.
All who are born are gripped by (the) disease (of the soul);
they are tormented by the pain of Haumai and Maya.
Those alone escape whom God has kept safe;
serving the True Guru, they have tasted the savour of Amrit.
(One who) holds back the wandering mind and tastes the Amrit,
(who), serving the True Guru, utters the Amrit Shabad,
through the true Shabad attains liberation and the high state;
O Nanak, he casts out the self from within. ॥4॥
352.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One whom he has made (his own) has become (one with) the True;
to him the True Guru gave the Amrit Name.
The Name is in (his) heart, and (his) mind is never broken off (from the Lord);
night and day he is in the Beloved's company.
O dear Lord, keep (me) in your refuge.
By the Guru's grace (I) have found the Lord's savour; the Name, that precious thing, the nine treasures, has come to (me).
(One whose) deeds and dharma are the true Name of the True One:
to him I am ever a sacrifice.
Those steeped in the Lord are accepted (at his court);
their company is the supreme treasure.
The bride who has gained the Lord for her Husband is blessed;
dyed in the Lord, she reflects on the Shabad;
she herself crosses over, and carries (her) companions and family across;
serving the True Guru, she reflects on the essence.
The True Name is our caste and honour;
true love is (our) deeds, dharma and self-restraint.
O Nanak, no account is asked of one whom (the Lord) forgives;
that One alone wipes out (all sense of) a second. ॥4॥
353.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Some come (into the world) and, having come, go away (empty-handed);
some, steeped in the Lord, remain absorbed (in him);
some find no place to rest, neither on earth nor in the sky;
they are the luckless, who do not meditate on the Lord's Name.
From the Perfect Guru are found the high state and the (right) way of living.
The world is a sea of dread, full of poison; through the Guru's Shabad the Lord carries (us) across.
Those whom God himself joins (to himself),
death cannot crush.
Through the Guru those beloved ones stay pure,
as lotuses stand above the water, untouched by it.
Tell me, whom can we call bad or good?
God (Brahm) is seen (in all); through the Guru the True One is found.
Reflecting on the Guru's teaching, I tell of the Untellable;
joining the Guru's company, I reach the farther shore.
(Pondering) the many distinctions of the Shastras, the Vedas and the Simritis,
(and) bathing at the sixty-eight (tiraths): (all this is) the Lord's savour in the heart.
Through the Guru one stays pure; no filth clings (to him).
O Nanak, the Name (dwells) in the heart by great good fortune written from the start. ॥4॥
353.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Bowing low again and again, I fall at my Guru's feet; (by his grace) I have beheld within (me) the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram).
Reflecting (on his virtues), I have dwelt on the Lord in my heart; seeing (him) in my heart, I have pondered (him).
Utter (the Name of) Ram (the Lord); he brings deliverance.
By the Guru's grace one gains the Lord, the jewel; ignorance is wiped away, and light dawns.
(One who) only talks with the tongue: (his) bonds do not break; caught in Haumai, (his) wandering does not end.
When the True Guru is met, Haumai breaks; only then is one accepted in the (Lord's) reckoning.
(One who holds to) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and devotion to the Beloved, and enshrines in the heart the Dear One, the Ocean of peace:
him the Lord, Lover of devotion, the Life of the world, the Giver, carries across, (granting him) the wisdom of the Guru's teaching.
One who fights his mind and dies (to self) finds God, and stills the mind's desire within the mind itself.
O Nanak, (one on whom) the Life of the world shows mercy keeps (his) loving attention fixed (on him) in Sahaj. ॥4॥
353.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who have come to understand: to whom do they speak, to whom do they recite, whom do they instruct?
Whom do they teach? Having read and reflected, they have understood, and through the True Guru's Shabad they live in contentment.
Through the Guru's teaching, such a Lord, pervading every body,
so deep and profound: worship him, O my mind.
(Within them rise) endless waves of devotion to the Lord and of his love;
keeping company with the Lord's virtues, they are pure night and day.
The worldly Saakat's birth is wasted;
the servant devoted to the Lord stays detached (from the world).
Pure is the body of one who has sung the Lord's virtues;
recognising his own self, he keeps his mind fixed (on the Lord).
(The Lord) is the Primal One, infinite, beyond the farthest beyond, a diamond;
dyed in that ruby (the Lord), my mind has grown steady.
Those who only talk, talking on and on, are dead (within).
That God is not far; O God, you are (near).
I have seen the whole world to be Maya's shadow;
Nanak has meditated on the Naam through the Guru's teaching. ॥4॥
354.1: Raag Asa, a Tituka, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One is a beggar who lives on alms;
another is a king, lost (in his kingship).
One receives honour, another dishonour;
another pulls down and builds up again, his mind fixed (on that).
(O Lord,) no one is greater than you;
whom could I point out as good?
For me, your Name is my only support;
you are the Giver, the One who can do all, the Creator.
I do not find the way; I go off on crooked paths;
(so) in the Lord's court there is no place for (me) to sit.
I am blind in mind, bound by Maya;
(my) body wastes away and decays every day.
(Yet) great is my hope of eating and living on;
(while) every breath and every morsel is counted in your reckoning.
Day and night (the Lord) gives the blind a lamp (of understanding),
and cares for the one drowning in the terrifying world-ocean.
Those who speak the Name, hear it and accept it:
to them I am a sacrifice.
Nanak makes one prayer:
soul and body, all is in your keeping.
When you give it, I repeat your Name,
and (I) find a place to sit in the Lord's court.
When it pleases you, the evil mind goes away,
and the jewel of divine knowledge comes and settles in the mind.
When (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, the True Guru is met;
Nanak humbly prays: (then the soul) swims across the world-ocean. ॥4॥
354.2: Raag Asa, Panchpade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
A cow without milk, a bird without wings, plants without water are of no use;
what is a sultan whom no one salutes? (O Lord,) dark is the chamber (of the heart) in which your Name is not.
(O Lord,) why do you slip from the mind? (Forgetting you) brings great pain.
Let (any other) pain befall, but may you not be forgotten.
(In old age) the eyes go blind, the tongue loses its taste, and no sound reaches the ears;
one walks on one's feet (only) when led by the hand from in front: such are the fruits that grow without (the Lord's) service.
Those who plant the Word as the trees of a garden in the clean soil (of the heart), and water them with love:
on all of them grows the one fruit, the Naam; but without (the Lord's) grace how can (anyone) obtain it?
As many beings as there are, all are yours; without serving (you) no one gains the fruit.
Pain and pleasure are as you will; apart from the Name, the soul cannot endure.
To die (to self) within (the Guru's) teaching is life; what other life is there? If I live (any other way), that is no way (to live).
Says Nanak: (the Lord) gives life to all beings; (O Lord,) keep (me) wherever it pleases you, you alone. ॥5॥
355.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(My) body is the Brahmin, and the mind his dhoti;
divine knowledge is the sacred thread, and meditation the ring of kusha grass.
The Lord's Name and his praise are the bath I beg for,
that by the Guru's grace I may stay merged in God.
O Pandit, reflect on God in this way:
in the Name is purity, the Name is what I study, and in the Name are right conduct and observance.
The outer sacred thread lasts only as long as the light (of life) is with (the body);
keep the Name in your heart: (that is) the dhoti and the frontal mark;
(the Name alone) stands by you here and hereafter.
Apart from the Name, do not go seeking other rites.
Love is the worship; burn away Maya completely;
see the One alone, and seek no other.
One who recognises the Essence in the sky of the Tenth Gate
and keeps the Lord on his lips reads the (true) scripture and reflects on it.
Love (of the Lord) is (his) food, (and by it) doubt and fear flee;
with the radiance of the Watchman (the Lord) within, no thief comes near.
To know the one God is the tilak on (his) forehead;
one who understands God has discernment within.
(God) cannot be won over by rituals;
reading scripture, no one finds (his) worth.
the eighteen (Puranas) and the four (Vedas) have not found (his) secret;
O Nanak, the True Guru has shown (me) God. ॥5॥
355.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
That person alone is a (true) servant, slave and devotee
who becomes Gurmukh and so the Master's slave.
He who fashioned the creation destroys it again;
apart from him there is no other at all.
Reflecting on the True Name through the Guru's Shabad,
the Gurmukhs are found true in the court of the True One.
True is (their) plea, true their prayer;
the Husband Lord in his mansion hears it and gives his approval.
He calls (such a one) to his true throne
and bestows honour; whatever he does comes to pass.
(O Lord, the Gurmukh's) strength is yours alone; you alone are (his) support;
the Guru's Shabad is (his) true seal of passage.
Whoever accepts the Hukam departs in honour;
bearing the true seal, (he) meets no barrier (on the way).
The pandits read the Veda and expound it,
but they do not know the secret: the real thing (the Name) is within.
Without the Guru there is no awareness, no understanding
that the True God pervades (all).
What can I say? What can I say and describe?
You yourself know, O Lord of all wonders.
O Nanak, the one door (of the Lord) is (the Gurmukh's) only support;
there the Gurmukh lives on the Truth. ॥5॥
355.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The body is an unbaked clay pot, full of misery; it is born, it perishes, and it suffers pain.
This world is an ocean hard to cross; how can it be crossed? Without the Lord and the Guru no one reaches the far shore.
Without you (I have) no other, my Beloved; without you there is no other, O Lord.
In all colours and all forms you alone are; (the Lord) forgives the one on whom he casts his glance of grace.
The wicked mother-in-law (Maya) does not let me dwell in the house (of my heart); the wicked one does not let me meet my Husband.
