I serve the feet of my companions and friends (in the holy company); by the Guru's grace the Lord has cast his glance of grace (on me).
Reflecting on myself and subduing my mind, I have found there is no friend like you.
As you keep me, so must I live; you give pain and pleasure, and what you do, that alone (comes to pass).
Hope and desire are both destroyed; (I) have become free of hope in the three qualities.
The fourth state is reached through the Guru; (I) have taken the shelter of the assembly of the Sants.
All divine knowledge and meditation, all chanting and austerity, are (gained by) the one in whose heart is the Lord, unseen and unfathomable.
O Nanak, the one whose mind is dyed in the Lord's Name gains, through the Guru's teaching, (his) service in Sahaj. ॥5॥
356.1: Raag Asa, Panchpade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Family is attachment; all worldly affairs are attachment;
give up attachment: (it) is all corruption.
Give up attachment and doubt, O brother,
(so that) the True Name may dwell in heart and body.
When the True Name, the nine treasures, is found,
(then) no son weeps and no mother grieves.
In this attachment the world is drowned;
only a rare one crosses over, through the Guru.
Caught in this attachment, you will fall into births again;
clinging to attachment, you will go to the city of Jam.
(People) take initiation from a guru and practise chanting and austerities,
(yet) their attachment does not break, nor are they accepted (in the Lord's court).
When (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, this attachment departs,
and, O Nanak, (the soul) stays merged in the Lord. ॥6॥
356.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The True One, unseen and infinite, himself does (all);
I am a sinner; you are the Forgiver.
acting by the stubbornness of the mind, one is ruined in the end.
The manmukh's intellect is caught up in falsehood;
without the Lord's Simran, it suffers for its sin.
Give up the evil mind and earn some profit;
whatever is born comes from the (Lord), unseen and unfathomable.
Such is our Friend and Helper:
the Guru, the Lord, has met (me) and made devotion firm (within).
In all (other) dealings there is loss;
the Lord's Name is what pleases Nanak's mind. ॥5॥
356.3: Raag Asa, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Learning is truly reflected upon only when one does good to others;
when the five (passions) are subdued, then one truly dwells at a place of pilgrimage.
The ankle-bells ring (to purpose) only if the mind is attuned (to the Lord);
then what can Jam do to me hereafter?
One free of all hope is a (true) sanyasi;
when one keeps a yogi's continence, then one is (truly) a householder.
One who has compassion and reflects on his own body is a (true) Digambar;
he dies (to self) himself, and kills no other.
(O Lord,) you are One; the other guises are many;
Nanak does not know your wonders. ॥4॥
356.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
It is not with one (fault) alone that I am filled, that I could wash it away with virtues;
my Husband stays awake, while I sleep the whole night through.
How, like this, can I become dear to my Husband?
The Husband stays awake, while I sleep the whole night through.
Full of hope and thirst, I come to his bed,
(but I do not know) whether, before him, I shall please the Husband or not.
O mother, how am I to know what will become (of me)?
Without the sight of the Lord I cannot bear to live.
I have not tasted (his) love, nor has my thirst been quenched;
that youth is gone, and (now) the bride regrets it.
Even now, may I wake, hoping and thirsting (to meet him);
turned away (from the world), may I live free of (worldly) hopes.
If (the bride) sheds her Haumai and so adorns herself,
then the Husband delights in her on the bed (of the heart).
Only then, O Nanak, is she pleasing to the Husband's mind,
(when,) giving up her own greatness, she merges in her Master. ॥26॥
357.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In her parents' home the bride was very naive;
I did not know the worth of that Husband.
One alone is my Husband; there is no second (like him).
When he casts his glance of grace, union (with him) comes about.
In her in-laws' home the bride recognised the True One;
in Sahaj and in love she came to know her Beloved.
When, by the Guru's grace, such understanding comes,
then the bride is pleasing to the Husband's mind.
Says Nanak: she who adorns herself with the fear (of God) and with love,
the Husband ever delights in her on the bed (of the heart). ॥4॥
357.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
No one is anyone's son, and no one anyone's mother;
(yet the world,) in false attachment and doubt, has gone astray.
O my Master, I am of your making;
when you give (it), I repeat your Name.
Someone full of faults may cry out (at his door);
when it pleases him, he alone forgives.
By the Guru's grace (my) evil-mindedness is gone;
wherever I look, there is that One alone.
Says Nanak: if such understanding comes,
then one merges in the True One alone. ॥4॥
357.3: Raag Asa, Dupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(Our) dwelling has come to be in that terrible lake whose water he himself has made fire.
In the mire of attachment the foot cannot move; before our eyes (many) have drowned there.
O mind, O foolish mind, you do not remember the One.
As you forget the Lord, your virtues have wasted away.
I am neither celibate (jati) nor virtuous (sati), nor am I learned; my life has turned out the life of a foolish, ignorant one.
Nanak humbly prays: (let me be) in the refuge of those who have not forgotten you. ॥2॥
357.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Six are the schools, six (their) teachers, and six (their) teachings;
but the Guru of these teachers is the One (God), whose guises are many.
The house (the school) in which the Creator is praised:
hold fast to that house; in it lies your greatness.
Visas, chasas, gharis, pahars, lunar days and weekdays (together) make up the month;
the sun is one and the seasons many;
(in the same way,) O Nanak, the Creator has so many guises. ॥2॥
358.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(Though you have) lakhs of troops, lakhs of drums and spears, and lakhs rise to salute (you),
(though) your command runs over lakhs, and lakhs rise to do you honour;
yet if (this) honour does not count in (the Lord's) reckoning, all these works are fruitless.
Without the Lord's Name the world is (mere) entanglement;
however much the fool is taught, he is still blind, wholly blind.
Lakhs may be earned, lakhs amassed and spent; lakhs may come and lakhs may go;
yet if (this) honour does not count in (the Lord's) reckoning, where then will beings find a place?
There may be lakhs of expositions of the Shastras, and lakhs of pandits reading the Puranas;
yet if (this) honour does not count in (the Lord's) reckoning, all of it is rejected.
Honour springs from the True Name, and the Creator's Name is received by (his) grace.
If (the Name) dwells in the heart day and night, then, O Nanak, by (his) glance of grace one reaches the far shore. ॥4॥
358.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The One Name is my lamp, and into it I have poured suffering as the oil;
its light has dried that (oil) up, and my meeting with Jam is ended.
O people, let no one take this for idle jest:
gather lakhs of heaps (of wood) together, and a speck of fire is (all it takes to burn them).
My pind and my leaf-plate are (the Name of) Keshav, and my kiria the True Name of the Creator;
here and there, hereafter and before, this is my support.
Your praise is (my) Ganga and Banaras, (in which my) soul bathes;
the true bathing comes only when love (for the Lord) holds fast day and night.
One (pind) for the gods, another for the forefathers: the Brahmin rolls the pind and eats (it himself);
O Nanak, the pind of (the Lord's) grace never runs out. ॥4॥
358.3: Raag Asa, Ghar 4, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
For the sight (of you) the gods have borne pain and hunger and made pilgrimages;
yogis and celibates, keeping to their disciplines, have put on the saffron garb.
For your sake, O Master, they are dyed in (your) love.
Your names are many, your forms without end; how many your virtues are cannot be told.
(Some) have left gates and homes, palaces, elephants and horses, and their native lands, and gone away;
pirs, prophets, saliks and sadiks (the steadfast in faith) have left the world to be accepted (at your door).
They gave up tastes, comfort and pleasures, and every savoury food; they left off clothes and took to skins;
sorrowing and aching (for you) at your door, dyed in your Name, they became dervishes.
(Some took) the leather pouch, the begging bowl, the staff and the deerskin; (some) the topknot, the sacred thread and the dhoti.
You are the Master, and I am your player in guises; Nanak humbly prays: what (pride) of caste (is mine)? ॥4॥
359.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 5, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Within, in the mind, the five (lust and the rest) dwell hidden;
they do not stay still, but roam about like homeless wanderers.
My mind does not stay steady with the Merciful One;
(it is) greedy, deceitful, sinful and false, and Maya has a strong hold on it.
(The bride says:) I will wear a garland of flowers round my neck as a necklace;
when my Beloved meets me, then I will adorn myself.
My friends are five, and (their) husband is one;
(they) cling to the tree (of the body), but the dear soul is bound to depart.
The five friends join together and wail;
Nanak humbly prays: the husband (the soul) is seized to give his account. ॥4॥
359.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 6, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If the mind becomes a pearl for her jewel, and the breath the thread that strings it;
if the bride wears forgiveness as the adornment of her body, then, made dear (to him), she delights in her Beloved.
O Beloved, (your) many virtues have charmed the bride;
virtues like yours are found in no other.
If she takes the Lord, Har Har, for a necklace and wears it at her throat, and takes Damodar for her dandasa (the bark that colours the teeth);
if she makes the Creator the bracelets she wears on her hands, and in this way holds her mind (on him);
if she wears Madhusudan as the ring on her hand, and takes the Supreme God for her silk;
if the bride has patience braided into her hair, and puts on Sri Rang as the kohl (of her eyes);
if she lights a lamp in the temple of the mind, and makes her body the bed;
then, when the King of wisdom comes to the bed, O Nanak, he takes his joy in her. ॥4॥
359.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The one who is created does as he is made to do; what complaint, brother, can be made of him?
Whatever (God) means to do, he is doing; what cleverness has the created?
(O God,) the one who pleases you finds your Hukam good;
O Nanak, it is he who receives greatness and merges in the True Name.
By the deeds done, the writ (of life) has been written; no order comes again (to undo it).
What was written is what unfolds; none can wipe it out.
If anyone talks too much in the (Lord's) court, he gets the name of a loose-tongued talker;
his game of satranj is not won, and his piece is left raw.
No one is wise for being a learned pandit, and no one bad for being a fool;
the one whom (God) keeps in submission (to his will) and moves to praise him: he alone is called a banda (his servant). ॥4॥
359.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Guru's Shabad in my mind is my earrings, and forgiveness the patched coat I wear;
whatever (the Lord) does, I accept as good; (so) I gain the treasure of the yoga of Sahaj.
O brother, the one whose soul is joined (to God) is a yogi through all the ages; his union is with the Supreme Essence.
He has found the Amrit Name of the Immaculate One, and within his body he enjoys the relish of (divine) wisdom.
Having given up imaginings and disputes, I sit on my seat in the city of Shiv (the Lord, the source of good);
the Shabad is my horn, its sound ever beautiful; day and night (my mind) sounds its note.
Reflection is my begging bowl, wise understanding my staff; (seeing the Lord) present everywhere is my ashes.
The Lord's praise is my discipline (of yoga); to live turned to the Guru is (my) path of the detached (Atit).
(Seeing) the light (of the Lord) in all, in its many kinds and countless colours, is my sammia (arm-rest).
Says Nanak: listen, Bharthari the yogi: (true yoga is) attention fixed on the one Supreme Lord. ॥4॥
360.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Make divine knowledge the molasses, meditation the dhava flowers, and good conduct the kikar bark to put in;
make the body the furnace and love the cooling cloth: from this wash the nectar is distilled.
O brother, the mind, intoxicated, drinks the essence of the Name and stays absorbed in the joy of Sahaj;
day and night it stays rapt in loving attention (to the Lord), and it has taken hold of the unstruck Shabad.
The Perfect One, in Sahaj, gives this true cup to drink to that one alone on whom he casts his glance of grace.
One who deals in Amrit: why would he set his love on worthless wine?
The Guru's teaching is the Amrit Bani; as soon as one drinks it, one is accepted.
One who loves the sight of (the Lord's) door: what would he do with liberation or paradise?
Dyed in (the Lord's) praise, he is ever detached, and does not lose his life in a gamble.
Says Nanak: listen, Bharthari the yogi: (such a one) is intoxicated with the stream of Amrit. ॥4॥
360.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The Creator) took Khurasan under his protection and struck terror into Hindustan;
the Creator takes no blame upon himself: he made the Mughal (Babur) into Jam and sent him to invade.
Such slaughter fell that (the people) cried out in anguish; did you feel no pain?
O Creator, you are the one who takes care of all.
If the strong strike the strong, the mind feels no grievance;
(but) if a mighty lion falls upon the herd and kills, its master is called to account.
The dogs have spoiled and ruined jewels (of people); no one takes any thought of the dead.
You yourself join and you yourself part; see, (this is) your greatness.
If someone gets himself a great name and enjoys whatever pleasures his mind fancies,
in the Master's eyes he is still an insect, however many grains he pecks.
Only if he dies (to himself) again and again and so lives, and utters the Name, O Nanak, does he gain anything. ॥3॥
360.3: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
By great good fortune one receives the darshan (sight) of the Lord,
through the Guru's Shabad and through true bairag (longing for the Lord).
The six darshans (schools of philosophy) hold sway (in the world),
but the Guru's darshan is beyond reach and boundless.
Through the Guru's darshan come liberation and the high state,
and the True One himself comes to dwell in the mind.
Through the Guru's darshan the world is saved,
if one gives (it) love and affection.
But rare is the one who gives such love and affection;
through the Guru's darshan there is lasting peace.
Through the Guru's darshan (is found) the door of liberation;
one who serves the True Guru becomes a support for his family.
The one without a Guru attains no high state at all;
robbed by their faults, such people suffer blows.
Through the Guru's Shabad there is peace and calm in the body;
through the Guru, no pain touches such a one.
Jamkaal comes nowhere near him;
O Nanak, the Gurmukh merges in the True One. ॥4॥
361.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who has died through the Shabad sheds self-conceit from within;
he serves the True Guru without a trace of greed.
The fearless Giver is ever in his mind.
Only by good fortune does anyone receive the True Bani.
Gather virtues, and the faults within will depart;
through the Shabad of the Perfect Guru you will merge (in the Lord).
One who is a buyer of virtues knows (the worth of) virtues;
through the Amrit Shabad he utters the Naam.
Through the True Bani he becomes pure;
through virtues the Naam is obtained.
Virtues are priceless; they cannot be obtained (for any price);
through the True Shabad they come to dwell in a pure mind.
Fortunate are those who have meditated on the Naam
and enshrined the Giver of virtues in their minds forever.
I am a sacrifice to those who gather virtues;
at the True One's door I sing the praises of the True One.
(The Lord) himself gives (this gift), and (the receiver abides) in Sahaj and in love.
O Nanak, the worth (of this gift) cannot be told. ॥4॥
361.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Great is the glory in the True Guru:
he unites in union (with the Lord) those long separated.
(The Lord) himself brings (them to the Guru) and, having brought them, unites (them with himself);
he himself assesses his own worth.
By what means can the Lord's worth be assessed?
The Lord is beyond the farthest beyond, beyond reach and beyond the senses; only a rare one meets him through the Guru's Shabad.
Rare is the one who, through the Guru, knows (his) worth;
few receive (this understanding), by his grace.
Through the lofty Bani one becomes lofty;
rare is the one who, through the Guru, utters (the Naam) by the Shabad.
Without the Name there is sorrow and pain in the body;
when the True Guru is met, then the pain is lifted.
Without meeting the Guru, one earns only sorrow;
the manmukh receives heavy punishment.
The Lord's Name is sweet, rich in relish;
(but only he) keeps drinking it whom he (the Lord) gives it to drink.
By the Guru's grace one obtains the Lord's relish;
O Nanak, dyed in the Naam, one attains the high state. ॥4॥
361.3: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
My God is true, deep and profound;
even as one serves him, the body finds peace and calm.
Through the Shabad his servants have crossed over (the world-ocean), in Sahaj and in love;
I fall at their feet forever.
Those whose minds are dyed, having embraced the Lord's love:
their pain of birth and death is gone, and through love they have met the Lord in his court.
One who tastes the Shabad finds the true flavour
and enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind.
The Lord God always fills every place;
he himself is near, he himself is far.
Everyone speaks and talks (of him) for the sake of speaking,
(but) he himself forgives and unites (one with himself).
He is not found by saying and describing;
by the Guru's grace he comes to dwell in the mind.
The Gurmukh sheds self-conceit from within,
and, dyed in the Lord's love, puts an end to attachment.
Through reflection on the Guru's Shabad he becomes utterly pure;
O Nanak, (joined) to the Naam, he becomes able to embellish (the lives of others). ॥4॥
362.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those attached to the love of another have suffered pain;
without the Shabad they have squandered their life for nothing.
One who serves the True Guru gains understanding,
(and then) no such one clings to the love of another.
Those who hold to the root (the Lord) are accepted.
Night and day repeat the Name of Ram in your heart, and through the Guru's Shabad know the One Lord.
One who clings to the branch goes without fruit;
for blind deeds the blind one is punished.
The blind manmukh finds no place of rest;
a worm of filth, he rots in the filth.
Through service of the Guru one finds lasting peace;
joining the company of the Sants, he sings the Lord's praises.
absorbed in the Naam alone, he reflects on the Naam;
he himself crosses over and becomes the saviour of his family line.
One who, attuned to the Naam, makes the Guru's Bani resound (within),
O Nanak, finds through the Shabad (the Lord's) mansion, (his true) home.
One who, by the Guru's teaching, has bathed in the pool of Truth, in the Lord's water,
has washed away the filth of evil-mindedness and all sin. ॥4॥
362.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukhs die, and in dying they spoil their death;
in the love of another they destroy their own soul.
Saying mine, mine over and over, (the manmukh) comes to ruin;
he does not recognise his own self, and stays asleep in doubt.
He has truly died who dies through the Shabad:
the Guru has taught (him) to hold praise and slander alike; in this age, repeating the Lord's (Name), he departs with the profit.
One without the Naam wastes away in the womb (of births);
lured by another, he (wastes) his life in vain.
Without the Naam the whole (world) burns in pain;
the Perfect True Guru has given this understanding.
The fickle mind suffers many blows;
having slipped away from here (this human life), it finds no place of rest.
The womb and the round of births are a dwelling of filth;
in that house the manmukh makes his home.
To my own True Guru I am ever a sacrifice;
he has merged the Gurmukh's light in the Light (of God).
Through the pure Bani one comes to dwell in one's own home (within);
O Nanak, (such a one) subdues Haumai and remains ever detached (from Maya). ॥4॥
362.3: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The slave (of the Lord) has lost (the pride of) his caste;
offering body and mind, he has come to the True Guru's refuge.
The Naam in his heart is (his) great glory;
the beloved God is ever his companion.
He is the (true) slave who dies while living;
he holds sorrow and joy both alike, and by the Guru's grace is saved through the Shabad.
The work (for him) to do has been ordained from the Lord's court:
without the Shabad no one is accepted.
(His) deed is the Lord's praise, and he enshrines the Naam (in his heart);
(the Lord) himself gives (this gift) and makes no delay.
Following its own mind, the world strays in doubt;
without capital it carries on a false trade.
Without capital no merchandise comes into one's hands;
led astray by self-will, one wastes one's life.
One who serves the True Guru becomes (the Lord's true) slave;
his caste is exalted, and he himself is exalted.
By the Guru's ladder he rises higher than all.
O Nanak, through the Naam comes greatness. ॥4॥
363.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The self-willed (soul-bride) practises falsehood upon falsehood;
she never attains her Master's mansion.
attached to another, she strays in doubt;
bound by the sense of mine, (the soul) keeps coming and going.
O mind, look at the adornment of the forsaken soul-bride:
(so is one who) fixes the mind on sons, wife, wealth and Maya: (all) falsehood, attachment, hypocrisy and vice.
She who pleases God is a happy wife for ever;
through the Guru's Shabad she adorns herself.
Her bed is a place of ease; night and day she enjoys union with the Lord;
meeting her Beloved, she finds lasting peace.
She is a true happy wife who loves the True One;
she keeps her Husband always enshrined in her heart.
She sees him close at hand, ever present:
my God pervades all.
Caste and beauty do not go along to the world hereafter;
as are the deeds one does, so does one become.
Through the Shabad one rises ever higher;
O Nanak, such a one merges in the True One. ॥4॥
363.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The servant dyed in devotion (abides) in Sahaj and in love;
living in the true awe of the Guru, he merges in the True One.
Without the perfect Guru there is no devotion;
having lost their honour, the manmukhs weep.
O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, and meditate on him always;
(so) there is bliss always, day and night, and one gains whatever fruit one wishes for.
From the perfect Guru one finds the Perfect (Lord),
and makes the Shabad and the True Name dwell in the heart.
Bathing in the pool of Amrit, the inner self is made pure;
merged in the True One, (such ones) are pure for ever.
(Such a one) sees the Lord God ever present;
by the Guru's grace (he sees him) filling every place.
Wherever I go, I see him there;
apart from the Guru there is no other giver (of this gift).
The Guru is an ocean, filled with treasures,
with excellent jewels and gems beyond measure.
By the Guru's grace the Giver gives (these jewels);
O Nanak, the Forgiving Lord grants his grace. ॥4॥
363.3: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Guru is an ocean; the True Guru is that True One himself.
Only by perfect fortune is the Guru served.
That one understands (this) whom (the Lord) himself makes understand,
and by the Guru's grace (the Lord) has him do (his) service.
With the jewel of wisdom comes full understanding;
by the Guru's grace ignorance is destroyed; one stays awake night and day, and sees that True One.
One who burns away attachment and pride with the Guru's Shabad
and gains understanding from the perfect Guru
recognises through the Guru's Shabad the (Lord's) mansion within;
his coming and going ends, and, merged in the Naam, he becomes steady.
The world is (only) birth and death;
the manmukh is heedless, and attachment to Maya is (for him) thick darkness.
He speaks ill of others and lives by much falsehood;
a worm of filth, he sinks into filth.
Joining the Sat Sangat, one gains full understanding;
the Guru's Shabad makes devotion to the Lord firm (within).
One who accepts (God's) will has peace for ever;
O Nanak, he merges in the True One. ॥4॥
364.1: Raag Asa, Panchpade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who dies (to self) through the Shabad has bliss for ever;
he meets the True Guru, and (through him) Gobind, the Great.
He does not die again, nor does he come and go;
through the perfect Guru he merges in the True One.
Those for whom the writ of the Naam was written from the very beginning
meditate on the Naam night and day, always; from the perfect Guru (they receive) the mark of devotion.
Those whom the Lord God unites (with himself):
their profound state cannot be told.
The perfect True Guru has given (them) this glory:
the highest rank, and absorption in the Lord's Name.
Whatever (God) does, he does himself alone;
in a single moment he sets up and pulls down.
(One who) only says it over and over, telling it to others,
even if he toils a hundred times, (his toil) is not accepted.
Those who have merit stored in their treasury, (God) brings to meet the Guru;
the Guru lets them hear the True (Name), the Bani and the Shabad.
Where the Shabad dwells, from there pain departs;
through the jewel of wisdom one merges, in Sahaj, in the True One.
There is no other wealth as great as the Name;
(it comes to) the one on whom that True One bestows it.
Through the perfect Shabad, he enshrines it in the mind;
O Nanak, one dyed in the Naam finds peace. ॥5॥
364.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One dances and plays many instruments,
(but) this mind is blind and deaf: to whom does he speak and recite?
Within him greed is a fire, and wandering doubt a gale;
the lamp (of wisdom) does not burn, and he gains no understanding.
With devotion through the Guru, light dawns in the heart;
recognising one's own self, one meets that God.
The dance done through the Guru: love for the Lord takes hold;
casting out the self from within, one keeps the beat.
My true God himself is the knower (of all);
through the Guru's Shabad, recognise Brahm within.
With devotion through the Guru, affection and love (spring up) within,
the Guru's Shabad (dwells there), and reflection (on the Lord) in Sahaj.
Devotion through the Guru is the way; (by it) that True One (is found);
devotion and dance in hypocrisy bring only pain.
This is devotion: that the servant dies while living,
and by the Guru's grace crosses the world-ocean.
Devotion by the Guru's word is accepted,
and the dear Lord himself comes and settles in the mind.
When the Lord is gracious, he brings (one) to meet the True Guru;
(then) one's devotion is unwavering, and one fixes the mind on the Lord.
Those dyed in devotion have lasting glory;
O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam have peace. ॥5॥
365.1: Raag Asa Kafi, Ghar 8, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
By the Lord's will the True Guru is met, and the True One is understood;
the one in whose mind the Lord dwells by the Guru's grace, he alone understands (him).
My Husband Lord alone is the Giver; there is no other at all.
When by the Guru's kindness he dwells in the mind, then there is peace for ever.
In this age the Lord's Name is fearless (and makes one fearless); it is found through reflection on the Guru's teaching.
Without the Name, the blind and foolish self-willed (soul-bride) is in Jam's power.
By the Lord's will his servant serves him, and understands that True One.
By the Lord's will he is praised; in accepting his will there is peace.
By the Lord's will the precious gift of human birth has been received, and the understanding made noble.
O Nanak, praise the Naam; through the Guru the supreme state is reached. ॥4॥
365.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
You are the Creator, the abode of truth, my Master.
Whatever pleases you, that alone will be; whatever you give, that alone I receive.
All (creation) is yours; all have meditated on you.
The one to whom you show grace has found the jewel of the Naam.
The Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) found it; the manmukh (the self-willed) lost it.
You yourself have parted (beings from you), and you yourself have united (them).
You are the river; all is within you alone.
Apart from you there is no other.
All beings and creatures are your play.
By the will that parts, even one who had met is separated; by the will that unites, there is meeting (again).
Only the one whom you make to understand comes to know (you),
and he ever speaks and tells of the Lord's virtues.
Whoever has served the Lord has found peace;
in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) he has merged in the Name of the Lord.
You yourself are the Creator; all that happens is your doing.
Apart from you there is no other, no second.
You create and create, watch over (your creation), and know all about it.
O servant Nanak, (the Lord) is revealed within the Gurmukh. ॥4॥
366.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Someone has formed a faction with a friend, a son and a brother;
someone has formed a faction with in-laws, kinsmen and a son-in-law;
someone has formed a faction with officials and headmen, for his own ends;
my faction is the Lord, who pervades all.
I have formed my faction with the Lord; the Lord is my support.
Apart from the Lord I have no other side or faction; I sing the Lord's virtues, countless and many.
Those with whom (people) form factions pass away;
forming factions in falsehood, (people) repent.
They do not last for ever, and they practise deceit in the mind.
I have formed my faction with the Lord, whose equal in might there is none.
All these factions are the spread of Maya and attachment;
the foolish fight over Maya.
They keep being born and dying, and lose the game (of life) in a gamble.
My faction is the Lord, who sets right this world and the next, all of it.
In Kalyug, the five thieves stir up factions and quarrels;
and lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride are made to grow.
The one on whom (God) shows grace, he unites with the Sat Sangat.
My faction is the Lord, who has done away with all these factions.
False love of another, settling in, creates factions;
(one) scrutinises others' faults and swells one's own pride.
As one sows, so one eats.
Servant Nanak's faction is the Lord; (this) dharma comes back victorious over the whole world. ॥5॥
366.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
As (Gurbani) is heard over and over in the heart, the Amrit (of the Name) has grown dear to the mind;
Gurbani has revealed the Unseen Lord.
O my sisters, through the Guru, listen to the Naam;
the One alone pervades within every heart; with your mouths speak the Guru's words of Amrit.
In my mind and body there is love (for the Lord) and a great longing;
by great good fortune I have found the True Guru, the Purakh.
Those who wander in the love of another, after Maya, the poison,
are luckless: they have not found the True Guru.
The Lord himself has given (me) the Amrit to drink, the sweet essence of the Lord;
through the perfect Guru, Nanak has found the Lord. ॥4॥
366.3: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
In my mind and body is love (for God), and (his) Name is my support.
I repeat the Name; the Name alone is the essence of peace.
Repeat the Name, my friends and companions.
Without the Name I have no other (support); only by great good fortune is (the Name of) the Lord received through the Guru.
Without the Name one cannot live.
By great good fortune one finds the Lord through the Guru.
Those empty of the Name bear the soot of Maya on their faces.
Without the Name, cursed, cursed is such living.
The Lord, greatest of the great, is found by great good fortune;
O Nanak, (he himself) has the Name given through the Guru. ॥4॥
367.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
I sing (God's) virtues, I speak the word of (his) virtues;
through the Guru I utter and tell the Lord's virtues.
Repeating the Name again and again, bliss has come into my mind.
The True Guru has made the Name, the True, the True, firm (within me); with delight I have sung the praises of (the Lord of) supreme bliss.
The Lord's servants, his people, sing the Lord's praises;
by great good fortune they find the Lord, who is detached (from all).
Those without virtue carry the filth of Maya about;
without virtue the proud are born and die.
In the pool of the body (God's) virtues have been brought to light;
O Nanak, through the Guru, by churning (it), the essence is drawn out. ॥4॥
367.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
I hear the Name; the Name alone is pleasing to my mind.
By great good fortune one finds the Lord through the Guru.
Repeat the Name through the Guru, and light dawns (within).
Without the Name I have no support; with every breath and every morsel I dwell on the Name.
(Since) I heard tell of the Name alone, it has been dear to my mind;
whoever tells me of the Name is my friend and companion.
The fools empty of the Name have gone (from the world) naked;
seeing the poison (of Maya), they burned and burned to death like the moth.
(God) himself establishes, and having established, himself pulls down;
O Nanak, the Lord himself gives the Name. ॥4॥
367.3: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Gurmukh has made the vine of the Lord, Har Har, grow;
it has borne fruits, full of flavour to those who relish the Lord.
Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the Lord of endless waves.
Repeating the Name again and again, praise (God) through the Guru's teaching; (so) death, Jam's servants and the serpent are slain.
The Lord, Har Har, has placed (his) devotion in the Guru;
the Guru, pleased, gives (it) to the Sikh, O my brother.
One who does deeds in Haumai knows nothing of the way (of devotion);
he is like the elephant that bathes and (then) throws dust over its head.
If (people's) fortune is great, great and lofty,
O Nanak, (they) repeat the Name and, (joined) to the True One, become pure. ॥4॥
367.4: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
A hunger for the Name of the Lord, Har Har, has been awakened in my mind;
hearing the Name, the mind is satisfied, O my brother.
Repeat the Name, my friends, Sikhs of the Guru.
Repeat the Name; in the Name itself you will find peace; through the Guru's teaching keep the Name in your mind and consciousness.
Hearing the Name, the Name alone, the mind turns green (with life);
earning the profit of the Name through the Guru's teaching, it blossoms.
Without the Name one is a leper, blinded by attachment;
all the deeds one does are fruitless, entanglements that bring pain.
It is the one of great good fortune who repeats the praise of the Lord, Har Har Har;
O Nanak, by the Guru's teaching, his attention (liv) is held fast in the Name. ॥4॥
368.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 6, three shabads by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The yogi takes (his instrument) in hand and plays the string, but the veena sounds hollow.
O yogi, through the Guru's teaching utter the Lord's praises, and this mind will be drenched in the Lord's love.
O yogi, give your understanding the teaching of the Lord.
In every age the one Lord, Har Har, is at work; before him I bow.
They sing raags and speak in many ways, but this mind keeps playing its own games.
(They are like those who) yoke (the oxen to) the well to water the land, but the oxen have got up and gone off to graze on the vines.
In the town of the body sow the deeds of (remembering) the Lord; the Lord sprouts, and the field turns green.
Make the mind steady and yoke that mind as the ox, and with it water (the field) with the Lord through the Guru's teaching.
(O God,) the yogis, the jangams, the whole creation are yours; whatever understanding you give, by that they walk.
O God of servant Nanak, Knower of hearts, O Lord, urge my mind on and join it (to yourself). ॥4॥
368.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Why should one go looking for ankle bells to keep time, why play the rabab?
In coming and going (for them) an instant passes; for that long I would hold the Name in my heart.
Such devotion has taken shape in my mind
that I cannot live an instant, a moment, without the Lord, as a fish dies without water.
Why should one tune the five (strings) and the seven (notes) to sing, why raise the strain of a raag?
In tuning and choosing, an instant, a moment, a little while passes; for that long my mind sings the praises of the Lord (Ram).
Why should one dance, stretching out the feet, why stretch out the hands?
In stretching out hands and feet a moment's delay passes; for that long my mind remembers the Lord (Ram).
Why should one try to win the people's trust? When the world is won over, no honour comes of it.
O servant Nanak, meditate on the Lord in your heart always; then everyone hails (you). ॥4॥
368.3: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Let us join the Sat Sangat, meet the Lord's Saadh (the Guru), and, joined in the Sangat, sing the Lord's praises.
(So) the jewel of divine knowledge shines, there is light in the heart, and the darkness of ignorance goes.
O servants of the Lord, dance, meditating on the Lord, Har Har.
If I meet such Sants, O my brother, I would wash the feet of those servants.
O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, holding your attention on the Lord night and day.
Whatever you wish for, that fruit you will obtain, and hunger will not come upon you again.
The Lord himself is the boundless Creator; the Lord himself speaks and makes (all) speak.
(O God,) those Sants alone are good who are pleasing to you, whose honour you accept.
Nanak is never sated with uttering the Lord's praises; the more he utters them, the more peace he finds.
The Lord has given the storehouses of his devotion; the buyer of virtues trades and carries them away. ॥4॥
369.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa Kafi, Ghar 8, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Death has come, ordained from the very start; it is through Haumai that one weeps (over it).
Meditating on the Name through the Guru, one becomes steady.
Those who, through the Perfect Guru, have understood that they must depart win acclaim;
they have earned the Name, that excellent profit, and through the Shabad they are merged (in God).
The days written beforehand, O mother, those days have come;
the departure, today or tomorrow, has been decreed from the start.
Wasted is the life of those who have forgotten the Name;
they have played a game of dice in the world and lost this mind.
Those who have found the Guru have peace in life and in death;
O Nanak, true, they merge in the True One, in the True One. ॥4॥
369.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
(Whoever,) having received the precious gift of human birth, has meditated on the Name
has, by the Guru's grace, understood (its worth) and merged in the True One.
Those for whom it was so written from the start have practised the Name;
at the True One's door they are found true, and (he) has called them into his palace.
The treasure of the Name is within (everyone), (but) it is found through the Guru;
meditating on the Name night and day, let us sing the Lord's praises.
Within lies the wealth (of the Name) with its countless virtues, (but) the self-willed do not find it;
(the manmukh) swells with pride in Haumai, and through that pride goes astray by himself.
O Nanak, (the manmukh) goes astray by himself, by his own doing alone;
through the Guru's teaching there is light in the mind, and the True One is found. ॥4॥
369.3: Raag Asavari, Ghar 16, two shabads by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji), Sudhang.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Night and day I sing the Kirtan of the Lord's Name.
The True Guru has shown me the Lord's Name; I cannot live an instant, a moment, without the Lord.
Hearing (of the Lord), Simran and the Lord's Kirtan are (all) I have; I cannot live without the Lord, not for a single instant.
As the swan cannot live without the lake, so how can the Lord's servant live without serving the Lord?
Some have set their love on another, holding duality in the heart; some have set their love on attachment and pride;
the Lord's servant has set his love on the Lord, the state of nirvana; O Nanak, he keeps remembering the Lord God, Har Har. ॥2॥
369.4: Raag Asavari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O mother, tell me (where to find) my Beloved, the Lord (Ram), O mother.
I cannot live an instant, a moment, without the Lord, as the camel delights in the vine.
My mind has grown full of longing and turned away (from the world), for the sight of the Lord, my Friend.
As the bumblebee cannot be without the lotus, so I cannot live without the Lord.
Keep me in your refuge, O beloved Lord of the world; fulfil my longing, O Lord, Master of the earth (Gusain).
Bliss wells up in servant Nanak's mind when you show him your sight, O Lord, even for the blink of an eye. ॥2॥
370.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Whoever set his love on (Maya) was in the end devoured by her;
whoever seated her in comfort, to him she showed great fear.
Brothers, friends and family quarrel (among themselves) at the sight of her;
by the Guru's grace she has come under our control.
Seeing her so, (all) have been bewitched:
seekers, Siddhas, gods and men; all but the Saadh (the Guru) have been cheated by the cheat.
Some wander as renunciates, but she seizes them through lust;
some, as householders, hoard her, but she does not become their own;
some are called sati (givers of charity), and she torments them greatly;
the Lord has saved us by attaching us to the True Guru's feet.
She has led the ascetics astray even as they practise austerities;
all the pandits she has enticed through greed;
she has enticed (the beings of) the three qualities, she has enticed the heavens;
the True Guru has saved us, giving (us) his hand.
To the one who knows (God) she is a handmaid in waiting;
with folded hands she serves him and prays:
Whatever you say, that work I will do;
O servant Nanak, (she says,) I will not come near the Gurmukh. ॥4॥
370.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My Husband has set me apart from my mother-in-law;
my sisters-in-law, younger and elder, have died of grief and anguish;
the hold of the household's elder brother-in-law has ended;
my Husband, skilful and wise, has protected me.
Listen, O people: I have found the sweet essence of love.
The wicked are slain, the enemies destroyed; the True Guru has given me the Lord's Name.
First, I gave up the love of Haumai;
second, I gave up the ways of the world;
leaving the three qualities, foe and friend have become alike (to me);
meeting the Saadh (the Guru), I have recognised the quality of the fourth state (turiya).
In the cave of Sahaj I have set my seat;
the unstruck sound (Anhad) of the One whose form is light has begun to ring;
reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, there is supreme bliss;
the bride steeped in the love of her Beloved is blessed, a happy wedded wife.
Servant Nanak speaks of the contemplation of God;
whoever hears it and lives it crosses over.
He is neither born nor dies, neither comes nor goes;
he remains merged in the Lord. ॥4॥
370.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Single-minded devotion (to the Lord) is a bride of noble nature,
peerless in beauty, perfect in conduct.
The home in which she dwells is graced with glory;
(but) only some rare being has won her, through the Guru.
Meeting the Guru, I have won a bride of noble deeds,
who graces the sacred rite, the wedding, and every occasion.
As long as she lived with her father (the Guru),
so long did her husband (the soul) wander about in great sadness.
(When he) served and won the favour of the True Being,
the Guru brought her into the home, and then every comfort was found.
She bears the thirty-two good marks; Truth is her offspring, her sons.
She is obedient, accomplished and fair.
She fulfils the wishes of her husband and master's heart,
and she has contented all the wives of her husband's brothers, younger and elder.
In all the family she is the best,
and she gives good counsel to her husband's brothers, younger and elder.
Blessed is the home where she comes and shines forth;
O servant Nanak, (life there) passes in peace upon peace. ॥4॥
371.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Every resolve I make, she (Maya) keeps from ripening;
she stands on guard close by goodness and self-restraint.
She takes on many disguises and displays many forms;
she will not let me dwell in my home, and leads me astray this way and that.
She has (set herself up as) mistress of the house, and gives me no place to live in it;
if I make an effort, she tangles me (all the more).
She came sent from the Source as a servant,
(yet) she has conquered the nine regions and every place and space;
on river banks and at places of pilgrimage she spares neither yogis nor sannyasis;
(scholars) have worn themselves out reading the Simritis and studying the Vedas.
Where I sit, there she sits too, at my side;
in her might she forces her way into all the worlds.
Taking refuge with the feeble, I cannot stay safe (from her);
tell me, friend, to whom shall I go?
On hearing counsel, I came to the True Guru;
the Guru made the mantra of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm within me.
Singing the praises of the Infinite, I have come to dwell in my own home within;
God has met me, and Nanak is free of care.
The house is mine (now), and this mistress is mine;
(now) she is my servant; the Guru has made me one of (the Lord's) court. ॥4॥
371.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The first counsel was that I should send a letter;
the second, that I should send two men (to speak for me);
the third, that I should try some means or other;
but I gave up everything, O God, and meditated on you alone.
(Now) there is supreme bliss, freedom from care and Sahaj;
the foes and the enemies have perished, and I have found peace.
The True Guru gave me this teaching:
soul and body are all the Lord's domain.
Whatever I do is by your strength;
you are my shelter, you alone my support.
Leaving you, O God, to which side could one go?
There is no other, no second, equal to you.
To whom does your servant owe deference?
It is the Saakat who strays, wandering in the wilderness.
Your greatness cannot be told;
wherever it may be, you take (your servant) in your embrace and save him.
Nanak, your servant, is in your refuge;
God has kept (my) honour, and songs of rejoicing ring out. ॥4॥
372.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Banker,) struggling across alien lands, I have come for trade;
I had heard of a peerless, profitable ware.
I have brought a capital of virtues tied in the hem of my cloth;
seeing the jewel (of the Name), this mind of mine clings to it.
O Banker, the traders have come to your door;
bring out the goods, and let the deal be struck.
The Banker (God) sent me to the Banker (the Guru);
priceless is the jewel, priceless the capital.
I found a loving friend to act as go-between,
(through him) the bargain was made, and my mind is steady.
It fears no thieves, no wind, no water;
in Sahaj I bought it, and in Sahaj I shall take it away.
Earning it by truth, I have met no pain,
and I have brought it home safe and sound.
The profit is gained, and joy has come;
blessed is the perfect, forgiving Banker!
Only someone rare has gained this bargain, through the Guru;
Nanak has brought home a fruitful cargo. ॥4॥
372.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(My Husband) did not weigh any merit or fault of mine,
nor look at my beauty, my colour or my adornment;
I knew nothing of the ways of good manners and good conduct;
(yet) the Beloved took me by the arm and brought me to his bed.
Listen, my friend: my Husband has done a husband's part by me;
his hand upon my brow, he has made me his own and kept me safe; what do these unknowing people know (of it)?
Now, at last, my wedded happiness shines;
my Husband has met me, and has looked into all my pain.
In my courtyard is the radiance of the moon;
night and day there is bliss with my Beloved.
My clothes are dyed a deep red;
all my jewels and the flowers at my throat adorn me.
My Beloved looked upon me with his glance, and I gained all treasures;
the hold of the wicked enemies is at an end.
I enjoy happiness ever, and delight ever;
the Naam, the nine treasures, is in my home, and I am fulfilled.
Says Nanak, when the Husband has adorned (the soul-bride),
she is a happy wife, abiding for ever with her Husband. ॥4॥
372.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(People) give alms (to the Brahmins) and pay them worship;
yet even as they take what is given, they deny it.
O Brahmin, at the door to which you must go,
at that door it is you who will repent.
Such Brahmins are drowned, O brother,
who plot harm against the innocent.
Greed is within them; they wander about as if rabid;
they slander others, and lift a load (of sin) on to their heads.
Robbed by Maya, (the Brahmin) does not remember (the Lord);
lost in doubt, he strays on many paths.
Outwardly they put on many religious garbs,
but within, the poison of Maya has laid siege and encamped.
He teaches others but has no understanding himself;
such a Brahmin succeeds nowhere.
O foolish Brahmin, keep God in mind;
seeing and hearing, he is with you.
Says Nanak, if (it is your) good fortune,
give up your pride and fall at the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
372.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Pain and sickness have gone from the body; the mind is pure, singing the praises of the Lord, Har Har;
joining the company of the Saadh (the Guru), there is bliss; now my mind wanders nowhere.
The burning (within) is quenched through the Guru's Shabad, O mother;
all fever and dread are gone; I have met the Guru who cools and calms, and (abide) in Sahaj and in love.
My running about has ended, for I have understood the One alone; now, unshaken, I have settled in my place.
(O Lord,) your Sants save the world; beholding the sight of them, I am content.
The sins of (many) births have fallen behind me; now, steadfast, I have taken hold of the feet of the Saadh (the Guru).
(My) mind sings songs of joy in the strain of Sahaj; death no longer devours it.
O Cause of creation, my all-powerful (Lord), Giver of peace, my Lord King, Har Har:
Nanak lives by repeating your Name; like warp and weft you are with me, my help. ॥4॥
373.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, has slipped from his mind; the slanderer receives what he himself has done.
If anyone keeps him company, (the slanderer) takes him along on his way.
The slanderer carries a load as huge as a python, of things that are not, and burns (himself) in the fire.
What comes to pass at the door of the Supreme God, Nanak tells aloud:
the Lord's devotees are in bliss for ever; singing the Lord's Kirtan, (the devotee) blossoms. ॥2॥
373.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When I had made every adornment,
even then my mind was not content.
I put many perfumes on my body,
(yet) I do not find that joy, not even a sesame seed's worth.
In my mind I cherish this hope:
that seeing my Beloved I may live, O my mother.
Mother, what am I to do? This mind finds no patience.
Longing for my darling Beloved steals it away.
Clothes, jewellery and pleasures of many special kinds:
these too I count as of no worth.
Honour, fame, respect and greatness,
the whole world at my command,
a home so fair, like a ruby:
(yet) only if I please God shall I be happy for ever.
Dishes and foods of many kinds,
pleasures and shows spread out in plenty,
kingdom, lands, and wide command:
(with these) the mind is not filled, and its thirst does not go.
Without meeting (him), I cannot get through this day;
if God is met, (the soul-bride) gains every comfort.
Searching and searching, I have heard this word:
without the Saadh Sangat no one has crossed over.
One with good fortune on the forehead has found the True Guru;
that one's hope is fulfilled, and the mind is satisfied.
When God was met, the burning (within) came to an end;
O Nanak, (that one) found (him) within mind and body. ॥4॥
373.3: Raag Asa, Panchpade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
First, your kind is noble (you are born human);
second, your family line is held in honour;
third, your dwelling place is beautiful;
yet your form is marred, for there is pride in your mind.
(O soul-bride,) you are lovely, fair of form, wise and clever,
yet you are caught in great pride and in attachment.
Your kitchen is spotlessly pure;
having bathed, you worship and put a red tilak (on your brow);
you boast with words, and with your mouth you utter wisdom;
but the dog of greed has wasted all your good ways.
You wear (fine) clothes and enjoy pleasures;
you keep up (religious) observances for a good name among people;
you spread about perfume, sandalwood and sweet scents;
but your companion is wicked anger, the chandal (outcaste).
All other species are your water-carriers (your servants);
on this earth the rule is yours;
gold, silver and wealth are in your keeping;
but lust has spoilt your virtuous character.
She on whom the Lord King casts his glance of mercy
is set free from captivity (to the vices).
One who, joining the Saadh Sangat, has found the Lord's sweet essence:
says Nanak, that body is fruitful.
As a happy wedded wife (of the Lord), all beauty and all comforts become you;
(then) you are truly most beautiful and wise. ॥12॥
374.1: Raag Asa, two Iktuke, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Whoever is seen to be alive (in ego) must surely die;
whoever has died (to self) shall remain unshaken.
Those who have died while living: those dead ones truly live;
they have put the medicine of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, into their mouths, and through the Guru's Shabad they drink the essence of Amrit.
The unbaked pot (of the body) must surely break;
one whose trikuti (the knitted brow of inner fretting) is loosed comes to dwell in his own home within.
Whoever climbs high (in pride) falls into the nether world;
whoever lies low on the ground (in humility) is not touched by death.
Those who went wandering about have gained nothing;
those are steadfast who have lived the Guru's Shabad.
Soul and body, all is the Lord's property;
O Nanak, meeting the Guru, (those who know this) are filled with joy. ॥5॥
374.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Your puppet (of a body) has been fashioned with great skill;
know it for the truth: it will turn to dust.
Keep your Root (the Lord) in mind, O heedless fool;
why do you take pride in so little?
You are a guest (in this world), given three seers (of grain) a day;
everything else is with you only in trust.
Filth, bones and blood, wrapped up in skin:
over this you have taken up pride.
If you understand the One Thing (the Name), you will become pure;
without that understanding you remain impure for ever.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to the Guru,
by whom the Lord is found, the all-pervading, all-knowing Being.
Raag Asa, Iktuke Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One ghari of the day is to me as many days;
my mind finds no rest: how shall I meet my Beloved?
Not one moment, not one day ever seems to pass for me;
in my mind is a great longing for his sight; if only some Sant would unite me with my Husband.
The day's four watches are as long as the four ages;
when night falls, there seems to be no end to it.
She whom the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) together have parted from her Husband
wanders and wanders, weeping and wringing her hands.
To servant Nanak the Lord has shown his sight;
knowing his own self, he has attained the highest peace. ॥4॥
375.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the Lord's service is the supreme treasure;
the Lord's service is (to utter) the Amrit Name with the mouth.
The Lord is my companion, my friend ever at my side;
in pain or in pleasure he is present whenever I remember him; how can poor Jam frighten me?
The Lord is my shelter; the Lord's is the strength I have;
the Lord is my friend, the support of my mind.
The Lord is my stock in trade, the Lord my credit;
I earn the wealth (of the Name) through the Guru; the Lord is my Banker.
Through the Guru's grace this understanding comes;
servant Nanak merges in the Lord's embrace. ॥4॥
375.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If God is merciful, then I fix this mind (on the True Guru),
and serving the True Guru I obtain every fruit.
O mind, why should you grieve? My True Guru is perfect;
he grants the mind's desires, he is the treasure of every comfort, a pool of Amrit ever brimming full.
Whoever has enshrined the lotus feet (of the Lord) within the heart,
in him the Light has shone forth, and he has met the beloved Lord (Ram).
The five companions (the senses) joined to sing a song of joy,
and sounded the unstruck music (nad) of the Bani.
Guru Nanak was pleased, and the Lord King was met;
the night (of life) has passed in peace, in Sahaj and in love. ॥4॥
375.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In his mercy the Lord has become manifest (within me);
I have met the True Guru and found the perfect wealth.
Such wealth of the Lord should be gathered, O brother:
fire does not burn it, water does not drown it, and it never leaves one's side to go elsewhere.
It never falls short, nor does it run out;
the mind, eating of it and spending it, stays satisfied.
He is the true banker in whose house the Lord's wealth is stored;
from this wealth the whole world gains.
He alone has found the Lord's wealth whose due it was, written beforehand;
O servant Nanak, at the very end the Name is (the soul's) adornment. ॥4॥
375.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As a farmer sows his crop
and cuts it, unripe or ripe, O mortal, (so death comes at any age).
Know that whoever is born shall die;
the devotee of Govind (alone) has become steadfast.
After the day, night will surely fall;
and when the night is gone, morning comes again.
The unfortunate lie asleep in attachment to Maya;
by the Guru's grace some rare one wakes.
Says Nanak, let (the Lord's) praises be sung every day;
(so) the face becomes radiant, and the mind pure. ॥4॥
376.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) yours are the nine treasures, all the treasures;
(you are) the Fulfiller of desires, who protects at the last.
You are my Beloved; then what hunger can there be?
When you dwell in my mind, no pain touches me.
Whatever you do, that alone is accepted;
O true Master, true is your command.
When it pleases you, then I sing the Lord's praises;
in your house there is justice for ever and ever.
O true Master, unseen, beyond all knowing,
as you attach him, so Nanak is attached to (your) service. ॥4॥
376.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Lord) is near to every being, ever at their side;
his power is at work in every form and colour.
(My) mind does not fret, nor pine, nor is it given to weeping,
(for) our Master is imperishable, unmanifest, beyond the reach of the senses, secure for ever.
(O Lord,) to whom need your humble servant defer,
when the King himself upholds his honour?
The slave whom God has freed from caste
(The Lord) depends on no one, and is free of all care;
says servant Nanak: hail the Great Master as wondrous (Wah). ॥4॥
376.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Forsaking the Lord's sweet essence, (man) is drunk on shallow pleasure;
the treasure is in his own house, yet he gets up and goes outside (to seek it).
He cannot bear to hear the true, Amrit discourse;
caught up in false tales, he quarrels.
He draws his wages from the Master, but serves another;
with such sins is the mortal covered over.
He hides from the One who is ever his companion;
what is of no use, that he begs for again and again.
Says Nanak: O God, merciful to the meek,
as it pleases you, so cherish (us). ॥4॥
376.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord's Name is the wealth of soul and breath;
here and hereafter it is what serves them (soul and breath).
Without the Lord's Name, all else is too little;
my mind is sated and fulfilled by the Lord's sight.
The Gurbani is a ruby, a storehouse of devotion;
singing it, hearing it and living it, (the mind) is filled with joy.
(My) mind is attached to the lotus feet (of the Lord);
the True Guru, pleased, has given this gift.
The Guru has given Nanak such teaching
that he has recognised the imperishable God in every heart. ॥4॥
376.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord who fills every place has brought forth delights and wondrous plays;
his own work he has himself made fair.
Complete is all the making of the perfect Master,
whose glory is spread abroad, filling every place.
He whose Name is a treasure, whose renown is spotless,
is himself the Creator; there is none other.
All beings and creatures are in his hand;
God pervades all, and is with everyone.
The Perfect Guru has made a perfect arrangement;
O Nanak, the devotees have been given honour. ॥4॥
377.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the Guru's Shabad, shape this mind of yours;
the sight of the Guru is the Lord's wealth: gather it.
O noble understanding, come and dwell in my heart,
that I may meditate on Govind and sing his virtues, and that the Name may grow most dear to me.
In the True Name are fullness and content;
the dust (of the feet) of the Sants is bathing at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.
In all I know the one Creator;
joining the Saadh Sangat, the intellect has gained discernment.
Giving up pride, (I have become) the servant of all;
the Guru has blessed Nanak with (this) gift. ॥4॥
377.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(My) intellect is lit up, (my) understanding made whole;
by it, evil-mindedness and distance (from the Lord) are destroyed.
Such is the Guru's teaching I have received
that, drowning in a dreadful dark well, I have come out (of it), O my brother.
(This world) is a vast, unfathomable ocean of fire;
the Guru, a mine of jewels, is the ship that carries (one) across.
This Maya is hard to cross, dark and perilous;
the Perfect Guru has shown (me) the way, plain to see.
I have no chanting, no austerity, no clever argument at all;
O Guru, Nanak (has come) into your refuge. ॥4॥
377.3: Raag Asa, two Tipade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Drinking the Lord's sweet essence, one stays dyed (in it) for ever;
other tastes wear off in a moment.
Those drunk with the Lord's essence have bliss in the mind for ever;
in other tastes, anxiety takes hold.
Whoever drinks the Lord's essence is wholly intoxicated, enraptured;
all other tastes are shallow, O brother.
The worth of the Lord's essence cannot be told;
the Lord's essence is kept in the shop of the Saadh (the Guru).
For lakhs and crores (of coins) no one obtains it;
(O Lord,) you give it to the one whose lot it is to receive it.
Tasting it, Nanak is lost in wonder;
O Nanak, this savour has come from the Guru.
here and hereafter, (he) does not leave it to go anywhere else;
Nanak is steeped in the Lord's sweet essence. ॥3॥
377.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O soul-bride,) if you wipe out lust, anger, greed and attachment, the evil-mindedness you have taken up yourself falls away;
if, becoming humble, you serve, you will be dear to your Beloved's heart.
Listen, O lovely one: the words of the Saadh (the Guru) bring rescue;
your pain, hunger and dread will be gone, and you will find peace, O woman who longs for a mind at peace.
Wash (his) feet and serve the Guru: the soul grows pure, and the poison and the thirst (of Maya) are driven out.
If you become the handmaid, the lowly handmaid, of (the Lord's) servants, you will win honour at the Lord's door.
This alone is right conduct, this alone the daily way: obey (the Lord's) command, and your devotion is fulfilled.
Whoever lives by this mantra (teaching), O Nanak, is carried across the terrifying world-ocean. ॥3॥
378.1: Raag Asa, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You have received this lovely human body;
this is your turn to meet Gobind (the Lord of the universe).
All other tasks are of no use to you at all;
join the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) and remember the Naam alone.
Set yourself to the task of crossing the ocean of the world;
your life is passing in vain in the love of Maya.
(O Lord,) I have practised neither repetition (of the Name), austerity, self-restraint nor any deed of dharma;
I have not served the Saadh (the holy one), nor have I known you, O Lord, my King.
Says Nanak, we are of lowly deeds;
save the honour of one who has come into your refuge. ॥2॥
378.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) apart from you I have no other at all; you are within my mind.
You are (my) friend, my companion, my God; why then, O my soul, are you afraid?
Yours is my shelter, in you my hope;
sitting or rising, sleeping or waking, with every breath and every morsel, may I never forget you.
Keep me, keep me in your refuge, O God; (this world) is a fearsome ocean of fire.
O True Guru, Giver of peace to Nanak, we are your children, O Gopal. ॥2॥
378.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
God has set the Lord's servants free;
my mind is at one with the Beloved; the fever has died, as if it had eaten poison.
Neither chill nor heat touches (one) at all who sings the praises of the Name of Ram;
the witch has no hold at all on the mind that is in the refuge of the lotus feet.
By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), (the Lord) has become merciful and has himself become (my) help.
Nanak sings ever of the Treasure of virtues, dread and pain wiped away. ॥2॥
378.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have taken the medicine of the Lord's Name;
I have found comfort, and the very seat of pain is destroyed.
The fever has left, by the word of the Perfect Guru;
there is joy, and all sorrows are wiped away.
All beings and creatures have found peace
who, O Nanak, have meditated on the Supreme Lord in their minds. ॥2॥
378.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That hour (of death), which no one wishes for, arrives;
without (the Lord's) Hukam, how can one understand, though it be explained?
(The body) is consumed by the cold (water), the hot (fire) or the earth;
(but) that (soul) is neither child nor old, O brother.
Servant Nanak is in the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru);
by the Guru's grace (he) has crossed beyond fear. ॥2॥
378.6: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
For ever and ever the soul is lit up
in one who, in the Saadh Sangat, dwells at the Lord's feet.
Repeat the Name of Ram every day, O my mind;
you will find coolness, calm and lasting peace, and all your sins will go, O mind.
Says Nanak, one whose destiny is perfect
meets the True Guru, and meets the perfect Supreme Lord.
The thirty-four (shabads) of the Second Ghar.
378.7: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
She whose friend is the Lord, the Master, God:
her pain is gone, and never again is she in misery.
In his mercy he has joined her to his feet;
she is at ease, in comfort, Sahaj and bliss.
Singing (his) virtues in the Saadh Sangat, she has grown beyond all weighing;
remembering the Lord, O Nanak, she has become priceless. ॥2॥
379.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Lust, anger, Maya, pride and envy: all these (we) have gambled away and lost;
truth, contentment, compassion, dharma and truthful living: these (we) have brought into our own home.
All the burdens of birth and death are ended;
joining the company (of the holy), the mind has become pure; the Perfect Guru has taken (us) along and carried (us) across in an instant.
The mind remains the dust (of the feet) of all, and all appear as dear friends.
My Master pervades all; giving his gifts, he takes care of all beings.
He himself is the One, the One alone, only the One; the whole expanse is the One's alone.
Repeating (the Name) again and again, all have become holy; meditating on the one Name, they have saved a great many.
The Lord of the world is deep, profound and boundless; he has no end at all, no near shore and no far shore.
By your grace, (O Lord,) Nanak sings (your) praises, and, meditating again and again, bows before God. ॥4॥
379.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) you are infinite, unmanifest, beyond the reach of the senses; all this (visible) form is yours.
What cleverness can we creatures show, when everything is within you?
O my True Guru, by your wondrous play keep your children safe;
give (me) good understanding, that I may ever sing (your) virtues, O my Master, inaccessible and infinite.
As the mortal in the mother's womb lives on the support of the Name:
he is in bliss, keeps (the Lord) in mind with every breath, and the fire (of the womb) cannot touch him.
Another's wealth, another's wife, the slander of others: take away (my) love for these;
may I serve (your) lotus feet within my heart, upheld by the Perfect Guru.
Home, mansions and palaces, whatever is seen: none of them goes along;
as long as you live in this age of Kalyug, O servant Nanak, cherish the Naam (in your heart). ॥4॥
379.3: Raag Asa, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Rule, lands, the bloom of youth, home, renown, a handsome form, youthful vigour,
great wealth, elephants and horses, rubies bought for lakhs and brought home:
hereafter, in the Lord's court, (none of it) is of use; the proud man departs and leaves (it all) behind.
Why should the mind be set on anything but the One?
Rising, sitting, sleeping and waking, let us meditate on the Lord for ever and ever.
One may win marvellous, splendid contests in the arena and win the fights on the battlefield,
and brag with his mouth like this: I kill, I bind, I let go;
(yet when) the Hukam of the Supreme Lord came, he left (it all) one day and was gone.
One may perform religious rites and duties in many ways, yet not know the Creator;
he preaches but does not practise it himself, and does not recognise the Shabad, the essence;
naked he came and naked he will go, like an elephant that (bathes and then) scatters dust over itself.
Listen, Sants, good people, all my friends: this expanse is false (it perishes).
Crying mine, mine, the fools have drowned; they have wasted away and died.
O Nanak, (whoever) has met the Guru and meditated on the Naam has been carried across through the True Name. ॥4॥
380.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The whole world lies asleep in delusion, blinded by its worldly affairs; only some servant of the Lord stays awake.
It is engrossed in the great enchantress (Maya), her love dearer to it than life; some rare one renounces her.
The peerless lotus feet of the Lord, the mantra of the Sants: to these some Saadh holds fast.
O Nanak, in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) they awake, dyed in divine knowledge; this is (the Lord's) grace on the most fortunate. ॥4॥
380.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) whatever pleases you is accepted (by your servants); that alone is peace and Sahaj in (their) minds.
(You are) the Cause of creation, all-powerful, infinite; O brother, there is no other (like God).
Your servants sing your praises, relishing them again and again.
What you yourself do and have (others) do is your servant's counsel, resolve and wisdom.
Your Naam is Amrit, O Beloved; in the Saadh Sangat (your servants) have found its taste.
Those servants alone are filled to contentment and made whole who have sung of the Lord, the treasure of peace.
O Master, one who leans on you has no anxiety.
Those on whom your mercy has fallen are worthy bankers, rich in good fortune.
From the moment (one) has had the sight (of God), doubt, attachment and deceit have all gone out (of him);
O Nanak, he has made the True Naam the stuff of his daily life, and is merged in love of the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
380.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The slanderer) washes off the grime others gathered birth after birth, but reaps what he himself has done.
Here he has no peace, in the Lord's court no shelter; he goes to the city of Jam and burns there.
The slanderer has squandered his precious life.
In nothing can he reach (his aim), and hereafter he finds no place.
The hapless slanderer's own past deeds have come upon him; what can the poor man do?
He is brought to ruin where no one shields him; to whom can he cry for help?
Nowhere is there release for the slanderer; so it has pleased the Master.
As each one slanders the Sants, so the Sants find comfort in it.
The Sants lean on you, O Master; you are the Sants' helper.
Says Nanak, the Lord has kept the Sants safe and swept the slanderers away. ॥4॥
381.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) washes the outside while the mind within stays filthy has lost both his places (this world and the next).
Here he is gripped by lust, anger and attachment; hereafter he sobs and weeps.
The understanding that worships Govind is of another kind.
Beating its hole does not kill the snake; the deaf one does not hear the Naam.
(One) gives up and throws away the labour of earning a living, yet does not know the worth of devotion;
he takes to arguing over the Vedas and Shastras, but does not recognise the essence, union (with God).
As a false coin is laid bare when it comes under the eye of the money-testers,
(so) the Knower of hearts knows everything; what can be hidden from him?
Cheated in falsehood and fraud, the (mortal) whose days are few perishes in an instant.
Nanak has spoken the truth, the truth, the truth: keep (God) in your own heart and see. ॥4॥
381.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As he strives, (the servant's) mind grows pure; he dances by casting out his self-conceit.
He seizes the five (passions) and keeps them under control, and (keeps) Ekankar, the One Creator, in his mind.
(O God,) your servant dances (thus): he sings (your) praises,
and plays the unstruck Shabad as his rebab, pakhavaj, cymbals and ankle-bells.
First he awakens his own mind, and then he delights others.
He repeats the Name of Ram in his heart, and with his mouth recites it to all.
With his hands he washes the feet of the Saadhs, and puts the dust of the Sants on his body.
He offers up his mind and body, laying them before the Guru, and obtains the true treasure.
Whoever hears and beholds (this dance) with faith is rid of the pain of birth and death.
Such a dance wards off hell; O Nanak, (by it) the Gurmukh awakens. ॥4॥
381.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The mind's bent, once) a lowly Chandal woman, has become a Brahmin woman; from a Shudra woman she has risen to the highest, O brother.
The flame (of craving), left empty though (it took in) the underworlds and the skies, is quenched and spent, O brother.
The cat of the house (the mind's greed) has learnt another lesson; seeing the mouse (of worldly things), she takes fright, O brother.
The Guru has put the lion (of pride) in the power of the goat (of humility), and set the dog (of the senses) to (eating) grass, O brother.
With no props the thatch is held up; the homeless (wandering mind) has gained a home, O brother.
With no setter the jewelled ornament has been set, and a wondrous gem fixed in it, O brother.
The complainant could never reach justice; once silent, he has received the verdict, O brother.
She who sat in state upon the carpet (in pride) now seems as one dead; the glaring of eyes (at others) has fled, O brother.
Ignorant is he who says, I know; one who (truly) knows does not stay hidden, O brother.
Says Nanak, one whom the Guru has given the Amrit (of the Naam) to drink blossoms, relishing it again and again, O brother. ॥4॥
382.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Cutting (their) bonds, (God) has forgotten (their) faults; he has kept to his age-old way.
Like a mother and father he has been merciful, and has cherished (them) as his children.
The great Gopal has kept the Guru's Sikhs safe;
looking on (them) with his gracious eye, he has drawn (them) out of the vast ocean of the world.
He by whose Simran one is freed from Jam, and finds peace in this world and the next:
with every breath and every morsel repeat (his Name) with your tongue; let his praises be sung day after day.
Through loving devotion (they) have attained the supreme state; in the Saadh Sangat (their) sorrows have fled.
Nothing wears away or is lost, and no fear takes hold: the pure wealth of the Lord is tied in (their) knot.
At the last moment God has been (their) help; here and hereafter he is the protector.
(God is) my life, my friend, my well-wisher and my wealth; Nanak is for ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥4॥
382.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When you are (my) Master, what fear can there be? Whom but you should I praise?
If you alone are (mine), I have everything; for me there is no other but you.
O Father (God), I have seen the world to be poison.
Protect (me), my Lord of the world; your Naam is my support.
You know all the pain of the mind; to whom else should it be told?
Without the Name the whole world has gone mad; when the Naam is found, peace is found.
What is there to say, and to whom should it be told? Whatever is to be said is (to be said) to God.
All that comes to pass is your doing; for ever and ever my hope is in you.
If you grant (me) greatness, that greatness is yours; here and hereafter I meditate on you alone.
