O God of Nanak, ever the Giver of peace, my strength is your Name alone. ॥4॥
382.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Your Naam is Amrit, O Master; this supreme essence (your) servant has drunk.
The fears and burdens of birth after birth are ended; sin is destroyed, and the doubt of duality (is gone).
Beholding the sight of you, I have come alive;
hearing your words, O True Guru, my mind and body have grown cool and calm.
By your grace (I) came to the Saadh Sangat; this work you yourself have done.
I have clasped your feet firmly, O God; with ease the poison (of Maya) has withered away.
Your Naam, O God, is the treasure of peace; this imperishable mantra I have received;
the True Guru in his grace gave it to me; my fever, my anguish and my enmity are gone.
Blessed is the human body (I) have been given, through which God has united (me) with himself.
Blessed is that Kalyug (too), if Kirtan is sung in the Saadh Sangat and, O Nanak, the Naam is the heart's support. ॥4॥
383.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Everything has come about from the very first (by his will); what other knowledge can anyone have?
For all (its) slips and failings, the Supreme Lord God has forgiven his own child.
My True Guru is merciful for ever; he has kept me, poor and lowly, safe.
The sickness is cut away and I have found supreme peace; (the Guru) has put the Lord's Amrit Naam in my mouth.
(The Guru) has cast away my countless sins; my bonds are cut, and I am free.
Seizing (my) arm, the Guru has lifted (me) out of the blind well, deep and dreadful.
I have become fearless, all fear is erased; the Protector has protected (me).
Such is your gift, my God, that all (my) affairs are set right.
In my mind I have met the Master, the treasure of virtues;
Nanak has sought (his) refuge and is at ease. ॥4॥
383.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When I forget you, everyone turns against me; when you come to mind, (all) serve me.
No other, no second, do I see, O True One, unseen and unfathomable.
When (he) comes to mind, he is ever merciful; what can poor people do?
Tell me, whom should one call bad, and whom good? All beings are yours.
Yours is my support, yours my mainstay; giving (your) hand, you protect (me).
No one speaks an ill word to the person on whom your grace rests.
That alone is peace, that alone is greatness, which pleases God's mind.
You are wise, you are ever kind; if I am given the Naam, I revel in joy.
Before you is my prayer: soul and body, all is yours.
Says Nanak, all greatness is yours; no one even knows my name. ॥4॥
383.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Show mercy, O God, Knower of hearts; in the Saadh Sangat the Lord is found.
Opening the doors, he shows the sight of himself, and one does not come into birth again.
May I meet my beloved Master and be rid of all my sorrows, O brother;
in the company of one who has worshipped the Supreme Lord in the heart, may I swim across, O brother.
(The world) has become a great wilderness, an ocean of fire, where one dwells amid joy and grief;
meeting the True Guru, the mind has become pure, repeating with the tongue the Lord's Amrit (Name).
(Man) has set up body and wealth, all of it, as his own, and is bound in soft bonds (of attachment);
by the Guru's grace those servants are set free who have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
God the Protector has saved those who are pleasing to their God.
Soul and body, all is yours, O Giver; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥4॥
383.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You have broken free of the foul sleep of attachment, O friend; what grace has come upon you?
The great enchantress (Maya) has no hold on you; where has your sloth gone, O friend?
Lust, anger and pride are hard to master; by what discipline have you escaped them, O friend?
(They) have plundered good men, gods, demons, the beings of the three qualities, the whole world, O friend.
Fire in the forest has burnt up much of the grass; only some rare green plant is left, O friend.
I cannot describe one so mighty; no words can tell that one's worth, O friend.
(She answers:) In a room of lamp-black I was not blackened; my colour has stayed spotless, O friend.
The Guru's great mantra has come to dwell in (my) heart; I have heard the wondrous Naam, O friend.
God in his mercy cast (his) gracious glance and joined (me) to his feet.
Through loving devotion, O Nanak, (I) have found peace, and am absorbed in the company of the Saadh. ॥4॥
384.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The red gown looks lovely on your body, (O friend);
you have pleased the Beloved, and so you have won (his) heart.
How did this glow of yours come about, O friend?
With what dye have you turned so rosy red?
You alone are beautiful; yours alone is the married bliss;
in your house is the Beloved, in your house is good fortune.
You are pure in conduct, you are foremost;
you have pleased the Beloved, you alone have lofty wisdom.
(She answers:) I pleased the Beloved, and so (I am dyed) in the deep red (of his love);
says Nanak, (he) has looked on (me) with a kindly eye.
Listen, my friend: this is all my labour:
God, who adorns and makes beautiful, has himself adorned (me). ॥1॥
384.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When I was far (from him), the pain was great;
now, by (the Guru's) counsel, I have been brought into his presence.
My complaining is over, my friends and companions;
my doubt is gone; the Guru has united me with my Husband Lord.
Bringing (me) near, (he) has placed (me) on the Beloved's bed;
I am freed from bowing in deference (to others).
Through the Shabad there is light in the mansion (of my heart);
my Master is full of bliss and play.
Good fortune is on my forehead: my Husband has come home;
servant Nanak has gained a wedded bliss that endures. ॥4॥
384.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My mind is joined to the Name of the True One;
with people, my dealings go only as far as need requires.
Outwardly I am on easy terms with all, and glad with them,
yet I stay untouched, as the lotus does in the water.
With my mouth I talk with everyone,
but my God I hold close to my heart.
(To others my mind) seems very hard and cold,
(yet) this mind (of mine) is the dust of everyone's feet.
Servant Nanak has found the Perfect Guru,
(who) has shown (me) the One (Lord), within and without. ॥4॥
385.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Strong in his youth, (a man) revels in pleasures;
(but) without the Name he mingles with the dust.
He wears rings in his ears and fine clothes on his body,
(sleeps on) a soft bed, and is proud in his mind.
Elephants beneath him, a golden canopy over his head;
(yet) without devotion to the Lord, he is taken and buried in the earth.
(There may be) many women of beautiful form,
(but) without the Lord's sweet essence all tastes are insipid.
Maya is a deceiver, and the vices are poison;
O God, merciful Being, Nanak has come to your refuge. ॥4॥
385.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
There is a garden, in which very many trees have been planted;
in it the Amrit of the Naam has come to fruit.
O wise one, reflect in such a way
that the state beyond all desire may be reached.
All around are pools of poison, (but) in the middle is the Amrit, O brother.
The one who waters it is the one Gardener alone;
he looks after every leaf and every branch.
He has brought every kind of plant and set it (in this garden);
all of it has flowered; not one is without fruit.
The one who has received from the Guru the Amrit fruit, the Naam:
O servant Nanak, he has crossed over (the ocean of) Maya. ॥4॥
385.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) your Name has made (for me) the delights of a kingdom;
as I sing your Kirtan, yoga too is attained.
In your shelter every comfort has come about;
the True Guru has drawn back the curtains of doubt.
Understanding (your) Hukam, I enjoy every joy and delight;
through the True Guru's service (I) have become wholly free of desire.
One who has known you is approved, whether householder or renunciant;
the one dyed in the Naam is the one free of desire.
The one who has received the treasure of the Naam:
says Nanak, that one's treasury is full. ॥4॥
385.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If I go to a place of pilgrimage, (I find people) crying I, I;
if I ask the pandits, they are steeped in Maya.
O friend, tell me of that place
where the Lord's Kirtan, Har Har, goes on day after day.
The Shastras and the Vedas (teach) the reckoning of sin and merit,
(by which) one is born again and again in hell and in heaven.
In the householder's life there is anxiety, in renunciation there is pride;
doing rituals, the soul is caught in entanglements.
(The one whose) mind has come under control by God's grace:
O Nanak, through the Guru that one has crossed over (the ocean of) Maya.
In the Saadh Sangat let us sing the Kirtan of the Lord;
this place is found through the Guru. ॥7॥
385.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
There is peace at home, and peace outside too;
remembering the Lord, all sorrows are destroyed.
(O Lord,) when you come into the mind, there is every comfort;
(but) only the one who pleases you repeats the Naam.
Repeating your Name, body and mind are cooled and calmed;
repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, the camp of sorrow is torn down.
Only one who understands (God's) Hukam is approved,
one who bears the True Shabad as his seal of passage.
The Perfect Guru has made the Name of the Lord firm (within me);
says Nanak, my mind has found peace. ॥4॥
386.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) where you send me, there I go;
what you give me, in that I find my comfort.
O Govind, Lord of the world (Gosain), I am your servant for ever;
by your grace I am filled and content.
What you have given, that I wear and eat;
by your grace, O God, I spend (my days) in comfort.
Within my mind and body I meditate on you alone;
I set no one beside you as your equal.
Says Nanak: (grant that) I may meditate (on you) thus for ever,
(and) attain the highest state, falling at the feet of the Sants. ॥4॥
386.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Rising, sitting and sleeping, let us meditate (on the Lord);
walking on the road, let us sing of the Lord, Har Har.
With the ears, let us listen to the Amrit account (of the Lord's praises),
hearing which there is bliss in the mind, (and) all the sorrows and sicknesses of the mind are lifted away.
In every task and every work, on the road and at the river crossing, let us repeat (his Name);
by the Guru's grace, let us drink the Lord's Amrit (of the Name).
Day and night let us sing the Kirtan of the Lord;
(the one who sings it,) that person is not set on the road of Jam.
(O Lord,) the one who does not forget you at any hour:
O Nanak, falling at that one's feet, the highest state is attained. ॥4॥
386.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Remember the Lord,) through whose remembrance peace comes to dwell (in the mind);
there is well-being, and sorrows are destroyed.
Live in bliss; sing the praises of God;
for ever and ever win the favour of your True Guru.
Live by the True Guru's true Shabad;
(so,) steady and seated in your own home (within), you will find your God.
Do not hold ill will for another in your mind;
(then) no sorrow (will come) to you, O brother, O friend.
The Guru has given the Lord, Har Har, as the charm and the mantra;
O Nanak, (the one who received it) has come to know this peace, night and day. ॥4॥
386.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The lowly one, whom no one even knows,
is honoured in the four directions by repeating the Naam.
I beg for the sight of you: grant it, O Beloved;
whom has your service not carried across?
The one whom no one would come near:
the whole creation rubs and washes that one's feet.
The mortal who was of use to no one:
by the grace of the Sant (the Guru), that one's name is (now) repeated (by all).
In the Saadh Sangat the mind that slept wakes up;
then, O Nanak, God seems sweet. ॥4॥
386.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
With my eyes I behold the One, the One alone,
(and) ever and ever keep the Name of the Lord treasured (in my heart).
I sing the praises of Ram, of Ram the beautiful;
by the power of the Sant (the Guru), in the Saadh's company, I meditate, O brother, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The One on whose thread all creation is strung:
In an instant he brings about the creation and the dissolution (of the world),
(yet) himself stays untouched, beyond (Maya's three) qualities.
He does and causes all to be done; he is the knower of hearts;
387.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The wanderings of millions of births have ended;
(the game of) this human body, so hard to come by, is won, not lost.
Sins are wiped out, sorrow and pain are far away;
by the dust of the Sants' feet (they) have become pure.
God's Sants have the power to save;
(but) they meet only the one for whom such union was written from the very start.
The Guru has given the mantra (of the Name), and there is bliss in the mind;
craving is quenched, and the mind has become steady.
The Name, that precious thing, is the nine treasures and the siddhis;
O Nanak, (this) understanding is received from the Guru. ॥4॥
387.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Thirst (for Maya) and the darkness of ignorance are gone;
serving the Saadh (the Guru), a host of sins has been cut away.
There is peace, Sahaj, and abundant bliss;
through the Guru's service, minds have become pure, hearing the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Har Har.
The folly and the stubbornness of the mind are destroyed;
God's will has come to seem sweet.
The feet of the Perfect Guru were grasped,
(and) the sins of millions of births were washed away.
This life, a jewel, has borne its fruit;
says Nanak, God has shown mercy. ॥4॥
387.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Keep your True Guru treasured (in the heart), ever and always;
dust the Guru's feet with (your) hair.
Wake up, O mind, you who can wake!
Without the Lord nothing else will be of use (to you); attachment is false, (the world's) spread is perishable.
Fall in love with the Guru's Bani;
(when) the Guru is merciful, sorrow goes.
Apart from the Guru there is no other resting place;
the Guru is the Giver, and it is the Guru who gives the Name.
The Guru is himself the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God;
at all hours, O Nanak, meditate on the Guru. ॥4॥
